structured_checks.task: Code can be exported (GitHub or zip) and data downloaded
structured_checks.detail: run on 26 September 2026: the project zip export held the full source and its git history, but no database contents. Outside Replit it installed and built with pnpm 10 (pnpm 12 refused) once PORT and BASE_PATH were set, and ran against our own empty Postgres: schema created, a booking accepted and counted, admin login refused with a wrong password. sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested My Stories on a Shopify development store. The core action, making a story from an uploaded video, did not succeed because our browser tool could not reach the upload button inside the iframe of the app; that is a limit of the test tool and not a finding about the app. Seen were the install permissions, the plan screen with Free, Pro and Advanced, the Shopify approval screen for Pro (not approved), the Lead Form page on the Free plan, the upload screen, the Link Video page and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing (English, https://apps.shopify.com/videos-stories-on-products) opened the Install app dialog in the admin, which asked for View customer data (Sensitive data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner, blog contributors) and View and edit store data (Customers, products, Online Store, Shopify admin). The install was started at about 14:57 and approved at about 14:58, and about 1 minute after the start the app showed the screen Select a plan (/app/pricing); there was no other onboarding. Core action NOT DONE: the goal was to upload a video, link it to a test product and show it in the theme preview. This did not succeed. The reason was our browser tool and not the app: the app runs in a cross-origin iframe, and with our browser tools the file input of the upload button could not be reached, so the system file picker could not be used. A test video of 4 seconds (540x960, no faces) was ready but could not be offered to the app. The app was therefore not tried on its core action, and nothing here is a finding against the app. No story was made, no preview was seen, no theme change was made and nothing was saved in the theme. What was seen: the start screen Welcome to My Stories (You can upload vertical Story videos and display them on your product pages, collections, standalone pages, or homepage.) with 1 out of 6 steps completed (Upload your first video, Link your video to a product, Add Stories block to product page / collections page / Homepage / page template); the empty video library (No videos uploaded yet.); the Upload Video screen (Start uploading videos, with the button Upload Videos); and the Link Video page with four choices, Link to products, Link to collections, Link to homepage and Link to pages. Up to this point the steps were: install (2 clicks), choose a plan (1 click) and go to the upload screen (2 clicks). Plans: the in-app screen, the same as the App Store, has a switch Pay monthly or Pay yearly. Free: Up to 10 videos uploaded, Unlimited videos views, Link videos everywhere, Shoppables Videos, Watermark. Pro: $14.00 a month, 7 trial days, Everything in Free, Up to 100 videos uploaded, Lead Form, Up to 20 leads per month, Story performance analytics, NO watermark. Advanced: $45.00 a month, 7 trial days, Everything in Pro, Unlimited uploaded videos, Lead Form, Unlimited leads per month, Story performance analytics, NO watermark. The App Store lists $140 a year and $450 a year and a 7-day free trial. Deviation from the dossier: the dossier names the plans Beginner at $0, Advanced at $14 and Pro at $45, while the app and the App Store call them Free, Pro at $14 and Advanced at $45, so the names of the two paid plans are swapped. Checkout: the Free plan was chosen first (no approval screen; the button became Current plan). Then Pro was clicked to see the checkout: the Shopify Approve subscription screen shows My Stories by GetMyStories, plan Pro, $14,00 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., a subtotal of $14,00 plus any applicable taxes, a total of $14,00 due 24 Nov., an Add payment method row and a greyed out Approve button. The sentence about a test charge was NOT on this screen and a payment method was asked, so nothing was approved; no card was entered. The Cancel button gave a toast: The shop cannot accept the provided charge. Advanced was not opened. Lead Form: on the Free plan the page says Available on paid plans (The lead form and leads list are available on Advanced and Pro plans), and the switch Enable Lead Form is switched off and greyed out. Cancelling: no subscription ran, because the Free plan was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app (Open app, View details, Get support, Uninstall) and the dialog Uninstall My Stories?, which says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request is sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Select all that apply); we gave Testing multiple apps at about 15:04 and the app left the installed list. Not tested: uploading a video, linking it to a product, the Stories block in the theme, the preview, the shoppable button, the Lead Form itself (it needs a paid plan), the analytics, the watermark, the loading speed and the paid plans. Clean up: nothing was created in the store and nothing was saved in the theme; the app was uninstalled; the test video stayed on our own side; all browser tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
findings: Text we checked: "$14.00 / month". What we saw: The plan screen and the App Store list Free, Pro at $14.00 a month and Advanced at $45.00 a month. The dossier names the plans Beginner at $0, Advanced at $14 and Pro at $45, so the prices of the tiers match but the names of the two paid plans are swapped.

Text we checked: "Available on paid plans". What we saw: On the Free plan the Lead Form page says Available on paid plans and the switch Enable Lead Form is greyed out; the plan cards list Lead Form only under Pro and Advanced.

Text we checked: "You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov". What we saw: The Shopify approval screen for Pro says You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., as the plan card says 7 trial days, but it asks for a payment method and Approve was greyed out.
not_tested: Original store creation and identity check, which Daan did himself.

sessions.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 29 October 2026 the session tested Klap on a 30-day Pro period that Klap itself supplied, so nothing here describes the ordinary free route. We uploaded one of our own review videos (2 minutes 57 seconds, cut down to 720p so our upload tool could carry it), asked for shorts with the default settings and downloaded one clip. The Billing page showed no subscription, only a Choose a plan button; the Usage page showed 0 of 300 clips. Nothing was paid and no card was entered.
findings: Text we checked: "Generate ~7 shorts". What we saw: the dialog promised about 7 shorts; the finished run produced 4 shorts, each with a virality score between 65 and 75 out of 100, and the page showed the result less than 4 minutes after the start (09:52:40, done by 09:56:36 Dutch time).
Text we checked: "Clips 0 / 300". What we saw: the Usage page counted the run as 4 clips used of 300, so a run is billed by the clips it returns, not by the 7 it announced.

Text we checked: "Download HD". What we saw: the downloaded MP4 measured 1080 by 1920 pixels and showed no Klap watermark in the frames we inspected; the download routes we looked at offered no separate SRT, transcript or editable project file.

Text we checked: "Get $5 in free API credits". What we saw: the API page holds a separate prepaid balance of $0.00, not included in Pro, and asks for a card to unlock the free credits; we created no key and made no API call.
not_tested: The public free route, the paid checkout and when the supplied Pro period really ends.
Importing an editable project back into Klap, and the official CSV and PNG media kit.
Team roles and invitations, because the account menu offered no such screen.
Cancelling or downgrading, because the account held no subscription.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

On 17 November 2026 we installed Essential Cart Drawer on a Shopify development store, switched on the app embed, published the cart drawer and a free shipping reward bar, and read the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen. The app opened without any payment and the drawer was live about 3.5 minutes after install, in about 9 clicks. We paid, approved and uninstalled nothing. The full run is in the exit test section below.
findings: Setup: no plan had to be chosen before the app opened. The setup guide stood at 0 of 4; the drawer showed Live after the embed was saved in the theme and the drawer was enabled.

Preview: the app preview showed a countdown timer, a rewards bar that said All Rewards unlocked, two discount codes and a Secure checkout button. Upsell was On by default, but we saw no upsell product in the preview.

Plans: Free is $0 for up to 30 orders a month; nine plans run from Essential 1 at $8.99 to Unlimited at $198.99. The Shopify approval screen for Essential 1 showed no price and no trial, only a spending limit of $198.99 per 30 days.
Cancelling: the FAQ says cancelling is done on the Plans page and takes effect immediately, which also unpublishes the drawer. With no subscription we saw no Cancel button.
not_tested: Upsell products, Sticky Add to Cart, the announcement bar and spend tiers with a gift: not run.
The drawer on the live storefront (the store has a password), speed and theme compatibility.
A paid plan, the 30 order limit, the automatic plan switch, the uninstall dialog and support.

sessions.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 14 November 2026 the session tested SignThis on the free plan: one PDF to three signers, the document counter, VerySecure, a correction after sending, cancelling, and the page a signer sees without an account. The paid Professional plan was not activated. One PDF with three made up signers was uploaded at 12:56. Place signature blocks put a signature, name and date for all three signers on page 1 with one click. Review and send said Uses 1 of your 3 remaining free documents and that free workspaces can send each document to up to 10 recipients and to 25 in any 24 hours (0 of 25 used; this document goes to 3). It was sent at 12:58, and the counter then read 2 of 3 free documents left this month: three signers cost one document. VerySecure palm scan can be ticked per signer on the free plan, but Review and send then says VerySecure requires a paid subscription and that ordinary documents remain available within the free allowance. No palm scan or biometrics followed and the box was unticked again. The invitations to the made up signer addresses did not arrive: the activity log said Accepted by mail service, with a note that accepted does not mean the email is in the inbox. Our own mailbox does not deliver plus addresses, which is a limit on our side and not a fault of SignThis. Correct and resend as new version made a new draft with the same blocks; after changing signer 1 to a reachable address, Review and send said Uses 1 of your 2 remaining free documents, so a correction costs a new document. Afterwards both versions stood on Waiting: the first was not withdrawn by itself. Both requests were cancelled with Cancel request, and the counter stayed at 1 of 3 free documents left: cancelling does not give the document back. What a signer without an account sees: the invitation of 13:00 arrived in the Junk folder of our mailbox and says No account is needed and that the signer can decline or ask the sender for a paper alternative; the link is valid until 14 December. The link opens a page without any login, with the document name, the sender, the items You will be asked to give (a signature and a full name) and all participants. Review and continue offers Read it first, a reading mode (Reading only, Ready to sign?), Open original PDF, the electronic records and signatures disclosure and Agree and continue, with the note that continuing does not sign the document. The PDF could be read before agreeing. Agree and continue was not clicked and nothing was signed. The sender saw for signer 1 at once Opened, opened just now.
findings: Three signers cost one document: the counter went from 3 of 3 to 2 of 3 free documents left this month, and Review and send said Uses 1 of your 3 remaining free documents. One click on Place signature blocks put a signature, name and date for all three signers on page 1. Free workspaces can send each document to up to 10 recipients and to 25 in any 24 hours.

A correction costs a new document. Correct and resend as new version made a new draft with the same blocks and said Uses 1 of your 2 remaining free documents. Both versions then stood on Waiting. Cancelling both left the counter at 1 of 3, so cancelling does not give the document back.
VerySecure palm scan can be ticked per signer on the free plan, but Review and send then says VerySecure requires a paid subscription. The box was unticked and no palm scan followed.

A signer needs no account. The invitation says No account is needed, the link is valid until 14 December and opens without a login. The signer can read the PDF before agreeing, and continuing does not sign it. The sender saw Opened, opened just now at once.

The invitation landed in the Junk folder of our mailbox. The first invitations to made up plus addresses did not arrive (Accepted by mail service); our mailbox does not deliver plus addresses, which is a limit on our side.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 31 October 2026 on the 14-day trial that starts with a new account, without a card: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We answered the onboarding questions, imported a two-row CSV of made-up contacts, and tried to export them again. We connected no mailbox, calendar or phone, sent nothing, invited nobody and paid nothing. The session took about ten minutes.
findings: After sign-up Cloze asked four onboarding questions (industry setup, what to call people, what to call deals, and whether to track an active stage). We chose sales and services and left the defaults. The next screen said it was analysing our history and would email us when done, 'a few minutes to a few hours', although no mailbox was connected. The mailbox dialog offered Google, Microsoft 365, Exchange, iCloud, Yahoo and other email, and we connected none.

Settings showed the trial ending on 16 November 2026, which is 16 days after our account date of 31 October. Cloze's help page promises 14 days without a card. We were not asked for a card in the steps we recorded, but we did not count every sign-up screen, and we cannot say every account gets 16 days.

The CSV importer read the two rows and the sample values correctly, including accents and a line break inside a note, but detected no columns on its own, not even the email column. The 'Add person' field list runs to dozens of fields, and custom fields could only be mapped onto fields that already exist in the account. We mapped four columns by hand (display name, note, email, tags) and left the rest unmapped.

The import offered a dry run and a plain import; we ran the import and got 'Imported 2 of 2 records successfully', with the option to download our mapping. The two contacts did not show in the list until we searched for 'TEST', although the counter had already moved.

The email address and the multi-line note arrived intact. Our tag 'aibm-test|alpha' became one tag, '#aibm-test-alpha': the pipe turned into a hyphen and the tag was not split in two. That matters if you keep several tags in one spreadsheet column.

Settings > Import / Export offers CSV or Excel for people, companies and deals. The Dutch interface translated 'Excel' as 'uitmunten' (the verb 'to excel'). We pressed 'Export now' twice, at 21:21 and 21:24. Both times a loading spinner ran for about 30 seconds with no download, no message and no file, and the network log showed no export request. We do not know whether the file would have come by email later, so we do not call this a failed export. The export window points to support@cloze.com for help.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 2 November 2026 on the unpaid integration trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported two fictional contacts from a CSV file, then ran a second import to update one of them. We sent nothing, created no API key and did not open checkout.
findings: The trial shows 'Integration trial', 'No active subscription' and 100 recipient deliveries (0 of 100 used). No card was asked for. The plan page lists Transactional Starter at $9 a month, Marketing Starter at $19 and Scale at $39 a month, with a 10% annual discount and the note 'Hard monthly caps, no overage bills.'
Contacts accepts a CSV of up to 5,000 rows and 5 MB, and nothing is imported until you confirm. Name and email columns matched on their own. Every other column became a custom contact field.
The import asks why you may email these people and requires an answer. Our records were synthetic, so we said so; the answer is stored on each contact as evidence of consent.

Our test file marked one contact 'blocked'. SendHQ did not recognise that word and showed both rows as subscribed in the preview. After we changed the value to 'unsubscribed', the preview showed zero subscribed and both contacts arrived as unsubscribed.

The accented name, the e-mail address and the two-line note came through unchanged. The pipe-separated tag 'aibm-test|alpha' stayed one text value instead of two tags. A file name in the attachment column is stored as plain text; contacts have no file upload.

A second import with 'Update names and fields of contacts who already exist' ticked reported New 0 and Existing 2. The changed note on the second contact updated and the first stayed as it was. Contacts are matched on the e-mail address, not on an ID.
not_tested: Export: we found no export or download button on Contacts or Lists, so we could not check what a file would contain. That is not a finding that SendHQ has no export
A round trip with native record IDs, and any check of attachments
Checkout, tax and the final price: the browser session did not allow opening it
Support, team roles, invitations, downgrade and cancellation
Sending: we sent no message and created no API key or sending domain

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested Elite Site Optimizer on the free trial: domain verification in three steps, a site audit request, rank tracking, competitor and AI readiness pages, and the plan page. Verification took three steps. First the business email OTP, done by Daan at about 09:17. That gave temporary verification: the Keywords page said the domain is verified temporarily using business email and that a TXT record must be added to access all features, and Add Keywords and Add Bulk Keyword were grey. Then, at Daan request, our AI assistant added a TXT verification record at the root of the domain at the DNS host between 10:15 and 10:20, with a TTL of 3600. The token expires in 7 days and its value is not recorded here. The host panel reported that the record was not valid or conflicted with another record, but a DNS query to the name server showed the record, and it had been there since the first try. Submit in the tool then said the domain was already verified. After full verification the Keywords page still said This feature is available for our premium members only, and Add Keywords and Add Bulk Keyword stayed grey, so rank tracking is not part of the free trial. Competitor Ranking showed No Metric Data Available with a grey Competitor Settings button. AI Readiness has only a Run Report Now button, which was grey, and clicking it did nothing. The AI Add-ons tab was empty, and the Competitor Analysis tab next to Site Audit stays empty without a report. Site Audit, Run Report Now, offered only HARD RUN (it checks for new web pages and runs a complete report), with a Home Page section, and starts by itself after 60 seconds. The first attempt appeared to do nothing and the page stayed on No report available yet. The second attempt, with the section chosen, gave the notice that the report would be ready in about 7 hours, at 09:20. At 17:49, about 8.5 hours after the start, there was still no report and no notification apart from two Domain Added Successfully messages, so the promise was not met. The browser session had been logged out, and Daan logged in again before this check. Analysts needing market traffic data were not tested, as no traffic data part was viewed. The TXT record stays in the DNS of the tested domain until cleaned up. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Verification needs an email OTP and then a DNS TXT record, with only temporary access in between. Rank tracking is premium only, Competitor Settings and AI Readiness are grey, and the audit promised in about 7 hours had not arrived after about 8.5 hours.

Start and account: the test started at 16:11 (Dutch time) in an account that Daan made, already logged in on the vendor app, in our own tab, on a free trial. The dashboard showed 7 days left in your free trial and a checklist Finish setting up, 0 of 3 done: Connect your social accounts, Publish your first post and Schedule a post, the last two with the text Unlocks once an account is connected. The Agent page says Connect an account to put me to work, and that it can already brainstorm ideas and captions, but that to draft posts, plan your week or reply to comments and DMs it needs a connected social account. The Posts page says Connect a social account to publish and schedule from here. The composer says No account to publish to, with Connect Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, LinkedIn, X or Threads, then come back to this post, and No account connected yet, save it as a draft. Publishing, scheduling, auto-replies and Plan my week were therefore not possible, and nothing was connected, published or scheduled. What did work without an account: (a) on the Agent page the button 3 post ideas to boost engagement this week gave Here are three engagement-focused ideas for this week, a this or that choice on Wednesday, a behind the scenes moment on Friday and a useful tip on Sunday; the ideas are generic and not shaped to a business. The first try, typing the question in the search field of the dashboard, emptied the field without an answer; the Agent page worked. (b) In the composer (Posts, Create Post) the prompt Announce a spring sale for a small coffee shop and the button AI Assist gave the toast AI generated your caption! and a caption of 195 characters with emoji and four hashtags; AI Assist without a prompt said Please enter a prompt first. The first result (the ideas) came about 1 minute after the start at 16:11 and the caption at 16:13, in 4 steps (Create Post, the text box, the prompt and AI Assist), in about 15 seconds. The draft was not saved (Cancel). Networks: the composer names six networks (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, LinkedIn, X and Threads) and no others; YouTube is not named. The Connect account dialog itself was not opened on purpose, so a full list of networks offered there was not seen. Plans: See plans opened the window Choose your plan. Monthly: Starter $19/mo (5 social accounts, 1 workspace, unlimited posts, 10 AI images a month, AI auto-replies, a unified inbox, AI content ideas and a weekly auto-plan, MCP); Team $39/mo, most popular (20 social accounts, unlimited workspaces and team members, 20 AI images a month, a post approval workflow, API access and a priority tier); Pro $59/mo (50 accounts, 50 AI images); Max $99/mo (100 accounts, 100 AI images and a VIP priority tier). Settings, Subscription shows Current Plan Free trial, Trial ends 24 November 2026, Renews on 24 November 2026 and a button Manage Billing; during the trial the limits are at Team level (Social Accounts 20, Workspaces Unlimited, Users Unlimited). Only dollar signs are shown and no currency name. Upgrade and Manage Billing were not clicked, so no payment screen was opened. Cancelling: Settings, Profile has a section Delete Account (Once you delete your account, there is no going back), listing the profile, the spaces and workspaces, the connected social accounts and the posts and drafts; the red button was not clicked. Cancelling a subscription goes through Manage Billing, which was not opened. Not tested: connecting an account, publishing, scheduling, Plan my week, the inbox and AI auto-replies, the post approval workflow, API keys, MCP, the Story tab, AI Image, Hashtags, the Upgrade button and Manage Billing, and YouTube (not offered). Clean up: the account, the workspace and the trial stay as Daan made them; no account was connected and no draft was saved; one Agent chat 3 post ideas to boost engagement this week remains in the chat list; our tab was closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested EditEngine (Bulk Product Editor in the app) on a Shopify development store: the install, a storewide 5 percent price increase with a preview of old and new prices, applying it to 19 products in 8.0 seconds, undoing it, the Select your plan window with greyed out buttons and the uninstall of the app. Nothing was paid, no approval screen was reached and the prices in the store were not checked after the undo. Install: the app is called EditEngine Bulk Product Editor in the App Store listing (English; Free plan available, 4.9 from 162 reviews, Built for Shopify, developer Profitonium), Bulk Product Editor in the install dialog and EditEngine: Bulk Product Editor in the app. The first install attempt at about 13:24 used the wrong form and had no effect; the real install started at about 13:24:40 in our own tab. The dialog Install app warned that Bulk Product Editor doesn't support market-driven shipping and asked for View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Products, custom data, Shopify admin, other data); the listing also names View customer data and customers, orders, discounts and store credit. The app opened at once without a payment, plan choice, account or demo, with Products 19, Bulk edits 0, Exports 0 and Current plan: Unlimited. Core action, a bulk price change with preview, apply and undo: the start screen offers Ask EditEngine with the line You review a preview before anything is saved. We chose the example Increase all prices by 5% and sent it. The chat Storewide five percent price increase read the request, checked the fields and showed the preview card Raise price by 5% for All products, 19 products and all variants, with examples such as The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard $949.95 to $997.45, four Gift Card amounts and The Minimal Snowboard $885.95 to $930.25 (all agree with a plain 5 percent increase) and Show all 10 preview examples. The card says Nothing changes until you click Apply. You can undo it afterwards. and shows Apply to 19 products, Adjust, Cancel and Preview valid until 01:40 PM. Apply started the edit; after Refresh the job said Completed and a toast said Bulk edit finished. The summary says Processed 19/19 product in 8.0s, No errors, 1:26 PM, Action: IncreaseByPercent. The result was visible about 2.5 minutes after the start of the install (about 13:24:40 to 13:27) in 8 clicks (Install, confirm Install, the example sentence, Send, Review and apply, Apply to 19 products, Refresh status, View results); the edit itself took 8.0 seconds. Undo: Undo Edit opened the dialog Undo bulk edit (Are you sure you want to undo this bulk edit? This will revert all changes made to 19 product.) with the notice This action cannot be undone., and after Confirm Undo the summary said Bulk Edit Reverted, 19 product restored to previous state, with the button Reverted. The prices in the store itself were not looked at after the undo. Plans: Upgrade opens Select your plan with a switch Monthly or Annual (Save 17%). It says Your current plan: Unlimited and Development store: Free unlimited access while your store is in development. When it moves to a paid Shopify plan, you'll pick from the plans below. On Annual the cards show Basic $8.33 /month ($99.99 /year), Standard $16.67 /month ($199.99 /year), Pro $41.67 /month ($499.99 /year) and Free $0 /month. Basic allows 500 products and 10 collections per task and has no scheduled bulk edits (crossed out); Standard allows 10,000 products and 100 collections and has scheduled edits; Pro is unlimited with scheduled edits; all plans list Undo and rollback edits and Export metafields. An add-on, automatic daily backups, costs $6.99/month and works with every plan. The App Store shows monthly prices of $9.99, $19.99 and $49.99 and the same yearly amounts; the app shows a monthly equivalent on the Annual view, and the Monthly view was set but not captured. Checkout: the buttons Try Basic Plan, Try Standard Plan, Try Pro Plan and Try Free Plan were greyed out on the development store, so no Shopify Approve subscription screen came up, nothing was approved and no card was asked. Cancelling: no subscription existed (the development store has the Unlimited plan). The uninstall route is Settings, Apps, the menu of Bulk Product Editor and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Bulk Product Editor? says you will no longer be able to use the app and that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted; the Uninstall button only works after a reason is chosen (Testing multiple apps). No picture of that dialog was kept. Not tested: the plans Basic, Standard and Pro, scheduled edits, deleting products, import and export, the Backup add-on, the connection with Claude, ChatGPT or Sidekick, the storefront preview, and the product prices in the store after the undo. Clean up: the test edit was undone (status Reverted); the app was uninstalled after the test with the reason Testing multiple apps and is gone from the installed apps; no theme change was saved. Other apps were not touched. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

Basic account settings report an EU data region. The account-data download explicitly leaves your files out, so it is not a backup of your storage.
No card was asked for in the steps we saw; a lifetime pCloud Pass promotion appeared straight after login.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 2 November 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported two made-up contacts from a CSV file, then exported them again to CSV. We did not open the checkout.
findings: The dashboard showed '30 days left', matching the 30-day trial in the help centre, and the workspace already held sample contacts and candidates.
The importer started every column on 'Don't Import This Column' and had the header row switched off by default, so each field has to be mapped by hand. We found no custom fields in the mapping list.
The import warned that 'all the special characters in FirstName and LastName will be removed', yet both exported first names kept their accents.
The export kept the two contacts with their IDs, but left out the note text we entered: 'Last Note Added' is only a timestamp. The Contact Name column added a trailing space to each name.
Getting the export took four clicks: select the contacts, More, Export, then pick the fields and Export to CSV.

Re-importing the export and how duplicates are matched
Roles, API access and downgrading
Inviting teammates and contacting support

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 we installed Froonze Loyalty & Wishlist on a Shopify development store, switched on Wishlist and Loyalty on the Free plans, set a points rule, saved the app embed in the theme and read the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen for Loyalty Advanced. The Free plans needed no payment screen. We paid, approved and uninstalled nothing. The full run is in the exit test section below.
findings: Free plans: the welcome screen said a shop with under 100 monthly orders is eligible for free Wishlist and Loyalty. The Place an order rule (4 points per $1, so 400 points per $100) was active about 3 minutes after install, in about 20 clicks.
Widget: we saw no widget or launcher in the theme editor preview, and we placed no order, so earning points was not tested.
Plans: Loyalty is $0 up to 100 orders, then $10, $30 and $60 a month; Wishlist is $0, $10, $20 and $40. Loyalty Advanced plus Wishlist Free showed $10 a month on the plan page.

Checkout: the Shopify approval screen for Loyalty Advanced showed $10.00 every 30 days with a 14 day trial, asked for a payment method, had Approve greyed out and carried no test charge notice, although the app says all features can be tested free on development stores.
not_tested: A real order and points on the storefront, the wishlist heart on product pages and store credit.
Paying for a plan, the trial, a downgrade and behaviour above 100 orders.
Email templates, Loyalty Advanced features, support and chat.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Froonze Loyalty & Wishlist on the Free plans of a Shopify development store: the install, the Loyalty onboarding with a points rule, saving the app embed in the theme, the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen for Loyalty Advanced (not approved, a payment method was asked) and the uninstall dialog. Nothing was paid, approved or uninstalled. Install: the App Store listing (English) is called Froonze VIP Loyalty & Wishlist and says Free plan available. Free trial available.; in the admin the app is called Froonze Loyalty & Wishlist. The Install click at about 11:00 opened the dialog Install app with access to customer data, staff and contributor data and store data (view and edit), which was accepted. The welcome screen said Your shop has less than 100 monthly orders which makes it eligible for free Wishlist and Loyalty plugins.; Wishlist and Loyalty were switched on with Activate and no Shopify payment screen appeared. A chat window of the vendor opened at once and was closed. Core action: Loyalty onboarding, Next, the Points program was chosen (the alternative is a Store credit program), the cashback default of 4 percent was kept (the text says For each $100 spent, your customers will earn 400 points, which they can later redeem for a $4 discount), Create program rules, Activate now, and for the email notifications we chose I'll activate later, so no emails are active. Theme: Install for the app embed opened the theme editor, where the app embed Loyalty & Referrals was already on (toast Loyalty & Referrals activated) and the theme was saved (toast Changes saved.). That is a real change to the live theme of our development store and it is still on; the vendor needs it for the installation. Result in the app: Successfully installed. You can continue with the setup; the check list said Account page widget: No and Audit: No, finish onboarding. Program, Earning rules shows the rule Place an order, 4 points per 1USD spent, switched on (Active). In the theme editor preview we saw no widget or launcher on the home page. No order was placed, so no points could show; the Performance summary shows Activity 0, Points earned 0 and Emails sent 0. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 3 minutes from 11:00 to 11:03 and about 20 clicks, counting the onboarding and saving the theme. Plans: Manage plans starts with the note Plugin prices are flat monthly fees. You get 14-day free trial for your first subscription. You can test all of our app features for free in development stores. Wishlist: Free $0 (100 orders, All features), Advanced $10 (500 orders), Premium $20 (1000 orders) and Unlimited $40 (Unlimited orders, API). Loyalty program: Free $0 (100 orders, Points program, Store credit), Advanced $10 (500 orders, VIP program, Referral program, Shopify POS, Points expiration, integrations with Judge.me, PushOwl and Shopify Flow), Premium $30 (1000 orders, a customer tags blacklist and whitelist) and Unlimited $60 (Unlimited orders, Digital cards, API). The customer account widget shows $5 - 30/mo and the custom forms $6 - 30/mo with the label Legacy Accounts only. Under the plans there is a field Please consider adding a monthly tip (0) and Total: $10 / Month. Checkout: Loyalty Advanced was chosen and Update pressed; the app then said that after clicking Yes we would be prompted to accept a new Shopify recurring charge and that the old recurring charge would be cancelled automatically. The Shopify Approve subscription screen showed the plan Wishlist(Free) + Loyalty(Advanced), $10,00 USD every 30 days, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., Subtotal $10,00 plus any applicable taxes and Total $10,00 due 1 Dec. It did not say that the charge is a test charge that will not be billed; it showed Add payment method, and the Approve button was greyed out. Nothing was approved; Cancel gave the toast The shop cannot accept the provided charge. Cancelling: the plans stayed Free for both, so there was no paid plan to cancel. The routes seen are going back to the Free plan (not tried) and the Uninstall item in the app menu (the three dots, with Manage app, Get support, Pin to your navigation and Uninstall). The Uninstall dialog says that after uninstalling any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request is sent to the developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; it was cancelled and nothing was removed. The pricing FAQ of the vendor (read on 25 October, not read again) says cancelling is possible at any time and is prorated. Not tested: a real order and earning points on the storefront, the widget in the theme preview (not seen), the wishlist heart on product pages (only switched on, not shown), store credit and legacy accounts, the behaviour above 100 orders, paying for a plan, the trial, a plan downgrade and the email templates. Clean up: the app stays installed, both plans stay Free, the Place an order rule is active, the email notifications are off and the app embed is on and saved in the theme. All tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app embed has to be saved in the live theme, the Advanced plan could not be approved without a payment method although development stores are said to test all features free, and no widget showed in the theme preview.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Try You on a Shopify development store. The core action, a virtual try-on, was not run, because it needs a photo of a person and we deliberately use no photos of real people. Seen were the install permissions, the two-step onboarding with five models and a safety cap, the Playground screen, the Shopify approval screen with a test charge that was approved without a card (billed 0 dollars), the prices per try-on, the options and the volume tiers, and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing (English) showed the button Install and a rating of 5.0 from 5 reviews. The Install app dialog in the admin asked for View customer data (Device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View store data (Products, orders, store analytics). The install was approved at about 15:05 and at 15:06 the app was open on its welcome screen with the texts $0 today, free to install, Turn your product pages into fitting rooms. and In 30 seconds, your customer uploads a selfie and sees themselves wearing your product. Onboarding: step 2, Pick your model, then put it to the test., shows 10 free credits and five models: Light 1 credit, Medium 1 credit, Pro 1 credit, High 2 credits and Ultra 2K 3 credits, five sample person photos of the app and the auto-detected test product The 3p Fulfilled Snowboard. Step 3, Set your safety limit., says You pay nothing today and that the cap is the limit of the shop and not an amount that is charged, with a standard cap of $10 a month, which on Light means up to about 250 try-ons, and the line that the price drops up to 50% at volume. Core action NOT DONE: the virtual try-on needs a photo of a person (in the Playground 2. Person photo, with Samples or Upload, and in the onboarding a Sample photo). We deliberately use no photos of real people and no real faces, so this step was skipped and the button Generate the try-on was not pressed. No result image was made, so there is no time to a first result and no judgement on the quality, the speed or whether a snowboard is a fitting item. Showing the button in the shop (the block Add to theme) was also not tried, so that no theme change was saved. What was seen: the Playground with You have 10 free tests remaining out of 10., 1. Product to test (My catalog or Custom upload), 2. Person photo and 3. Configuration with Compare 2 configs side by side. Checkout: Activate TryYou ($0 today) opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen with the notice You will not be billed for this test charge., the plan TryYou: pay per try-on, This app bills you for usage charges, and the App spending limit (to a maximum of $10,00 USD per 30 days), with Your next bill: You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it. An optional row Add payment method stood on the screen, no card had to be entered and Approve could be clicked. Because the screen says it is a test charge, the test charge was approved at about 15:09 without a card; nothing was billed. There is one plan, so this is the cheapest. After the approval the app said You are live and Welcome aboard! with 10 free credits left in the Playground and three display options (Classic button, Floating badge, Carousel slide). Prices in Settings, Quality and pricing (Light selected): Light $0.04, Medium $0.12, Pro $0.19, High $0.37 and Ultra 2K $0.58 per try-on. Options: Multi-Image Context (+$0.01 / try-on), Intelligent AI verification (+$0.01 / try-on), which starts a second generation billed at the selected model rate when the AI sees a major error, and Sensitive-content fallback, which was switched ON by default: it retries with a backup model when the main AI refuses a try-on it judges too explicit and is billed at a flat $0.08 instead of the level price. Your volume tiers: Starter full price (0 to 499 a month), Growth -15% (500 to 1,999), Scale -30% (2,000 to 4,999), Pro -40% (5,000 to 9,999) and Enterprise -50% (10,000+). Raising the monthly cap needs a fresh Shopify approval and lowering it takes effect right away. Deviations from the dossier: the volume thresholds ARE published in the app (the dossier says they are not published). The dossier does not name the extra charges of $0.01 a try-on for Multi-Image Context and for AI verification, nor the $0.08 of the fallback that is on by default. Cancelling: the usage plan has no subscription fee and nothing was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (the Uninstall button stays grey until one is chosen) and there is a feedback box of 250 characters. There is no cancellation fee or waiting time. The reason Testing multiple apps was given at about 15:16 and the app left the installed list. Not tested: generating a try-on (it needs a photo of a person), so the quality, the speed and the cost per result, the storefront blocks and the capture of e-mail addresses (Klaviyo, Shopify Customers), where the selfies go (the privacy policy names AI providers; this was not checked in the app), and the analytics and the CSV export. Clean up: the test charge approval was the only change; the spending cap stayed at $10 as set by the app on activation; no theme change was saved; the app was uninstalled; all browser tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
findings: Text we checked: "up to 50% off at volume". What we saw: Your volume tiers in the settings show Starter at full price for 0 to 499 try-ons a month, then -15%, -30%, -40% and -50% from 10,000 a month. The dossier says the thresholds are not published; the app shows them.

Text we checked: "Multi-Image Context (+$0.01 / try-on)". What we saw: The settings list Multi-Image Context and Intelligent AI verification at +$0.01 a try-on each, and the dossier names no such extra charges.

Text we checked: "at a flat $0.08 instead of the level price". What we saw: The Sensitive-content fallback is switched on by default and bills a flat $0.08 when it recovers a try-on that the main AI refused, which is twice the Light price of $0.04; the dossier does not mention it.

Text we checked: "With $10/month on Light, up to ~250 try-ons". What we saw: The onboarding says that a cap of $10 a month on Light gives up to about 250 try-ons; at $0.04 a try-on in the settings that is 250.

Text we checked: "You will not be billed for this test charge". What we saw: The Shopify approval screen says You will not be billed for this test charge., asks for no card and has an Approve button that could be clicked; it was approved at about 15:09 and nothing was billed.

Seen were the install permissions, the two-step onboarding with five models and a safety cap, the Playground screen, the Shopify approval screen with a test charge that was approved without a card (billed 0 dollars), the prices per try-on, the options and the volume tiers, and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing (English) showed the button Install and a rating of 5.0 from 5 reviews. The Install app dialog in the admin asked for View customer data (Device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View store data (Products, orders, store analytics). The install was approved at about 15:05 and at 15:06 the app was open on its welcome screen with the texts $0 today, free to install, Turn your product pages into fitting rooms. and In 30 seconds, your customer uploads a selfie and sees themselves wearing your product. Onboarding: step 2, Pick your model, then put it to the test., shows 10 free credits and five models: Light 1 credit, Medium 1 credit, Pro 1 credit, High 2 credits and Ultra 2K 3 credits, five sample person photos of the app and the auto-detected test product The 3p Fulfilled Snowboard. Step 3, Set your safety limit., says You pay nothing today and that the cap is the limit of the shop and not an amount that is charged, with a standard cap of $10 a month, which on Light means up to about 250 try-ons, and the line that the price drops up to 50% at volume. Core action NOT DONE: the virtual try-on needs a photo of a person (in the Playground 2. Person photo, with Samples or Upload, and in the onboarding a Sample photo). We deliberately use no photos of real people and no real faces, so this step was skipped and the button Generate the try-on was not pressed. No result image was made, so there is no time to a first result and no judgement on the quality, the speed or whether a snowboard is a fitting item. Showing the button in the shop (the block Add to theme) was also not tried, so that no theme change was saved. What was seen: the Playground with You have 10 free tests remaining out of 10., 1. Product to test (My catalog or Custom upload), 2. Person photo and 3. Configuration with Compare 2 configs side by side. Checkout: Activate TryYou ($0 today) opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen with the notice You will not be billed for this test charge., the plan TryYou: pay per try-on, This app bills you for usage charges, and the App spending limit (to a maximum of $10,00 USD per 30 days), with Your next bill: You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it. An optional row Add payment method stood on the screen, no card had to be entered and Approve could be clicked. Because the screen says it is a test charge, the test charge was approved at about 15:09 without a card; nothing was billed. There is one plan, so this is the cheapest. After the approval the app said You are live and Welcome aboard! with 10 free credits left in the Playground and three display options (Classic button, Floating badge, Carousel slide). Prices in Settings, Quality and pricing (Light selected): Light $0.04, Medium $0.12, Pro $0.19, High $0.37 and Ultra 2K $0.58 per try-on. Options: Multi-Image Context (+$0.01 / try-on), Intelligent AI verification (+$0.01 / try-on), which starts a second generation billed at the selected model rate when the AI sees a major error, and Sensitive-content fallback, which was switched ON by default: it retries with a backup model when the main AI refuses a try-on it judges too explicit and is billed at a flat $0.08 instead of the level price. Your volume tiers: Starter full price (0 to 499 a month), Growth -15% (500 to 1,999), Scale -30% (2,000 to 4,999), Pro -40% (5,000 to 9,999) and Enterprise -50% (10,000+). Raising the monthly cap needs a fresh Shopify approval and lowering it takes effect right away. Deviations from the dossier: the volume thresholds ARE published in the app (the dossier says they are not published). The dossier does not name the extra charges of $0.01 a try-on for Multi-Image Context and for AI verification, nor the $0.08 of the fallback that is on by default. Cancelling: the usage plan has no subscription fee and nothing was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (the Uninstall button stays grey until one is chosen) and there is a feedback box of 250 characters. There is no cancellation fee or waiting time. The reason Testing multiple apps was given at about 15:16 and the app left the installed list. Not tested: generating a try-on (it needs a photo of a person), so the quality, the speed and the cost per result, the storefront blocks and the capture of e-mail addresses (Klaviyo, Shopify Customers), where the selfies go (the privacy policy names AI providers; this was not checked in the app), and the analytics and the CSV export. Clean up: the test charge approval was the only change; the spending cap stayed at $10 as set by the app on activation; no theme change was saved; the app was uninstalled; all browser tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

The Unibox sorted the 15 demo conversations into Starred, Hot, Nurture and Follow-up, with a 'Needs reply' filter. Opening one showed an AI reply marked 'Drafted · not sent' with a category; it only goes out when you click Send.

On 17 November 2026 the session tested EliteCart on a Shopify development store: the install, the app embed switched on and saved in the theme, a cart drawer in the theme preview (not proven to be EliteCart alone, because the cart apps Cross Sell Auto and Essential Cart were also switched on, and the Buy Two discount came from another app), the plan screen with the order slider, the Shopify approval screen for Essentials (not approved, a payment method was asked) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Install: the install form was sent at 14:13 in our own tab; Shopify showed the Install app dialog for EliteCart & Upsell by GEFA Technology with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved. The app opened on Welcome to EliteCart with a Get started list (1 of 4 complete). Step 3, Start your trial, said that as a Shopify Partner development store we have free access and need not subscribe. No separate account, demo or call was asked. Core action, turn on the cart drawer and look at it in the theme preview, about 2 minutes (14:14 to 14:15) and 13 steps: in the theme editor, in our own tab, the app embed EliteCart & Upsell was switched on and the theme was SAVED (Changes saved.), because that was needed to see a result. In the preview we went to The Complete Snowboard and pressed Add to cart. IMPORTANT, this result is not proven to be EliteCart alone: our development store also had the cart apps Cross Sell Auto and Essential Cart switched on in the theme. With EliteCart off, the cart icon showed a different drawer (Cart - 1, You may also like); with EliteCart on, the cart icon still opened that other drawer, and the Matching Items drawer appeared only when Add to cart was pressed. We believe the Matching Items drawer comes from EliteCart because it appeared after the embed was switched on, but this was not confirmed separately in the Cart designer. sessions.what: We generated one text-to-speech clip in Inworld AI's playground on the free On-Demand plan on 13 November 2026 and read the billing and data retention screens. The account is Daan's, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We created no API key, so a realtime conversation through the API was not tested. We did not use the MP3 download or test checkout, support or cancellation.
findings: The playground used the voice Sarah, language Auto and the model Inworld TTS 2, with sliders for delivery and talking speed and MP3 as the download format. Input is limited to 5,000 characters. It offers an Add speaker option and example roles such as Support Agent, AI Companion and Language Teacher. We saw no timeline or video editor.

We entered a support line of 123 characters and pressed Generate. Audio played within about 3 seconds by our eye, not timed, and the playground reported 'First audio in 0.8 s' for a clip of 0:05. The two figures measure different things. The 0.8 s is the playground's own message for one short input, not a latency guarantee for an app.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Kedra Checkout Rules and Upsells on the Free plan of a Shopify development store: a payment rule that did not work on the test gateway, a validation rule that blocked a 600 dollar test checkout, the Free plan limit, the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen and the uninstall dialog. Nothing was paid or uninstalled. First rule: Manual Setup, the template Hide COD over an amount, edited into Hide Bogus gateway over USD 100 (order total greater than USD100, then hide payment methods that contain the string Bogus), saved ACTIVE at about 14:44:40. The Hide settings say that Credit card (Shopify Payments) can only be customized on Shopify Plus plans. A test checkout through the theme editor preview used a snowboard of 600 dollars, a made up name, address and email, and no card; nothing was paid. A first check before the rule existed (ski wax at 24.95 dollars) showed the card block Pay with credit card with a Testing instruction. The payment rule did not work: at 600 dollars Pay with credit card and Test Payment Gateway stayed visible, also after changing the string to Test Payment Gateway and then to Credit card. The cause was not established; it may be that the test gateway counts as the card block that is Plus only, but that is a guess. The Free plan allows 1 active rule: creating a second rule while one is active shows ACTIVE Locked with Your Free plan includes 1 active rule and it is in use. The payment rule was set to INACTIVE and a validation rule Block orders over an amount (order total greater than USD500, message Order total exceeds the maximum allowed amount.) was made ACTIVE. At about 14:49 a checkout of 600 dollars showed a red banner at the top that this order cannot be completed with the current checkout details. That is Shopify default text and not the app message; Your own checkout wording is not included on Free. A cart of 24.95 dollars showed no message. Timing, approximate tester observations: Install at 14:43:00 and a visibly working rule in the test checkout at 14:49:20, about 6 minutes 20 seconds, of which about 3 minutes went on the first rule that did not work; one working rule straight away would have taken about 2 minutes; more than 25 clicks and typing actions including the detour. Uninstall: the app menu offers Manage app, Get support, Pin to your navigation and Uninstall; the Uninstall dialog (reason list, feedback box) was opened and cancelled. Not tested: post-purchase upsells (a paid plan), hiding, renaming or reordering shipping and payment methods, draft orders, completing a real payment, Plus only features, own wording in the block, and a payment rule with a real second payment method. No kit records were entered.
findings: Vendor claim "7 dagen". What we saw: The Dutch App Store listing named a 7 day trial. The app and the Shopify approval screen showed a 5-day free trial ending on 21 Nov. The trial is 5 days and not 7.

Vendor claim "Your Free plan includes 1 active rule". What we saw: Creating a second rule while one was active showed ACTIVE Locked with this text, so the Free plan really allows 1 active rule over all rule types. A store that needs a payment rule and a validation rule at the same time has to pay for a plan.

Vendor claim "Credit card (Shopify Payments) can only be customized on Shopify Plus plans". What we saw: The Hide settings say so. Our rule that hides the test payment method did not work on the test gateway; whether that gateway counts as this card block is unknown. Hiding or renaming the credit card method of Shopify Payments needs Shopify Plus, so a standard store cannot do that with this app.

Vendor claim "Shopify stores with mixed payment and shipping options". What we saw: The payment rule that should hide the test payment method did not work at 600 dollars, so this audience was not confirmed; shipping rules were not tested and the store only had the test gateway. Whether the app helps a store with mixed payment and shipping options was not shown by this test.

Vendor claim "Shopify merchants with no upsell after checkout". What we saw: Post-purchase upsells are not included on Free or Starter; they come with Starter Plus at $8.99 per month after the first 3 months at 1 dollar, or Unlimited. They were not tested. Post-purchase upsells need Starter Plus or higher.
Vendor claim "Stores that create many draft orders by hand". What we saw: Draft orders were not tested. No evidence for or against draft order help.

Vendor claim "$1 $6.99 /month for your first 3 months then $6.99/month". What we saw: The Starter plan card shows $1 now $6.99 per month for the first 3 months, then $6.99. The Shopify Approve subscription screen for Kedra Starter showed Subtotal $6,99, Discount -$5,99 and Total $1,00 due 21 Nov after a 5-day free trial, $1,00 USD every 30 days, plus any applicable taxes. Card and approval screen agree; tax is unknown and nothing was approved. The yearly price of $58.70 matched the dossier. Starter costs $1 for each of the first 3 months after a 5-day trial and then $6.99 a month, before taxes.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on the free plan in Imagify's web app: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We uploaded three of our own simple test images (a 12 KB PNG, a 50 KB JPG and a 3.4 MB PNG), compared Smart and Lossless and watched the quota counter after each step.
findings: The account started at '0.0KB / 20MB used. You have 100% credit left.' Auto-converting PNG to JPEG is marked 'only for Pro users'; resizing is available on free.
Smart compression took the PNG from 11.8KB to 3.3KB (72.36%) and the JPG from 48.9KB to 12.3KB (74.91%), each within about 8 seconds.

After the first two images the quota counter read 61.44KB of 20MB, much closer to their input sizes than to the compressed results. The later counter increments varied, so we did not establish the exact quota accounting rule.
Lossless took the same PNG from 11.8KB to 5.8KB (51.05%), against 3.3KB with Smart.
The 3.4MB file was refused straight away with 'File size must be under 2.0 MB. Current file size is 3.4 MB' and used no quota.

The summary on the optimizer page is mislabelled: 'You saved 15.5KB out of 60.7KB' gave the size after compression (3.3KB + 12.3KB), while the real saving was about 45KB. The History page showed the right saving per file.
History notes 'Optimized images are available to download for 24 hours' on a free account. End state: 92.16KB of 20MB used after four optimisations and one refused upload.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 6 November 2026 on the free plan: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We converted our fictional invoice from the test kit into a PDF, uploaded it, ran the analysis and read the result and the pricing page. We downloaded nothing and did not open checkout.
findings: Sign-up asked for no card. The dashboard showed 25 credits and a 15 MB limit per file. The page says you can download results as CSV or Excel.
Upload, 'Start Analysis' and 'Analysis complete' took about 15 seconds. The credit counter then read 24.

The document detail page showed only the file name, the date and a 'Merge tables' menu. It held no table and no value, and we saw no download button. No error or warning appeared, yet the analysis had used a credit.

Our invoice lists its lines as plain text (date, amount, custom code, tags, net, tax) and has no table. The app extracts tables, so for this layout we got nothing: none of the seven fields was read out. This is a result for one document of this type, not a measure of accuracy on invoices with tables.

sessions.what: A review account in SurFox's review sandbox, given to us by the founder. The sandbox says so on every page: leads, dashboards and results are sample data, messaging is switched off and the AI Learning page is a mock-up. Two things work for real there, the test conversation on a campaign and Surf, the campaign assistant. We played leads against a sample campaign for an analytics company over SMS on 3 October 2026, sent our findings to SurFox, and re-tested on 6 and 12 October 2026 after they shipped fixes. We did not send a real text, connect a CRM, take a voice call or see the learning feature work on real conversations.
findings: It did not invent a price. Asked what the product costs, the AI said the price depends on data sources and users and would be given on the call, which matched the knowledge document we gave it. A request to stop texting was honoured at once and classed as an opt-out.

The first test, on 3 October, had visible faults: a placeholder [SLOTS] sent as text, a summary claiming the lead had picked a time slot when they had not, a question answered as unknown although the knowledge document covered it, and openers longer than the 150 characters SurFox aims for. SurFox fixed these after our feedback. On 12 October the AI offered three real times, the booking produced a hot-lead email with a calendar file and a 20-minute duration that matched the conversation, and two openers came in at 143 and 130 characters.

Asking for a call directly ('Can someone call me this week?') ended the test as a hand-off to the team without offering a time; asking to book a demo did offer times. Both are reasonable, but you choose which one your campaign should push.

The learning feature that defines the Growth plan could not be judged: the sandbox shows sample data and says real learning needs hundreds of real conversations over several weeks. Delivery, voice, CRM syncing and real costs per conversation were also outside what a sandbox can show.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on a new account, without connecting a website or paying: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. findings: Onboarding has four steps: Train, Brand, Test and Install. Training sources are a website (with linked pages on the same domain, or a sitemap), files, text or YouTube, against a counter of '0 / 500K characters'. Our 177 characters of text were trained in about 10 to 20 seconds.
The dashboard only opens after the onboarding: going to the app sent us back to the get-started steps. The first sign-in magic link returned 'INVALID_TOKEN'; a second one worked.

The guardrails slider starts on 'Max (default): Most sophisticated', which refuses off-topic questions and answers in the user's language; Chatwith warns that 'customizing or overriding the guardrails is difficult'.
All five fact questions were answered correctly, and four of the five rephrased ones, such as 'No. The Lila-17 is purple.' when we asked whether it was red.

Asked whether a fault after one month was covered by the 37-day warranty, it answered 'No. The Lila-17 warranty is 37 days, so it is still covered after one month.': it starts with no and ends with yes.

Asked about Sunday opening, which our text did not cover, it said 'I do not know the answer to this question.' and made nothing up. Our last question, on return costs, stayed at 'Not sent. Retry', also after a retry; we did not find out why.
The test chat made suggestion buttons from the knowledge itself (Product, Color, Pickup, Warranty) and shows 'Powered by Chatwith'.

On 16 November 2026, 26 days after the test, the same agent on our unpaid account answered two questions only with 'This assistant can't reply right now.' That day the pricing page listed no free plan: the cheapest plan was Starter at $9 a month.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Upsell & Cross Sell AW on a Shopify development store: the install, the Free plan, the setup wizard with the app embed saved in the theme, one handpicked upsell seen in the theme editor preview, the plan screens, the locked locations on Free, the Start-Up approval screen (not approved) and the app menu. Nothing was paid, no paid plan was started and nothing was uninstalled. Install: the App Store listing (English) is called Upsell & Cross Sell AW by Aheadworks and says Free plan available. Free trial available., with a rating of 4.8 from 485 reviews; the install screen calls the app Upsell, Cross sell & Bundles and asks for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. Install was approved at about 11:15. Plans: straight after the install the app opened an in-app plans screen (Try any paid plan free for 14 days. Cancel anytime.). We chose the Free plan with Start plan. There was NO Shopify approval screen and no charge; the app went straight to a welcome wizard. Core action: the wizard has four steps: language (English), Enable app embed, Enable blocks on pages and Setup complete. Enable application embed opened the theme editor with the message Cross Sell Auto activated, and we SAVED the theme there (Changes saved.), so the app embed Cross Sell Auto is now on in the theme of our development store. In step three we switched on only the Product pages block. The Dashboard then said Your app embed status is: Enabled, You have 0 active app block(s) on your store and Clicks used in this cycle 0 / 50 (0%). Offer: in Assign > Product page > Upsells we pressed Assign products for The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard and picked The 3p Fulfilled Snowboard, which showed 1 of 15 Cross-Sell(s) Selected. In the theme editor preview of the product page the heading Would you rather like these? appeared with the link Powered by Cross Sell (a brand line on the Free plan) and a card for The 3p Fulfilled Snowboard at $2,629.95 with a plus button. No app block had to be added by hand. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 3 minutes from the start of the install (11:15) to the first offer in the preview (about 11:18), in about 14 clicks. The click counter stayed at 0 / 50 because we did not click the offer, and no order was placed. Plans in the app (monthly): Start-up $29.99 (Visible on first 2 pages, 2,500 clicks monthly, Extra recommendation clicks: $0.01/click, No branding, Upsell pop-up, QuickView button), Small store $49.99 (All 8 types of pages, 5,000 clicks monthly, $0.012/click), Medium store $59.99 (All 8 types of pages, 10,000 clicks monthly, $0.006/click) and Large store $79.99 (50,000 clicks monthly, $0.0016/click). The Account page says the Free plan has a click limit of 50 and 50 clicks remaining before cross-sell recommendations are no longer visible; its renewal date is 17 December 2026. That page shows an admin email and was not kept as evidence. Checkout: via Please upgrade and Upgrade we reached the Shopify Approve subscription screen for the Start-Up plan: You will not be billed for this test charge., Cross Sell - Start-Up Plan (Dev Shop), $29,99 USD every 30 days, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., a subtotal and total of $29,99 due on 1 Dec, an Add payment method row and an Approve button. We did NOT approve: the Free plan was already active and the screen also asked for a payment method. We pressed Cancel and Shopify said Charge declined.; nothing was charged and no plan was started. Cancelling: the app menu in the list of installed apps has Open app, View details, Get support and Uninstall, and no way to cancel or downgrade a paid plan; the plans page says Cancel anytime. and shows no cancel button. The FAQ link on the App Store listing opens a help site that says Not Found. We did not click Uninstall. Not tested: any paid plan, offers on the cart drawer, checkout, thank you page or post purchase, clicking the offer in the preview, an order, the upsell pop-up, real analytics, the storefront outside the theme editor, and uninstalling. Clean up: the app stays installed on the Free plan, the app embed Cross Sell Auto is saved in the theme, and the upsell for The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard still exists. Our own test tabs were closed except one admin tab on the apps list that could not be closed. No kit records were entered.

The app opened straight on the Free plan, with no plan choice, no separate account and no demo, on a screen Welcome to Vify Order Printer with a step guide at 0 of 4. Core action, an invoice for the test order #1001, a little over 1 minute after the start of the install (about 14:29:20) and 3 clicks from the order list: Orders, order #1001, the printer icon, Print invoice. The result was a page called invoice_1001.pdf on a Vify address (api-pdf.vify.ai), which is an HTML print view that calls window.print(); the browser tab stayed on the print dialog. IMPORTANT about the evidence image of the invoice: image 03 is NOT a screenshot of the PDF. Because the tab hung on the print dialog, we rendered the HTML of that same invoice page ourselves, locally and headless, and took the image from that rendering. It shows what the page contains, but we did not open or check the real PDF file, so page size, fonts and the real print result were not seen. You can only view the latest 50 orders. and, for removing the Vify branding in the PDF invoice, Please contact support to verify your store in order to have this feature for free. The profile form was only read for its labels and nothing was typed: the tabs Basic Info, Emails, Phones, Addresses, Addt'l Info, Relatives, Power of Attorney and Safety Program; in Basic Info the fields First Name, Last Name, Middle name (recommended), Birth Year, Birth Day (recommended), Birth Month (recommended) and Gender; a reCAPTCHA stands on the page. Not covered by the service (FAQ): blogs, news, forums, social media (LinkedIn, Facebook, TikTok and others), legal registers, documents online and the dark web. sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026: Daan created the account and our AI assistant finished the onboarding and ran the test in his browser. findings: Signing up did not start on Free. The account landed on a Plus trial ('Trial Period Oct 20 - Nov 03', 1 user, $54/user, 'First monthly payment on Nov 4, 2026') plus a 92-day AI Answers trial, without asking for a payment card.

Switching to Free needed two clean-ups first. Free allows no private Docs site, so the empty knowledge base Help Scout had created had to be made public, and Free allows 0 workflows, so the two '[Try me]' example workflows had to be deleted. The confirmation screen then listed the Free limits, including 10 tags and 10 saved replies.

The 10-tag limit was not enforced right after the switch: an eleventh tag was accepted without any message and Settings > Tags showed '11 tags'. Only a lighter style on the conversation set it apart. Two of the ten were 'welcome' and 'practice', which Help Scout had created itself.

The 10-saved-reply limit was enforced, but with a generic error: 'Could not create saved reply draft' when opening a new one and 'Could not create saved reply' when saving, with no mention of a limit. An example reply Help Scout added counted as one of the ten.
Editing a saved reply worked: changing only the number of warranty days from 37 to 41 left the rest of the text unchanged after a reload.

Two phone notes for the same email address joined one customer profile, and the second showed the first in the sidebar. Help Scout filled in the company on its own ('Internet Assigned Numbers Authority' for example.com), and timestamps did not follow our Europe/Amsterdam time zone: 5:53 am was shown at 07:53 local time.

AI Answers
The Docs site

sessions.what: A new account, which starts on a 14-day trial with paid-plan limits (10,000 sessions a month), not on the Free plan. We put the tracking snippet on a two-page test page of our own, with a sign-up form, a button, a link to a pricing page and an element that looks clickable but does nothing. Then we sent scripted visits whose every step we logged: eight visitors on desktop and phone who clicked, scrolled, filled in the form and gave up halfway, rage-clicked the dead element or left after five seconds, plus two later visits spaced more than a minute apart. We compared the recordings and the friction report with that log.
findings: Recording is off after installation. The dashboard confirmed 'Your tracking code is installed', but nothing was captured until we pressed 'Activate tracking'. Our first round of eight visits was lost that way.

After activation, only the first three visits of the second round were recorded. The other five, and two later visits spaced more than a minute apart, never appeared, while the billing page showed 3 of 10,000 sessions used and the recording rate stood at 100%. All visits came from one address and a scripted browser, so this may be a filter on repeated visits rather than a fault; we could not tell which, and the form, drop-off and rage-click checks could not be scored.

The recordings that did arrive were partly right. The visit that went on to the pricing page showed 2 pages and the phone visit was marked as mobile. The first visitor clicked the main button and scrolled to the bottom over about half a minute, yet the list showed 9 seconds and the friction report counted it as a bounce.
not_tested: the Free plan itself, heatmaps over many visits, funnels, surveys, and real visitors from many addresses
