exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Bold Custom Pricing (in the admin BOLD Custom Pricing: Wholesale) on a Shopify development store: the install, a forced plan choice, the Essential test charge approved without a payment method, one wholesale price rule of 20 percent for one product made in about 2 minutes after the plan approval (the sync stayed in the queue, so the price was not seen in the store), the three plans shown in the app and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was billed. Install: the install button of the App Store listing was pressed at about 14:40 in our own tab; Shopify showed the Install app dialog with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved. The app first showed an onboarding screen with Book my onboarding (a free session with an expert) and Continue without help; we chose Continue without help and booked nothing. The app then forced a plan choice (Select Your Account Plan) before the dashboard opened. In the admin the app is called BOLD Custom Pricing: Wholesale, while the App Store title is Custom Pricing: Wholesale B2B. Plans and approval: the plan screen shows Essential - $29 billed monthly (14-day free trial, 1 Customer Tag, Manual Customer Tagging, Tax Controls, Unlimited Quantity Breaks), Standard - $65 billed monthly (Most popular; 1-10 Customer Tags, Auto-Emails, Auto-Tagging) and Complete - $129 billed monthly (Unlimited Customer Tags, Advanced Detailed Pricing, CSV Price Imports, Shopify POS Integration, Expert Setup, Premier Support, SLA). The dossier names Standard at $69, while the app shows $65. We chose Essential, the cheapest; a dialog Update Plan said This change will update your plan to: Essential at $29 / month. Shopify then showed an Approve subscription screen: You will not be billed for this test charge., plan Essential, $29,00 USD every 30 days, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., Total $29,00 Due 1 Dec, with an Add payment method row that was not filled in. Because the screen said it was a test charge, we approved it; no payment method was entered and nothing was billed, and the app opened without a further payment question. Core action, one price rule for wholesale customers, about 2 minutes after the plan was approved (saved at about 14:42) and about 12 screens or clicks: Manage Tags, Add Tag with the tag wholesale and Discount % 20 (the description is required and the form said Description cannot be empty. until we typed Trade customers); then Product Pricing Groups, Create Product Pricing Group with the Internal Name Wholesale 20 percent off, Calculation Type Percent Discount, Select Products and The 3p Fulfilled Snowboard ($2629.95); Setup Pricing showed a column wholesale with 20 %, and Save. A first try with an empty group had been thrown away because the first group screen said You must have at least one price level for your group. until the tag existed. Result: the group list shows Wholesale 20 percent off, switched on, with Sync queued, and a notice Syncing 0 items with Shopify, 1 items in queue with Product prices will not be updated until its process is synced: and the label In Queue. After 10 seconds it still said In Queue. We did NOT see the price in the store or in the theme preview for a tagged customer, because the sync was still queued; the effect of the rule on a store page was not tested. The onboarding checklist (Select a theme, completed 0 of 5, with a remark about a password protected store) was not followed, because that would ask for a theme change. Cancelling: no payment was ever due, so there was no paid subscription to cancel, and no cancel step was looked for inside the app. The app was uninstalled via Settings, Apps, the row BOLD Custom Pricing: Wholesale and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason is required, we gave Testing multiple apps, and Shopify confirmed that the app was uninstalled. No call or demo was booked. Not tested: the price on the storefront for a tagged customer, checkout, POS, quantity breaks, Auto-Tagging (Standard), CSV import (Complete), a second group or tag, the theme selection and preview, and the onboarding session. Clean up: no theme changes were saved; the app was uninstalled, which removes its tag and group; other apps were not touched; our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app forces a plan choice before the dashboard, a tag with a description has to exist before a group can be saved, the price rule stayed in a sync queue so the result could not be seen, and the Standard plan costs $65 in the app against $69 in the dossier.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Bold Memberships on a Shopify development store: the install, guided setup of a free membership plan with exclusive access and a discount, the review screen with the price, the Shopify test charge (approved without a card, billed 0 dollars) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. The storefront was not seen. Install: the App Store listing (English, now called Bold Memberships & Loyalty) says Free to install. Additional charges may apply., with a rating of 4.4 from 89 reviews. Install was clicked at about 11:36 and the app opened at about 11:38 after the Install app dialog (customer data, staff and contributor data, view and edit store data). There was no plan choice and no price question at install. The welcome screen says Build a membership that brings customers back. and offers Launch with an expert (Book a call, Start a chat) or Build it yourself with Start guided setup. We did not use the call or the chat. Core action: guided setup in three steps. Step one, Free or paid: plan name Test Member (tag test_member), and we chose Free for all customers (Customers join automatically, at no cost). A checkbox offers to add the 6 existing customers now; the text says that if it is left off, existing customers join when they place an order or click Join Now, and that each member counts toward your app plan's member total. Step two, Rewards and benefits: we chose Exclusive access, with the product Bundle Product #1, and Discounts, 10 percent named Member 10 off on All orders. Step three, Finish initial setup: Open theme editor and Create plans page were skipped, so no theme was changed and no store page was created. The review screen Almost done! shows the plan Test Member, the enrollment Free (all customers) and the benefits Exclusive access and Discounts, and says that Bold Memberships is always $0.13 per month/customer, with no transaction fee, no monthly base fee, Free for your first 10 member signups, and Enterprise pricing for over 5,000 customers. After approval the app said You're all set! Your membership plan is live. with a Polish your plan list (1 of 4 done). Timing, approximate tester observations: about 11 minutes from opening the app at 11:38 to the live plan at about 11:49, in about 14 steps. The plan was seen only in the app: the theme embed was not switched on, so the storefront widget and the gated product were not seen. Listing: Scale at $0.13 per member per month, 100% free for the first 30 days, First 10 members are free forever, No flat monthly base fees and No transaction fees. The app agrees on the price, no base fee and no transaction fee; the review screen says free for your first 10 member signups without the word forever and shows no 30 days free. Checkout: the review screen has one button, Start free trial, which opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen for Scale: You will not be billed for this test charge., This app bills you for usage charges, an App spending limit of a maximum of $10.000,00 USD per 30 days, and Your next bill: You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it. The screen shows no price and an Add payment method row. No card was entered and we approved this test charge at about 11:48, which cost nothing. Members: the app text says each member counts toward your app plan's member total, including free members. This was read from the screen only and was not proven with an invoice. Cancelling: we did not look for a cancel button in the app. Cancelling means uninstalling from Settings, Apps. The dialog Uninstall BOLD Memberships? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app such as discounts will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information. A Reason for uninstalling is required (we chose Testing multiple apps) and feedback is optional. The dialog has no warning about running charges or a refund. Not tested: a paid plan with member payments through Stripe, the storefront widget and the gated product (theme embed off), the wallet card, loyalty points, store credit, Shopify POS, the chat or call and the free setup with the team. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 11:55 and is no longer in the list of installed apps; the plan Test Member went with it. No theme change was saved, no page or navigation link was made. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Skip To Checkout, called PF AI: Skip to Checkout in the admin, on a Shopify development store: the install, Skip To Checkout switched on, the app embed switched on, the sticky bar with the button action Direct Buy, the preview in which a click on Shop now went straight to the checkout with one product, and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Two theme changes were saved. Nothing was paid and no plan page exists on the Free Plan. Install: the install button of the App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/cart-auto-update) opened a new tab outside our tab group, so the install was done again through the form in our own tab. The Install app dialog showed Skip to Checkout by Effective Apps and the access View customer data (Device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Customers, products, store analytics, Shopify Functions, Online Store). Install was approved at about 15:24. The app is called PF AI: Skip to Checkout in the admin, with the label Free Plan; the App Store title is now STKY: Sticky Add To Cart Bar, free, 4.8 stars from 38 reviews. The session began at about 15:21. Core action, Skip To Checkout so that the buy button goes straight to the checkout: the dashboard Getting Started lists Enable Skip To Checkout, Enable Sticky Add To Cart Bar App Embed, Enable an Additional Tool and Verify your setup, and an advertisement for another app of the maker is at the top. The page Skip To Checkout says ACTION REQUIRED: Activate the App Embed (The App Embed must be toggled on from the theme settings for Skip To Checkout to work.). Turn on gave Unsaved changes, Save gave Settings saved. The choice Checkout Redirection Type offers Start a checkout just the product that was added to the cart or Start a checkout with the entire cart contents, and the second was selected. In the theme editor, under App embeds, PF Add To Cart/Buy Now was switched on and saved (Changes saved.), which is a theme change that was needed. In the theme preview (without a password), on the product page The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard, the Add to cart button of the theme only opened the cart drawer (Your cart) and did not go to the checkout, also not after a reload, so switching Skip To Checkout on was not enough in this theme. The sticky bar already showed in the editor (Shop now) but with Button click action: Standard Add to Cart. We changed it to Skip to Checkout (Direct Buy) with Checkout mode: Current product only and saved it, a second theme change. Result in the preview: a click on Shop now in the sticky bar (The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard, $949.95) went straight to Checkout of the shop with only that product (1 piece, $949.95, Total USD $949.95), with no cart page and no cart upsell. The preview bar of Shopify at the bottom hid the sticky bar until Hide bar. Time, approximate tester observations: about 3 minutes from the install at about 15:24 to the checkout at about 15:27, in more than 10 steps (install, switch Skip on, switch the embed on and save, open the preview, change the button action and save, reload the preview, hide the bar, Shop now). Plans and checkout: only Free Plan was seen; there was no plan page and no Shopify approval screen, nothing was paid and no card was asked, which agrees with the listing (Free). Cancelling: no subscription ran. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Skip to Checkout? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (the Uninstall button stays grey until one is chosen) and Testing multiple apps was chosen. The app was uninstalled at about 15:28 and left the installed list. Not tested: hiding Add to cart or Buy it now for shops that sell in person, the sticky bar on a phone and the scrolling on long product pages (Show on Mobile), the effect on the add to cart rate, Verify Setup (it asks the vendor experts) and the vendor contact. No call, demo or separate account was asked. Clean up: two theme changes (the app embed on and the button action Direct Buy) stay saved in the theme test-data, but the embed belongs to the app and goes away with the uninstall; the cart of the preview already held products from earlier tests and one Snowboard was added, so it held 2 pieces after the test; the app was uninstalled; one tab that the install button opened outside our tab group could not be closed with our tools. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Kumo (B2B Wholesale Tools) on a Shopify development store: the install, a 20 percent price rule for customers with a tag, the preview price, the Plans page with greyed out Select buttons and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was saved in the theme and nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing (English) is called Kumo B2B Wholesale Tools, from Cloudlift, and says From $15/month. Free trial available., with a rating of 5.0 from 9 reviews and a launch date of 21 November 2024; it names B2B at $15 a month and PLUS at $30 a month, both with a 7-day free trial, and says all charges are billed in USD, with recurring and usage based charges every 30 days. Install was clicked at about 11:52 and asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data (customers, products, discounts, Shopify Functions, Online Store, Shopify admin). The app, called B2B Wholesale Tools in the admin, opened straight on Home with no plan screen and no Approve subscription screen. Home showed a Setup Guide at 0 / 3 completed (Enable the app, Setup your first price config, Test pricing on your store), App not enabled with a button Enable App in theme editor, and an onboarding call with Book a call, which we did not use. Core action: Setup pricing, Create pricing. We named the rule Wholesale 20 percent, type Percentage, discount 20, customer conditions Targets customers with specific tags with the tag wholesale, product conditions Applies to all products, status Active. Save gave Config saved and the rule showed as Active; the Message field filled itself with WHOLESALE_20_PERCENT. Preview product with Bundle Product #1, which the product picker lists at $1,382.31, showed $ 1,105.60 in the app. A 20 percent discount on $1,382.31 is $1,105.85, so the app preview is 25 cents lower than that; we did not find out why. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 2 minutes from the install click at about 11:52:57 to the preview price at about 11:54:58, in about 10 steps. The theme editor was not used and nothing was saved in the theme; the app was not enabled in the theme, so the price was not seen in the store preview and no customer with the tag wholesale was tried. The menu also has Add Volume pricing, Add Bulk ordering, Add Minimum quantity, Forms, Submissions, Checkout and Price lists; these were not tested. Plans: the Plans page said Your current plan: DEVELOPER and You are on a development store! You are on a unlimited trail plan until this store goes live. B2B $15 a month lists Wholesale pricing, Volume pricing, Registration forms and Approval workflow; PLUS $30 a month lists All of B2B features, Product catalog assignment and Shopify plus checkout integration. The PLUS card shows two Plus features in the app, while the listing names three, including company registration. Both Select buttons were greyed out, so no Shopify approval screen was reached and nothing could be approved. Cancelling: there was no subscription to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, Uninstall; the dialog says that you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information. A Reason for uninstalling is required (we chose Testing multiple apps) and feedback is optional. Not tested: a real customer with the tag wholesale in the store, volume pricing, the registration form, the approval workflow, CSV price lists, the checkout settings, the Plus features, any paid plan and the trial. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 11:56 and Shopify confirmed it; the plan and its discounts went with it. Nothing was saved in the theme. Our own tabs were closed, except one tab opened by the install button that could not be closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on the free Pay As You Go plan, without a card and without connecting a mailbox: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We described a made-up bicycle repair workshop in four fields, with three hard facts (repairs only, no bike sales; open Monday to Friday 09:00 to 17:00; no appointments by phone), and checked what the onboarding built from it.
findings: The whole onboarding, which built a company profile, an ideal customer profile, an AI team, a knowledge base, website agents, first leads, an email sequence, a content plan and sample content in about two minutes, cost 4 credits in 14 requests (Company Search 7 requests / 2 credits, Content Engine 6 / 2, Sequence 1 / 0). The General page then read 'Monthly credits 4 / 50'.

Of our three facts, the profile kept one ('without the sale of retail bicycles'), blurred one into 'standard weekday business hours' and replaced the third with something we never said: 'By operating as a walk-in facility'. It also set the industry to 'Transportation'.

Without asking, it built a list of 16 real people (facility and operations managers at large companies in Amsterdam) around a partnership idea of its own, and enrolled all 16 in a five-email, AI-personalised sequence. The screen says the sequence 'stays paused until you connect a mailbox and turn on sending'; we connected no mailbox and nothing was sent. We did not record the names.

The content plan, in three funnel stages, promised things we never said: 'Our same-day repair policy explained', 'Success stories: Keeping busy local families mobile' and a 'high-speed repair experience'. Our opening hours and the phone rule appeared nowhere, and the blog draft targeted 'bicycle repair shop' at 22,200 estimated searches a month in the US, for a Dutch audience.

It proposed six AI employees (sales, support, an appointment scheduler and SEO among them) and two chat widgets, for sales and support, each with a ready-made script snippet to paste into a site. sessions.what: We did not summarise the marketing. Nextify.ai gave us Pro access for this test (disclosed here and in the video that goes with this review) and nothing else was agreed: no copy approval, and no draft shared before publication. On 7 September 2026 we generated a real ad from a product image inside that account, read the credit cost the app charges for every model it offers, and checked the pricing page both signed in and signed out. Everything below is what the product did and charged, not what the site says it does.
findings: Credits are charged per second of output, not per video. A four-second 720p clip on Seedance 2.0, the model the editor pre-selects, cost 48 credits and took the balance from 3,000 to 2,952. The app's own credit table prices that combination at 12 a second, and the Generate button reads 48 before you commit, so the arithmetic is visible if you know to look for it.

Every tier's video count assumes 20 credits a video. Starter's 1,000 credits are sold as 50 videos, Pro's 3,000 as 150 and Business's 8,000 as 400: all exactly 20 apiece, which is four seconds on the cheapest 5-credit-a-second model. On the model the editor actually opens with, Pro is 62 clips; at the 15-second maximum it is 16.

No image model costs what the image counts assume. Those counts work out at 2 credits an image on every tier, including the free one. The cheapest image model in the table is Nano Banana 2 at 1k for 7 credits, and the pre-selected GPT Image 2 is 10: the button literally reads “Generate Image 10”. Starter's “up to 500 images” is about 100.

The avatar tools are the expensive ones, and they are the reason most people arrive. UGC Product Video and Lip-sync run on HeyGen AV4 at 6.7 credits a second, identical at 720p and 1080p, over 3 to 120 seconds. A 30-second avatar ad is 201 credits and a 60-second one is 402, so a Pro month is fourteen or seven of them.

Free users cannot reach the Seedance models at all. The model configuration marks seedance-2.0, seedance-2.0-fast and seedance-2.0-mini as unavailable on the free plan, so the 50 free credits run on Kling or MiniMax with a watermark: about two three-second clips.

“In seconds” is not what happens, but “three minutes” is fair. Our four-second clip took 126 seconds from submit to finished file, against the app's own on-screen estimate of four minutes. The homepage claim “Product Image to Viral Ad in 3 Minutes” holds up; the “in seconds” line on the same page does not.

The output was accurate to the prompt. We asked for a stainless steel insulated bottle on a kitchen counter in morning light, a hand picking it up, clean styling and no text overlay, and that is what came back: 9:16, 720p, four seconds, with generated audio. Nothing in the result argued against the tool; the argument is with the pricing page.
The pricing page hides the free plan once you sign in. Signed out, Free sits at the head of the ladder; signed in, the same URL starts at Starter.

sessions.what: Daan created the free account and logged in; everything after that was read inside the workspace on 11 September 2026 -- the credit screen, the plans and billing screen and the upgrade panel -- alongside Bitscale's own credit documentation. Two limits worth stating plainly. We did not run an enrichment: the grid renders in a canvas our browser panel could not drive, so the per-record credit costs below come from Bitscale's published credit table and not from a meter we moved ourselves. And Bitscale is an affiliate partner of ours; their partner manager offered 2,000 bonus credits that same morning, which had not been added when we looked -- the account was on the ordinary free allowance of 200, which is what a new reader gets.
findings: The free tier runs two meters, not one, and the account screen shows both: 200 platform credits and 2,000 search credits, each resetting monthly, with the next search reset dated on the page. Enriching a record spends platform credits; finding one through Find People or Find Companies spends a search credit, one per record. A reader budgeting on "200 credits" is reading half the meter, and it is the half that runs out first.

On Free, nothing carries over. The billing screen states it twice -- "Rolled-Over Credits: Not included in the plan" and "Rollover Limit: Not included in the plan" -- so an unused month is gone rather than banked. Rollover is listed among the things the first paid plan adds, next to credit rollover, the 100+ providers, action columns beyond 20 per grid, and the inbound integrations (RB2B, Factors, Vector).

What one enriched record costs is published, and the range is the whole story: one to twelve platform credits per successful email or phone lookup, depending on how many providers the waterfall is allowed to try. An AI enrichment is one to two credits a run, a BitAgent website scrape one per query, and anything arriving through the API is free. On Growth that turns 15,000 credits into anywhere between 1,250 and 15,000 enriched contacts -- 2.3 cents each at one credit, 28 cents at twelve.

The in-app upgrade panel carries a Growth benefit the public plan cards do not mention: three hours a quarter with a GTM engineer, alongside the 15,000 credits. Worth knowing before you compare the $349 against a pure data vendor, because it is consulting time rather than volume.

The two meters are set to become convertible. Bitscale's documentation announces 1 platform credit = 10 search credits as an upcoming feature, handled manually for enterprise accounts today. Until that ships, a month where you burn the enrichment pool cannot be topped up from the search pool, however much of it is left.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on the 14-day trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser. We could not create a ticket ourselves without connecting a mailbox, so Daan sent two test tickets with made-up details through SupportBee's own contact form, solving its reCAPTCHA himself. On those we added an internal comment, labels and a snippet, then edited the snippet and inserted it again. Nothing was sent to a customer.
findings: The '+ Ticket' action is blocked until a mailbox is connected: 'Please connect an email address to create tickets. New tickets can't be created without a connected email address.' Incoming tickets through SupportBee's contact form worked without that connection.

Admin > Emails > Add email offers only 'Gmail / Google Workspace' and 'Microsoft Outlook / Office 365', through a connection that copies your support mail into SupportBee. For any other provider the screen says 'Please contact us at support@supportbee.com'.

The contact form is the way in without a mailbox. It has a reCAPTCHA on by default, and setting 'Show captcha' to No did not stay saved. Both test tickets arrived as 'Unanswered', source 'Web Ticket', with a customer profile (name and email).

Internal comments sit in the right-hand sidebar, apart from the reply box. A comment was saved, the ticket stayed 'Unanswered', and SupportBee then assigned the ticket to the person who wrote the comment.

A label without a colour was not created and no error appeared (two tries, the list stayed at 1 label); with a colour it worked at once. Labels set from the ticket header showed in the list view and the sidebar.

A snippet ('Lila heeft 37 dagen garantie.', 'Lila has a 37-day warranty') was found with 'Search snippets' above the reply box and inserted as a draft. After we changed 37 to 41 and clicked Update Snippet, the second ticket showed the new text straight away and inserted 'Lila heeft 41 dagen garantie.' ('Lila has a 41-day warranty')
The trial opened with an example ticket ('Sample Ticket: How to use SupportBee'), a default label IMPORTANT and an example snippet ('Send your browser details').

sessions.what: We did not read the docs and summarise them: PartnerStack is the platform our own affiliate operation runs on. We manage 58 partner programmes through it, pull the Partner API v2 on a schedule, and stamp sub-IDs across 704 pages of our own site. PartnerStack is also an affiliate partner of ours, we earn 15% of every sale for a year on anyone who signs up through our link, which is why the findings below are things we measured against our own records rather than claims from their marketing.
findings: A record in the customers endpoint is a tracked click, not a signup. One plain curl on a tracking link produced a customer record one second later, has_paid false, with no browser and no account. Records surface in the API about five minutes after the click, so allow ten before concluding a test did nothing.

Clicks arrive without a source. There is no referring-URL field in the partnership data, so the platform can tell you a link was clicked and never which page produced it. We had to build sub-ID stamping across our own pages to answer that question ourselves.

Commission terms do not come from the API. offers.base_rate is returned null on every partnership we hold. The readable source is PartnerStack's own public directory at market.partnerstack.com, and it sometimes contradicts the vendor's own affiliate page, which is worth knowing before you quote a rate to anyone.

Programme status lags the reality by days. One partner sent us a welcome email with a working tracking link on 7 August; the API still read application-denied and only turned active somewhere between 13 and 18 August. Treat the vendor's email as the leading indicator and the API status as the one that catches up.
The earned-commission endpoints are the weakest part. rewards and transactions did not return usable data for us, so what you have actually been paid is a dashboard question rather than an API one.

Partner replies break email threading. A partner answers inside the PartnerStack dashboard and the platform sends that on as a fresh message from hello@partnerstackmail.com, with a new Message-ID and no reference to the mail it is answering. Any automation of yours that matches replies to threads will not match these.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on the 7-day trial that starts with a new account, without a card: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We gave the Lyro AI agent five questions and answers about a made-up shop, asked it ten questions in the Playground, two it could not know, and changed one answer to see how fast it followed. The chat widget was not installed.
findings: Sign-up requires a website URL ('Can't be empty!'). Within minutes Tidio read 71 pages of the site we entered into Lyro's knowledge on its own. The source list can delete or set an audience in bulk, but excluding a source without deleting it is one source at a time. Before testing our five Q&As we deleted all 71 website sources Tidio had imported automatically, so the answers were checked against our test knowledge alone.
Usage and plan showed 'AI conversations 0/50' marked 'Lifetime quota' for Lyro. After 13 Playground questions it still read 0 / 50: Playground questions do not count.
A CSV with the columns Question and Answer was accepted as it was (5 Q&As).

Lyro answered nine of the ten fact and paraphrase questions fully. For the warranty question it repeated the correct 37-day term but did not determine whether one month fell within it. Each answer was marked 'AI response based on your data sources'.
Asked whether a fault after one month was covered by a 37-day warranty, Lyro gave the 37 days but said 'I'm not able to determine whether one month falls within that period'.
For the two questions our data did not answer (Sunday opening, return costs) it said it had no information and offered 'Talk to a person'; it made nothing up.
After we changed the warranty from 37 to 41 days, the next question was answered with 41 days.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Storista on a Shopify development store only in part: the install, the empty dashboard on the free plan, the onboarding with its three sources (Instagram, TikTok, Upload files), the plan page with Starter at $15, Growth at $49 and Scale at $199, and the Starter approval screen (it asked for a payment method and had no test charge sentence, so nothing was approved). The core action, importing a video and placing a widget, was not achieved: the upload field sits in a cross-origin iframe that the test tool cannot reach, and the Instagram and TikTok route needs a username and a rights tick box that was not ticked. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Nothing was paid and nothing was saved in the theme. Install: the app was installed through the install form in our own tab at 16:55; the dialog Install app asked for access to customer data, staff data and store data, and the app was installed at 16:56. The App Store name is Storista Shoppable Videos UGC; in the admin the app is called Storista (by Storista LLC). The admin was in English. After the install the app opened straight on Welcome to Storista with three steps (Choose source, Import and Tag, Embed); no payment and no account on the vendor site were needed, and the dashboard said You're on Free. Core action, importing a video and placing a widget: this was NOT achieved and no result was measured. The onboarding asks Where should we get your videos from? with the choices Instagram, TikTok and Upload files. Instagram and TikTok ask for a username and a tick box with the text that you have all rights and permissions to import content from that account; the tick box was not ticked because we have no account of our own to import from. That is a limit of the test tool and not a fault of the app. The Media Library was empty (Click Import content to add content) and Recent widgets said You don't have any widgets yet. Starter adds auto-sync, multiple products per video, GEO/SEO optimization, Shop app integration, import by URL, upload files up to 1GB, manual captions uploads and removal of the branding. The sentence You will not be billed for this test charge was NOT on the screen and a payment method was needed, so the charge was not approved and it was cancelled. Nothing was billed and no card was entered. The Growth and Scale approval screens were not opened. Cancelling: no subscription was started, so nothing could be cancelled. The way to stop is to uninstall: Settings, Apps, Storista, Uninstall opens Uninstall Storista? with the text that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, a request to delete customer data within 48 hours and a required reason (Testing multiple apps). Not tested: a video import, a widget in the theme editor, the Shop app, auto-sync, AI tagging, the unlimited videos claim on Free, auto captions in any language, and any paid plan. No theme change was made or saved and no widget or page was created. Our own tabs were closed. The clock times in the notes (16:55 and 16:56) can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested MigrationPro on a Shopify development store: the install, the external dashboard, the choice of source platforms, a free demo migration of 2 made-up products from a self-made CSV file with an invented source address (done in about 2 minutes 10 seconds, with the products left Active in the store), the paid options, the one-time checkout of $29 (not paid) and the All-In-One package (not entered), and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid. Listing and install: the App Store listing MigrationPro: Store Migration shows a rating of 5.0 (190) and Free to install. Additional charges may apply. The dossier said (5 October) that the listing had been withdrawn; it is now installable. The install button opened a pop-up to the Shopify grant screen for MP - Store Migration & Import with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved at 14:51. After the install the app opened straight on an external dashboard, app.migrationpro.io, logged in through Shopify, with no separate account asked. A message Finish setting up your account (confirm a notification email and choose a company type) was not followed. A vendor live chat widget opened by itself and showed messages; we sent nothing. Core action, a demo migration, about 2 minutes 10 seconds from the install (14:51 to about 14:53:40) and more than 12 steps, partly because we had to make a file and invent a source address: Create New Migration offers 52 source platforms (among them WooCommerce, PrestaShop, Wix and CSV); for most platforms a real source URL and a connector file (mp_connector.zip, to upload by FTP) are needed, which was not possible without a source store. We chose the source CSV, which asks for a Source Store URL (required) and CSV files (Categories, Products, Product Variants, Customers, Orders, Order Items, Blog Posts, Blog Comments, CMS Pages, Discounts). There is no built-in demo or test source. We used a Products.csv that we made ourselves with 2 made-up products (Demo Mug and Demo Shirt) and the address https://example.com as source URL; no login details were entered. In the Configure step we ticked Products. Paid options: Migrate Only Active Products ($39), Migrate Content Images from Products, Categories, CMS pages and Blog Posts ($29), Implement 301 Redirects in Target Store Post-Migration ($29), Convert Categories to Shopify Automated Collections ($29), Set Out-of-Stock Product Quantity to 100 in Target Store ($19) and Calculate Product Price with Tax ($39); free options: Target Store Data Reset, Generate Product Variants from Option Combinations and Consolidate Short and Full Descriptions; none was switched on. The CSV Headers Mapping filled in name, description and price by itself. The button Next: Run Free Demo Migration was pressed at 14:53:31 and after about 10 seconds the page said Demo migration complete. Please review your data and proceed with full migration. with the table Products 2/2. In the Shopify admin, Demo Shirt and Demo Mug appeared as Active products, with our store name as vendor. This is a demo of two made-up products from a CSV with an invented source address; a real migration from a real source store was not tested. Plans and checkout: there is no Shopify subscription screen, no Approve subscription and no test charge; payment runs outside Shopify. The checkout page of the migration shows Entities $29, Enabled Additional Migration Options $0, Additional development $0, Order total $29, the note This is one-time payment only, a Discount code field, and the payment methods Credit card (Pay with credit card via Stripe) or PayPal (Pay with your PayPal account) with a Place order button, which we did not press because it is a real payment. The price depends on the number of records: 2 products gave $29; the pricing page has a calculator (products, customers, orders) that we did not use. The All-In-One Migration Package (A dedicated Personal Assistant will handle all aspects) is priced at $300 with Estimated time - 1 day and starts with a Consultation with the vendor experts; we did not go further because it means a conversation. Cancelling: there is no subscription to cancel, because the payment is one-time. The app was uninstalled via Settings, Apps and Uninstall; the dialog says that a request will be sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information, and asks for a reason and optional feedback; we gave Testing multiple apps at 14:58 and the app left the installed list. Not tested: a real migration from a source store, 301 redirects, images, customers and orders, Smart Sync, the payment, the All-In-One package with its consultation, the live chat and confirming the notification email. Clean up: the two demo products Demo Shirt and Demo Mug are still Active in the store and were not deleted; the app was uninstalled; a helper file with the CSV was kept outside the project; one pop-up tab of the first install attempt could not be closed with our tools. No kit records were entered.

Nothing was paid. Listing and install: the App Store listing MigrationPro: Store Migration shows a rating of 5.0 (190) and Free to install. Additional charges may apply. The dossier said (5 October) that the listing had been withdrawn; it is now installable. The install button opened a pop-up to the Shopify grant screen for MP - Store Migration & Import with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved at 14:51. After the install the app opened straight on an external dashboard, app.migrationpro.io, logged in through Shopify, with no separate account asked. A message Finish setting up your account (confirm a notification email and choose a company type) was not followed. A vendor live chat widget opened by itself and showed messages; we sent nothing. Core action, a demo migration, about 2 minutes 10 seconds from the install (14:51 to about 14:53:40) and more than 12 steps, partly because we had to make a file and invent a source address: Create New Migration offers 52 source platforms (among them WooCommerce, PrestaShop, Wix and CSV); for most platforms a real source URL and a connector file (mp_connector.zip, to upload by FTP) are needed, which was not possible without a source store. We chose the source CSV, which asks for a Source Store URL (required) and CSV files (Categories, Products, Product Variants, Customers, Orders, Order Items, Blog Posts, Blog Comments, CMS Pages, Discounts). There is no built-in demo or test source. We used a Products.csv that we made ourselves with 2 made-up products (Demo Mug and Demo Shirt) and the address https://example.com as source URL; no login details were entered. In the Configure step we ticked Products. Paid options: Migrate Only Active Products ($39), Migrate Content Images from Products, Categories, CMS pages and Blog Posts ($29), Implement 301 Redirects in Target Store Post-Migration ($29), Convert Categories to Shopify Automated Collections ($29), Set Out-of-Stock Product Quantity to 100 in Target Store ($19) and Calculate Product Price with Tax ($39); free options: Target Store Data Reset, Generate Product Variants from Option Combinations and Consolidate Short and Full Descriptions; none was switched on. The CSV Headers Mapping filled in name, description and price by itself. The button Next: Run Free Demo Migration was pressed at 14:53:31 and after about 10 seconds the page said Demo migration complete. Please review your data and proceed with full migration. with the table Products 2/2. In the Shopify admin, Demo Shirt and Demo Mug appeared as Active products, with our store name as vendor. This is a demo of two made-up products from a CSV with an invented source address; a real migration from a real source store was not tested. Plans and checkout: there is no Shopify subscription screen, no Approve subscription and no test charge; payment runs outside Shopify. The checkout page of the migration shows Entities $29, Enabled Additional Migration Options $0, Additional development $0, Order total $29, the note This is one-time payment only, a Discount code field, and the payment methods Credit card (Pay with credit card via Stripe) or PayPal (Pay with your PayPal account) with a Place order button, which we did not press because it is a real payment. The price depends on the number of records: 2 products gave $29; the pricing page has a calculator (products, customers, orders) that we did not use. The All-In-One Migration Package (A dedicated Personal Assistant will handle all aspects) is priced at $300 with Estimated time - 1 day and starts with a Consultation with the vendor experts; we did not go further because it means a conversation. Cancelling: there is no subscription to cancel, because the payment is one-time. The app was uninstalled via Settings, Apps and Uninstall; the dialog says that a request will be sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information, and asks for a reason and optional feedback; we gave Testing multiple apps at 14:58 and the app left the installed list. On 17 November 2026 the session tested StoreFAQ on a Shopify development store on the Free plan: the install, three test FAQs, the FAQ schema switch, the preview of the app page /a/faqs, the plan cards and the Professional approval screen (not approved). The preview said that no FAQs were found until a group was made, because FAQs without a group do not show; after the group Shipping and returns was made the question and its answer showed in the preview, about 4 minutes after the install. The structured data was not seen, nothing was paid, and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form on the App Store page was opened in our own tab at about 17:40 and the permissions of the app were approved at about 17:41; the app opened on the page Choose the perfect plan for your store. The admin was in English. The version of the app is 3.7.7 by Storeware. Plan: the Free plan ($0) was chosen at once, with no card, no phone number and no account on the vendor site. Core action, an FAQ page: at about 17:42 the first FAQ, How long does shipping take?, was made in the group Ungrouped and the message FAQ created appeared. In the setup guide Enable FAQ Schema was clicked, which gave the message FAQ Schema toggled., and the page Settings then shows Enable FAQ Schema with the label On. A second FAQ, What is your return policy?, was also made as Ungrouped. Result: the preview of the app page /a/faqs in the theme editor said Sorry, No FAQs found. The app gives the reason: if you keep the FAQ group as Ungrouped it will not show on the front end. FAQs without a group are therefore invisible. A group Shipping and returns was made (the first try hung on a spinner, the second worked) and a third FAQ, Do you ship internationally?, was put in it. At about 17:44 the preview showed the group and, opened, the answer Yes, we ship to most countries. Shipping costs show at checkout. So the first visible result took about 4 minutes and about 15 steps from the install, and only after the group was made; the app does not warn about the missing group when an FAQ is saved. The address of the FAQ page is an app proxy path, /a/faqs, on the store domain. FAQ schema: only the On switch was seen. The structured data (JSON-LD) in the output of the page was NOT read, because the preview is a cross-origin frame and the store has a password. Whether the FAQ schema is really output, and whether it is valid, was not tested. Plans: the plan cards in the app (Black Friday offer, code BFCMSALE40, 40 percent off) show Professional $7.99 struck through to $4.79 a month, Growth $14.99 to $8.99 and Enterprise $49.99 to $29.99. Free: Up to 100 FAQ Page Views and AI Conversations 25 (Lifetime). Professional: Monthly plan includes 500 page views, extra usage billed at $0.0075/view. Growth: 2,000 page views, extra usage billed at $0.0075/view. Both: $0.30 per extra conversation after limit. Enterprise: Unlimited usage of page views. Billing for page views and conversations is capped at $7.99, $14.99 and $49.99 a month individually. Differences with the dossier: the dossier gives an overage of $0.0159 a view on Professional and $0.0075 on Growth; the app shows $0.0075 a view on Professional as well, so the Professional overage in the app is lower than in the dossier. The Black Friday offer BFCMSALE40 is not in the dossier. Checkout: Subscribe now on Professional opened a dialog with Subtotal $7.99, Discount: (BFCMSALE40) -$3.2 and Total $4.79, and then the Shopify screen Approve subscription: plan professional-monthly, $7,99 struck through and $4,79 USD every 30 days, an App spending limit of a maximum of $15,98 USD per 30 days (twice the $7.99 cap), a badge 40% off 1 charge, a row Add payment method and a greyed out Approve button, with Total $4,79 due 17 Nov plus any applicable taxes. The sentence about a test charge was NOT on the screen and a payment method had to be added, so nothing was approved; no card was entered. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so nothing could be cancelled; the way to stop is to remove the app in Settings, Apps, which was done after the test. Not tested: the two Ungrouped FAQs (they stay invisible until they get a group), the AI chatbot and Instant Answer, Write with AI (it asks for an OpenAI key), Live Chat, import and export of FAQs as CSV, multilingual FAQs on the Professional plan, what happens when the limit of 100 page views is passed, and the JSON-LD of the FAQ schema. Clean up: the theme was not saved; the app made no page in the store, because /a/faqs is an app proxy that disappears when the app is removed; the app was uninstalled afterwards. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested SEOmatic on a Shopify development store on the Free plan: the install, the scan of the products with suggestions and scores, an AI title for Bundle Product #1 (59 characters) that was saved so that the score went from 60% to 65%, the empty Activity Log after that save, the plan page and the Starter yearly approval screen (not approved). The title stays in the store. Nothing was paid, and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form on the App Store page was opened in our own tab at 17:49; the permission screen listed View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data (products, Online Store, Shopify admin), and Install was clicked. The app opened on the Pricing page with Your plan: Free, with no card, no phone number and no account on the vendor site. The admin was in English. The app menu has SEO Optimizer, Image Optimizer, AI SEO Autopilot, Rich Results (Schema), Technical SEO, Pricing and Activity Log. Core action, a scan and one AI fix for one product: SEO Optimizer first said Your products are being imported please wait. After a reload (about 1 minute) the list stood there with per product a number of suggestions and an SEO score: Appointment 70%, Build Your Snowboard Gift Box 75%, Bundle Product #1 60% with 5 suggestions, Demo Mug 70% and Demo Shirt 70%. On the page of Bundle Product #1 the issues were Title length is too short, Description is empty, Alt tag missing in 1 image, Alt tag is too long in 1 image and Target keyword is not found. The button Rephrase with AI on the page title turned into Regenerate 1/3 (three tries per field) and gave a proposal that starts with Bundle Product 1 - Exclusive Bundle Deal and ends with the name of our development store, 59 of 70 characters. Use It and Save followed (the page showed Unsaved changes first) and the issue became Title length is good. After a reload of the list Bundle Product #1 had 65% and 4 suggestions (before 60% and 5), so the save really worked. Time, approximate tester observations: the scan was visible and the AI fix was saved within about 3 minutes of the install (17:49 to about 17:51), in about 12 steps. No bulk change was saved. Store change: one change was saved in the store, the SEO title of the product Bundle Product #1, and it was not put back; it stays in the store with the name of our development store at the end. Activity log: after the save the page Activity Log still said No record found., so the saved work is not in the log, which confirms the complaint in the dossier. Plans: the switch is on Annually (20% Off) by default: Starter $12.00 a month (Billed as $144.00 for 1 year, 6000 Pages), Basic $20.00 a month ($240.00 a year, 24,000 Pages) and Advanced $32.00 a month ($384.00 a year, 60,000 Pages), each with a 14-Day Free Trial. Monthly: Starter $15.00 a month with 500 Pages, Basic $25.00 with 2,000 Pages and Advanced $40.00 with 5,000 Pages. The list holds Unlimited Images Optimized, SEO Audit & Optimization, Auto-pilot, AI metatags (Limited Rephrasing on Starter yearly, Unlimited Rephrasing on the others), SEO Sitemap Submission, Schema MarkUps and Broken Links. Differences with the dossier: the app counts Pages and the dossier speaks of products; the yearly caps are 12 times the monthly ones (6000, 24,000 and 60,000 pages a year). The monthly prices $15, $25 and $40 are those of the dossier. Checkout: Get this deal on Starter, yearly, opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription: Starter Yearly, $144,00 USD every year, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., Subtotal $144,00 plus any applicable taxes, Total $144,00 due 1 Dec, a row Add payment method and a greyed out Approve button. The sentence about a test charge was NOT on the screen and a payment method had to be added, so nothing was approved; no card was entered; the screen was closed with Cancel. Cancelling: no subscription ran, because the Free plan was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall; the dialog says that you can no longer use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason is required (we chose Testing multiple apps). Not tested: the Image Optimizer, AI SEO Autopilot, Rich Results, Technical SEO, the meta description and the alt tags, bulk changes, restoring original images, what happens to the saved title after the uninstall, the theme editor and how the title looks in the shop. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test and left the list of installed apps; the saved SEO title of Bundle Product #1 was not reverted; our own tabs were closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.
findings: Text we checked: "Title length is good". What we saw: The AI title of 59 of 70 characters was saved for Bundle Product #1; the issue Title length is too short went away and the list showed 65% and 4 suggestions instead of 60% and 5. The title stays in the store.
Text we checked: "No record found". What we saw: After the title was saved the Activity Log still said No record found., so the saved work is not logged, as the dossier complains.
Text we checked: "Starter $15.00/month". What we saw: The monthly plan cards show Starter $15.00, Basic $25.00 and Advanced $40.00 a month, as the dossier says.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested StoreSEO on a Shopify development store: the install, one scan of 20 products that took 13 seconds and gave a score of 44 (19 of 20 meta titles and all 20 meta descriptions need work), no fix, the plan step with the Black Friday offer and all four plans including Growth, and the Lite checkout, where the Shopify approval screen showed $3,99 due 17 Nov, asked to add a payment method and had no test charge sentence. Install: the App Store listing (English) was opened at 18:16, the install form was submitted in our own tab, and the Shopify dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked at about 18:17. The app opened on a short start with the text that it was ready to scan the store and the buttons I want free SEO consultation, Detailed documentation guides, Full walkthrough and Analyze My Store; only Analyze My Store was used. The footer says Version: 4.1.7. No account on the vendor site, password, card or phone number was asked and no Google account was connected. The admin was in English. Core action, one SEO scan of the store: Analyze My Store was clicked once at about 18:17 and the result stood there at about 18:18. The progress line said Scan Progress 13 sec 100% Complete, with the steps Scanning Product and Analyzing SEO Score (Meta Title, Image Alt Text, Meta Description, Product Description, Focus Keyword Density, Optimized Images). The result: Your Current SEO Score is: 44; I've analyzed 20 products from your catalog; 19 of 20 Meta titles need work; 20 of 20 Meta descriptions need work; 20 of 20 Product descriptions need work; 0 of 18 Images missing alt text. Under Fix your first product the lowest products were The Hidden Snowboard (Not Optimized, Score 31), Harbour Tour Test (37), The Complete Snowboard (37), The Multi-managed Snowboard (38) and The Compare at Price Snowboard (38). No fix was run, Fix SEO score was not used and nothing was saved. Time from install to the scan result: about 1 to 2 minutes and 2 steps (install, Analyze My Store). Plans: Skip setup led to the plan step, Fix your 20 products with AI, Pick a plan. Every plan starts with a 7-day free trial., with a banner Grab Your First Month Black Friday Deal, Flat 80% OFF. The Black Friday offer in the app uses the code BFCM2026 for 80% off the first month. Checkout: by accident the checkout of Essential was opened first (it was preselected) and closed without paying. Then Lite was chosen and the dialog Checkout: Lite showed Plan Price $19.99, Duration 1 month, Sub Total $19.99, Discount BFCM2026 -$16.00 (applied 80% discount for the next 1 month, after that the regular price applies) and Total $3.99; Subscribe now was clicked. The Shopify screen Approve subscription then showed Lite, 1000 AI Credits, 500 Images, $19,99 $3,99 USD every 30 days, Your next bill Subtotal $19,99 plus any applicable taxes, Discount $16,00 and Total $3,99 Due 17 Nov, a row Add payment method and a greyed out Approve button. There was no free trial on this path and the sentence about a test charge was NOT on the screen. A payment method had to be added, so nothing was approved; no card was entered and the screen was closed with Cancel. The link Try free for 7 days was not used. Cancelling: no subscription was started, so nothing could be cancelled. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall; the app was uninstalled after the test. Not tested: a fix of one product, the bulk AI fix, the Free plan after Continue with FREE, the 7-day trial path, Google Search Console and Analytics, schema, the sitemap, LLMs.txt, the MCP connector, buying credits and a refund. sessions.what: accessiBe's free accessScan scanner, not the paid accessWidget overlay this review prices. We built two versions of the same small landing page: one with 20 accessibility errors we placed on purpose and wrote down beforehand (missing page language and title, images without text alternatives, unlabelled form fields, low contrast, a skipped heading level, a table without header cells, a clickable div, a positive tabindex, an unlabelled iframe and more), and a twin with all 20 fixed. We scanned both and, as a reference, ran the free open-source checker axe-core 4.10.2 over the same two pages.
findings: The verdict was right both ways. The broken page came back 'Non-compliant' with 14 issues (10 critical, 3 serious, 1 moderate); the fixed twin came back 'Accessible'.

Of our 20 planted errors, the full report identified 7 correctly: the missing language, the empty title, the unlabelled button, the unlabelled iframe, aria-hidden on a link, the missing main landmark and the clickable div. An eighth, a link containing only an image without alt text, was flagged under the wrong diagnosis: the report called the image decorative and advised hiding it, which would leave the link with no name at all. axe-core found 13 of the same 20.

What it missed: the form had an email field and a dropdown without labels and a phone field labelled only by its placeholder, and the report's Forms category read 0. It also missed the image with no alt text, the alt text that was a filename, the low-contrast text, the skipped heading level, the table without header cells and the positive tabindex. For the filename alt text and the 'click here' link the report has a rule, but marked it 'Relevant: No'.

The report contradicts itself on the title: the empty <title> fails one rule ('titles aren't descriptive') and passes another ('missing page title'). It also flagged the correctly hidden icon inside our button and the page's <body> element.

The scan itself is free, but the breakdown sits blurred behind a form. To see it you give your name and a business email and tick: 'I agree to enter into a contract with accessiBe under its Terms of Service, under which accessiBe will process my personal data for marketing purposes, for 6 months'. The same page says 'Always free'. The report arrived by email within a minute, with buttons to sign up and to install the widget.
It would not scan W3C's own before-and-after accessibility demo ('The scanner doesn't have permission to access this URL'), which is why we used pages of our own.
not_tested: accessWidget itself, any paid tier, accessFlow, multi-page scans and real sites
One page pair is a spot check of the free scanner, not a verdict on the product line.

sessions.what: We did not stop at the marketing. On 25 September 2026 we opened a free Jibble account (organisation 'AIBM hands-on test', web browser only), clocked in and out, invited a second user, exported a timesheet and opened the upgrade screen without buying anything. Nothing was agreed with Jibble about this test. Everything below is what the product did and showed, not what the site says.
findings: The account lands on Free at €0, marked as the selected plan, with a 14-day trial of the paid features running alongside it. During those two weeks nothing is locked, so what you see in week one is more than Free keeps.

The price table exists, just not on the public site. The upgrade button opens four plans with annual and monthly prices (euros, excluding VAT, as shown from the Netherlands): Free €0; Essential €1.79 or €2.99; Growth €3.79 or €4.99; Pro €6.79 or €9.29 per user a month. No demo form and no sales call in between.

Jibble's own plan comparison, one click further, answers what Free excludes: no timesheet approval workflow, no automatic break deductions or custom pay periods, no smart reminders, alerts or automatic clock-out, no groups, one admin, two locations, one work schedule and one kiosk, and no attendance report, leave workflow or leave balances. Free keeps overtime calculations, face recognition, selfie, PIN and NFC clock-ins, GPS-verified clock-ins and geofences, timesheet and report exports, and the Slack, Microsoft Teams, QuickBooks Online, Xero, Deel and Zapier integrations.
Setting up the organisation requires a phone number; the form will not continue without one. The marketing opt-in on the sign-up form is ticked by default.
Clocking out in the same minute you clocked in is refused, with a message saying you cannot clock out before clocking in. Jibble records whole minutes; two minutes later it worked.
Inviting a second member took a name and an email address and went through without any prompt to pay. The member shows as pending until they accept.

The weekly timesheet export offers XLS or CSV. Our CSV arrived within seconds and carries 32 columns per member per day, including worked hours, paid and unpaid breaks, deductions, payroll hours, daily and weekly overtime and billable amounts.
We did not switch on face recognition or GPS. The comparison puts both in Free; anti-spoofing, device lock and live location tracking are Pro only.

sessions.what: Daan started the 30-day trial; everything after that was measured inside the account. The first question the protocol asked was whether the trial takes a card, because their pricing page does not say. It does not, but the answer is on the signup page, not the pricing page, which is a small lesson in where vendors put the reassuring sentence.
findings: No card for the trial. The signup page states it plainly — “Try it free for 30 days. No credit card required. Cancel anytime.” — and the form asks only for an email address and a password. The pricing page, where you would actually look, says nothing about it.

The prices inside the account are not the prices on the pricing page. The public page leads with the promotional rate, currently a limited-time 90% off for three months. The in-app upgrade screen quotes the real thing: Lite $23, Plus $43, Premium $70 a month, with a Yearly toggle marked “Save 10%”. Sign up on the strength of $2.30 and the first screen you see afterwards is $23.
Two add-ons ride along on every tier, and they are easy to miss: Team Members at $11 per user a month, and Advanced Payments at $20 a month. They are listed under Lite, Plus and Premium alike.

Removing FreshBooks branding from the emails your client receives is not a paid feature: it is a quote-only one. It appears only on the top “Let's Talk” tier, alongside lower card fees and two included team members. On Lite, Plus and Premium your invoice mail carries their brand.

The client ceiling that decides the tier is not testable during the trial. Lite stops at 5 clients, Plus at 50, Premium unlimited, but the trial runs with full features, as the upgrade screen says in as many words (“Upgrade to a paid plan to continue using all of FreshBooks' great features”). We fed the client importer a six-client CSV and it accepted the file and moved straight to field matching, with no limit warning at the point where a Lite account would have stopped. So the meter that will actually bite you is the one you cannot feel while you are evaluating.
Prices are shown in USD on a Netherlands account, and the plan screen carries the note “Features vary by region.”

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Gorgias on a Shopify development store: the install, a workspace made by the app on its own with no password or card, one macro with made up text saved in about 1.5 minutes and 5 steps, and the Billing page with a free trial from 17 to 24 November, Starter at $10 a month for 50 tickets and the AI Agent at $30 a month for 30 interactions. The app said Shopify billing was inactive, and Activate in Shopify led to an empty screen, so nothing was approved and the checkout was not tested. Nothing was sent, no channel was connected, and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the App Store listing (English) was opened and the install form was submitted at 18:33 in our own tab. The first screen was Connect your Gorgias account to Shopify, with the choices Create Your Account and Already have an account. Create Your Account led to the Shopify dialog Install app, which asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked. The app then showed Generating your Gorgias workspace and opened a workspace of the vendor on its own; the address of that workspace contains the name of our development store, so it is not shown. No password, card, phone number or form was asked: the account came from the Shopify identity. A banner said Your account is not verified. Please check your email.; no e-mail was sent or opened. The admin was in English. Core action, one macro (a saved reply): Settings, Macros, Create macro, the name Test: Snowboard shipping delay and the text Hi, thanks for your patience. Your snowboard is packed and leaves our test warehouse tomorrow. This is invented test text., then Create macro. It was done at about 18:34, about 1.5 minutes after the start and 5 steps after the form was opened. The macro appeared in the list with usage count 0; the list already held 12 example macros of the vendor. No mailbox, social channel or phone number was connected and no ticket or message was sent. The AI Agent was not tested. Plans in the app: Billing, Usage & Plans said Your free trial started on November 17, 2026 and will expire on November 24, 2026 (seven days). Helpdesk was Starter at $10/month with 0 of 50 tickets used; AI Agent was $30/month with 0 of 30 automated interactions used; Voice (from $30/month) and SMS (from $20/month) were inactive and locked. Together Starter and the AI Agent are $40 a month, as the dossier says. The Basic plan and above were not looked at in the app. Difference with the dossier (from the listing, not from the app): the listing names Basic at $60 a month or $600 a year, while the dossier gives Basic at $90 a month or $77 a month billed annually. This comes from the listing and is not a test result; Basic was not opened in the app. Checkout: NOT reached. A banner said Your Shopify billing is inactive, so your payments may not go through, and that after activation the Starter plan ($10/month), the AI Agent ($30/month) and Gaia would be billed through Shopify, excluding sales tax. The button Activate in Shopify first opened an extra tab (closed) and, in our own tab, led to the billing activation address of the vendor and stayed on an empty screen of the vendor. The Shopify screen Approve subscription was not reached, nothing was approved, no card was entered and nothing was paid; so the checkout was not tested and no total, tax or test charge text was seen. Cancelling: not tested as a separate step; the app was removed through Settings, Apps, Uninstall (reason: Testing multiple apps) at about 18:37 and Gorgias no longer appeared in the list. Not tested: the AI Agent, live chat, real tickets, Shopify order data in tickets, seats, Basic and higher plans, cancelling inside Gorgias, e-mail verification and the Shopify approval screen. Clean up: the app was uninstalled; the test macro stayed in the workspace of the vendor, which is no longer linked to the store; no plan was approved and no theme change was made; our own tabs were closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on Freshdesk, during the trial that starts with a new account (Freshdesk Omni, EU data centre), without connecting a channel, a mailbox or an integration: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We created three tickets with known priorities and statuses, changed one and added a private note.
findings: The sign-up page promised a '14-day all-access free trial'; inside the app the banner said 'your 15-day trial starts today', next to a 'Buy now' button. Our own company domain was accepted without a business-email check.

All three tickets (#4, #5 and #6) were created with a 'Ticket created' message, and in All tickets all nine values we set (subject, priority and status) were right. The open Low-priority ticket got a deadline straight away: 'First response due in 7 hours'.

Times were off by default: tickets created on the evening of 21 October, Amsterdam time, showed as 'Thu, 22 Oct 2026 at 3:24 AM'. The new account's time zone was not Amsterdam, despite the EU data centre. It can be changed; we did not check whether SLA deadlines move with it.

Onboarding asked for industry, experience, up to three goals and support channels, then offered 'Build your first AI Agent' from a website, with 'Skip for now'; we skipped it. The workspace already held three sample tickets with sample contacts.
The New ticket form sets Source to Phone and Product to 'Example' by default and requires a Description; a 'Create another' box lets you add tickets in a row.
Changing FD-BETA from High to Low in the list view stuck: the opened ticket showed Priority Low and Status Pending. The private note was marked orange, and no email went out.

'Add AI summary' on every ticket, 'Write with AI' in the note editor and the AI Agent builder were all on offer during the trial. We did not click them, and what remains of them after the trial is not established.

AI Agent, AI summary and Write with AI
What happens after the 15-day trial (a move to a free plan or a block)

findings: Onboarding took six screens with a progress bar. On the last one, 'Stay up to date by subscribing to our emails' was ticked in advance; we unticked it. No card and no sales call.

Starter shows $0 with 2 static pages, 1 GB bandwidth, 50 form submits and a CMS limit of 50 items. Basic is $15 a month and Premium $25, both with 'Billed yearly' switched on by default. The page says prices are in USD with applicable taxes added at checkout.
A CSV import into a new CMS collection recognised the header and let us map each column. The preview showed our amount as 12.1 and joined the two lines of the description into one.

Both records then failed with 'Import Failed: All items failed to import' and 'Validation Failure' on each row. The screen does not give the reason; it sits in a summary file we did not download. A multi-line text field may be the cause, but we did not establish that, and it may be a mapping mistake on our side.
Export code in the Designer says 'Available on paid Workspace plans'. That is separate from the CMS, which has its own CSV export button.
On Starter with a CMS collection, 'Upgrade to Basic' opens 'Delete CMS items to upgrade to Basic'. To keep the collection you have to take Premium. We did not go further.
not_tested: Everything the kit checks after an import: both records failed, so export, special characters and round trip are untested, not failed
Checkout, tax and the final price: we never reached a payment screen
Support, team roles, API access and invitations
An actual downgrade or cancellation; we only read the dialog
The email verification link that the dashboard asks for was not used

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 28 October 2026 on the free Pro trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported three made-up tasks, set up one automation, asked the AI assistant one question, exported the board, imported it again with one change and opened the Pro checkout without entering a card.
findings: The account opened on a 14-day Pro trial without a card, after six onboarding screens. The first screen had 'allow automatic sign-ups with an @aibuildermarketplace.com email address' switched on by default.

The plans page started at 5 seats; the smallest choice was 3. For 3 seats Pro cost €19 per seat a month billed yearly or €24 monthly, and choosing monthly first opened a prompt to reconsider yearly billing.

The Pro checkout for 3 seats monthly added an AI add-on of €30 (3,000 credits) by itself, offset by a €30 discount 'only in the first year', plus €15.12 tax (21%): €87.12 a month. After the first year that add-on would cost extra if you keep it.

Our CSV import matched only the Status column automatically; task name and due date had to be mapped by hand. Start Date arrived as a text column. The status cells first showed colours without labels, but the labels appeared after reloading the board.

A 'when status changes to Done, move item to group' automation ran within seconds and used 1 of the 25,000 monthly actions on Pro. The Sidekick assistant correctly named the two tasks due on 29 October.
Re-importing with one changed description and 'Update' matched on task name: the description changed and no duplicates appeared, although the notice said '3 items imported'.

Invitations offer Admin, Member and a Viewer role described as 'view only, no edits (free)'. The 'downgrade to Free' link only said you can choose a plan when the trial ends. API tokens and an MCP server are offered in the developer centre.
not_tested: What the Free plan allows after the trial

sessions.what: On 13 November 2026 we tested Zendesk Suite Professional on its trial, using our own site as the knowledge source. We built a Billing group and a routing trigger with the admin copilot, saved one synthetic invoice ticket, and asked the AI agent a Dutch and an English question. We did not open checkout, and we did not test support, invitations, roles, API access, export or cancellation.
findings: Daan created the account the day before and we did not see that step. In the accelerated setup the website address came prefilled, and about 35 seconds later the AI agent had read our site. The setup asked for no card, no phone number and no mailbox connection. An optional banner offered an expert call.
The trial runs on Suite Professional with 12 of 14 days left when we looked. The trial therefore includes features that the entry plan Support Team does not.

The admin copilot created the Billing group on the first approval. The routing trigger took three approvals: the copilot first used the field subject, which Zendesk rejected, then title, then subject_includes_word. The whole job took about 1.5 minutes.

We then saved a synthetic ticket titled 'Vraag over mijn factuur van oktober' as an internal note, with no public reply. The assignee field showed Billing (Ticket #3). Only this Dutch 'factuur' branch was tested. We did not test the 'invoice' branch or reporting per department.
The plan page lists the admin copilot under Suite Professional. We did not test the same trigger on Suite Team, where it would be set up by hand.

The AI agent runs in Dutch because the account language is Dutch. Our English question was refused with 'Ik spreek uw taal niet'. A Dutch question about whether we test software ourselves got an answer in about 10 seconds that matches our site: some reviews are tested hands-on and dated, others are supplier-research reviews. This is one answer, not an accuracy benchmark.

The plan page in the trial shows, per agent per month in euros: Support Team 19 billed annually or 25 monthly, Suite Team 55 or 69, and Suite Professional 115 or 149. The annual option is labelled 24% off. Copilot is a separate add-on at 50 euros per agent per month. A recommendation popup suggested Suite Team and also listed Suite Growth, which the full comparison did not.
We opened no checkout, so tax, totals, minimums and renewal terms are unknown. These euro prices are not directly comparable with the dollar price read on the US page on 7 October 2026.

Support, invitations, roles and API access

The same routing on Suite Team without the copilot
