sessions.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 15 November 2026 the session tested EasyDMARC on the platform trial: adding our own domain, the first result, the verification route, the price of the plans and the checkout up to the card form. No DNS was changed and nothing was paid. Add Domain first offers Discovered Domains, which asks to connect providers such as Mailgun, Amazon SES, SendGrid, HubSpot, Klaviyo and HighLevel; we chose Add Manually. Our domain was added as type Sending (the other choice is Parked) at about 17:28. The step Verify Domain Manually followed: EasyDMARC recognised Hostinger as the DNS provider and says to delete the current DMARC record of type TXT at host _dmarc and then to add a new CNAME record with a value under easydmarc.pro. So verifying means removing your own DMARC record and letting EasyDMARC host DMARC through a CNAME (managed DMARC); stopping later means putting your own record back, which is derived from the steps and not tested. We chose Later: a DNS change needs a separate approval from the account owner, so no DNS was changed and the domain stays unverified. The domain list showed Policy None, Total Volume 0 and a warning triangle. A domain overview was available within a minute and was viewed at 17:29: Infrastructure Health Score, Total Score 32, with Domain Health 80/100, Authentication 40/100, Sender Insights 0/100 and Threat Intelligence 0/100. Authentication showed DMARC Policy None, DMARC Record Valid, SPF Valid (3/10 lookups) and DKIM No Record with Selectors N/A; DMARC Compliance Rate was 0%. Blocklist was Inactive with Monitoring off and Google Postmaster had No data. Our own dig check at 17:29 showed that the _dmarc TXT record is v=DMARC1; p=none, so the policy None is right, and that the SPF record includes the Hostinger mail servers, which is right. The DKIM selector hostingermail-a is a CNAME to the DKIM host of the mail provider with a valid RSA key. So our domain does have DKIM, and EasyDMARC reported No Record, presumably because it does not know the selector until reports arrive, which only happens after the CNAME verification. Pending Actions showed 1 Critical, Verify your domain to unlock full visibility; without verification no DMARC reports arrive. No kit records were entered.
findings: Our own domain was added on the platform trial at about 17:28 and a domain overview was available within a minute: Infrastructure Health Score 32, with Domain Health 80/100, Authentication 40/100, Sender Insights 0/100 and Threat Intelligence 0/100.

EasyDMARC read our DMARC policy (none) and SPF (valid, 3 of 10 lookups) correctly, as our own dig check confirmed. It showed DKIM as No Record, although our domain publishes a valid DKIM key for the selector hostingermail-a. The tool does not know the selector until reports arrive.

Verifying the domain means deleting your own DMARC TXT record at _dmarc and adding a CNAME to an easydmarc.pro host, so EasyDMARC hosts DMARC for you. Putting the old record back after leaving is derived from the steps and not tested. We chose Later, so no DNS was changed and the domain stays unverified.
Without verification no DMARC reports arrive. Pending Actions showed 1 Critical, Verify your domain to unlock full visibility.

There is no free plan in the app: the trial is 14 days without a card, then you pick a paid plan. Yearly billing showed DMARC Plus at 35.99 euros a month (44.99 crossed out) for 2 domains and 3 months of history, and Premium at 71.99 euros. Monthly billing showed Plus at 44.99 euros.
Checkout asks for card number, expiry date and CVV before it shows a purchase summary. We stopped there and entered nothing.
not_tested: We did not watch the original sign-up; the account was already open when our session began.
We did not finish the CNAME verification, so no real DMARC reports arrived. Email provider connections, AI Agents, DNS Manager, Sender Insights, Threat Intelligence, the API and MCP stayed closed.
We did not contact support, invite anyone, enter card details, or export and re-import data.
Account deletion, and putting an old DMARC record back after leaving, were not tried.
We did not examine roles, API entitlement or a downgrade.

sessions.what: We already knew from their pricing pages that Glide sells two products. What we had never done is the thing a reader does: go to glideapps.com and press the free signup button. Daan created the account; everything after that was measured in the product.
findings: The free signup button does not lead to the product our pricing section describes. Both “Sign up” and “Get started” on glideapps.com point at os.glideapps.dev: GlideOS. We signed up and landed there. The classic builder, with the free tier of unlimited drafts, one editor and 25k rows, sits behind glideapps.com/classic, which you only reach if you already know to look for it.

The two ladders are an order of magnitude apart. Classic business pricing starts at $199 a month billed yearly; GlideOS Basic is $25 a month. Same brand, same homepage, two different products with two different price floors.

And the meter is different. Classic bills updates: 5,000 included, 2 cents each after that. GlideOS bills credits: Basic 100 a month, Plus 250, Pro 500 and upward with team size. So the “updates, not seats” warning that applies to Classic does not describe the product a new signup actually lands in.

GlideOS's free tier publishes no number. Every paid tier lists its credit allowance; the free column says “Limited credits”, alongside 2 team members and 10 projects. Nowhere in the app is there a balance, not on the dashboard, not in the account menu, not on the upgrade screen. You cannot find out what you have or what you have spent.

The AI itself is not walled off on free. From one sentence — “build a simple app to track software subscriptions” — it drew up a plan, asked a sensible clarifying question about where the data lives today, produced a working mockup and then began importing components one by one. We hit no credit wall during any of it.

sessions.what: The free plan, on a test landing page of our own with PagePulse's tracking script pasted before </body>, as its setup screen instructs. We then sent scripted visits whose every detail we logged: 10 visitors in 11 sessions (one came back in a new tab), 4 arriving from google.com, 3 from x.com and the rest direct, 3 on a phone-sized screen, 6 clicks on 'Start free trial', 3 clicks on 'Book a demo' that led to a second page, and visits of 35, 20 or 5 seconds. A second, smaller run of 3 visitors with one click each followed later, with every message the script sent logged. We compared the dashboard with what we had done.
findings: The counts were right. Visitors 10 and page views 14 matched exactly, as did the source split (Google 4, X 3, direct 4 of 14 views) and the device split (3 mobile, 7 desktop). In the second run every number moved by exactly what we sent: visitors 10 to 13, page views 14 to 17, 'Start free trial' clicks up by exactly 3.
Clicks on links and buttons are captured without extra setup and named by their text ('Start free trial', 'Book a demo'). The script itself sent one event per click.

Engagement does not follow its own definition. The tooltip defines an engaged session as one lasting 10+ seconds, with 2+ page views, or a conversion. By that rule 8 of our first 11 sessions qualify, as they lasted 20 to 35 seconds. The dashboard showed 27%: exactly the 3 sessions with two page views. The 20-second sessions of the second run did not count either.
A click from our page to our own thank-you page shows up as a traffic source, listed as the site's own domain at 21% next to Google and X.

The 'Here's what we found' analysis was general copywriting advice drawn from the page text (move the call to action, add testimonials), not from the visit data, and it sat under the line 'Once your tracking is set up', while tracking demonstrably worked.

The free script records page views, clicks, time on page through a ping every 15 seconds, and load times. It does not record scroll depth, and conversions need your own trackConversion call, which the dashboard says is part of Starter and above.
not_tested: heatmaps and conversion tracking (paid plans), traffic beyond a few dozen events, and real visitors

sessions.what: A fresh WordPress 7.1.2 test site, the Clonable plugin from the WordPress directory and a new free Clonable account. We cloned the site into German, wrote and then changed a page of our own, corrected a translation by hand and connected the plugin, checking each result on the live pages and in WordPress. This test is also our entry in Clonable's review content campaign on Reditus, which offers a one-off €30 if Clonable approves it. We used the public free plan and Clonable did not see the article before publication.
findings: From typing the site address to a working German preview took under five minutes, about two of them waiting for the build. No DNS change or plugin is needed for the preview.
We changed a price on the English page from 49 to 59 euros; the German page showed the new price on our first reload, within fifteen seconds.

WordPress still listed the same three English pages afterwards. Clonable added no translated copies to the database; the only addition was its plugin. The other side of that: all clone traffic runs through Clonable's servers, which its own setup guide tells you to whitelist.

Connecting the plugin with an API key put hreflang tags for x-default, en-us and de-de in the head of both the original and the clone straight away. The URL slug stayed English; URL translation is a separate feature.
Correcting a single translation in the Clone editor works on the free plan. Translation Replacements and the Glossary, the tools for fixing a term everywhere at once, ask for an upgrade.
The plan picker inside the app showed one clone on every plan and 25 free pages, while the public pricing page the same day listed 3 to 20 clones per plan and 20 free pages.

findings: The poll went live with an empty option. The third answer we had typed was not saved, and nothing warned us: the live poll showed an option with only the placeholder 'Fill in an answer'.
A three-page PDF went through 'Processing', 'Converting to images' and 'Putting everything together' and became three slides, in the right order, in about 35 seconds.

Onboarding created three sample webinars on its own (a live one scheduled for the same evening, an automated one and an on-demand one, all marked 'Sample'). The account opened in Dutch, and switching to English took two separate settings: the language menu in the studio and Account > Settings > Language.

New webinar offers Start from scratch, Generate (AI), Copy or Add to series; Present live, Automated or On-demand; and Public, Unlisted or Private access. 'Offer replay' is on by default, and 'Create and customize' does not publish yet. The title field ignored the first title we typed.

Polls sit under Interactions, next to Call to action, Quiz and Information: single or multiple choice, with a default duration of 1:30, and at the start you choose 'End manually' or 'End after a set time'.

The studio did not open until we allowed browser notifications and then camera and microphone. In the dry run it said 'Only team members and invited test viewers can join' and 'Dry runs aren't recorded and don't collect statistics'. Slides changed straight away with the arrow keys, and ending the dry run reset all interactions.
The viewer link of the unpublished webinar returned 'Not yet published: Publish your webinar first before you can use the registration page.', so a test viewer can only watch after you publish.

sessions.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 15 November 2026 the session tested UptimeRobot on the free plan: how fast a free monitor alerts on a failing page, the limits of the free plan, the price of the cheapest paid plan up to the card form, and the way to delete the account. Nothing was paid and nothing was deleted. A new HTTP monitor was created for a page on our own site that returns 404 (checked with curl). It was created at 17:16:38. At 17:17:36 the dashboard still said Preparing and showed 100% for the last 24 hours with 0 incidents. The DOWN email, Monitor is DOWN for that page, arrived at 17:17:45, about 67 seconds after the monitor was created, although the free interval is 5 minutes. At 17:23:30 the dashboard said Down, currently down for 0h 5m 56s, with 1 incident and 16.6% uptime over 24 hours. The test monitor was paused afterwards and not deleted. The monitor for our own site, created in the onboarding, keeps running. No kit records were entered.

At 17:23:30 the dashboard said Down, currently down for 5 minutes and 56 seconds, with 1 incident and 16.6% uptime over 24 hours.

The free plan allows 50 monitors checked every 5 minutes, with email alerts and 1 status page. Keyword, heartbeat and API monitors, groups, 1-minute checks and several locations are paid. SSL certificate and domain checks are only in Solo, Team and Scale.

The cheapest paid plan has fewer monitors than the free plan. At checkout Solo 10 was 108 euros a year for 10 monitors, or 228 euros a year for 50 monitors. The summary said this is an auto-renewal payment. We stopped before the card details.
The pricing page lists 3 months of data and monthly email reports for the first 3 months only on Free. We read this and did not test it over time.
Deleting the account runs through Account details: UptimeRobot sends a verification email, after which all account information, monitors, logs and settings are lost and cannot be recovered.
not_tested: We did not watch the original sign-up; the account was already open when our session began.
Paid monitor types, SMS and voice alerts, a published status page, integrations, the API and MCP, and the mobile app were out of scope.
We did not contact support, invite anyone, enter card details, or export and re-import data.
The irreversible account deletion is left to the account owner.
We did not examine roles, API entitlement or a downgrade.

sessions.what: We set up a Netherlands-only Geo Redirect and a Geo Link on Geo Targetly's 14-day trial on 13 November 2026, opened the Geo Link from the Netherlands and read the plan screens. Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We placed no script on a real site, so the redirect rule itself never ran. We did not test checkout, support, export or cancellation.
findings: The trial needs no card. The subscription screen read '$0/mo on your free trial' with Payment Method None, and the account showed 13 days left. We joined an existing trial account, so we did not see the sign-up screens. A welcome window offered Start Setup and Skip for now, and a Book Free Setup Call is optional.

Geo Redirect saved without any code: from the fictional https://www.example.com to https://www.example.com/nl/ when the country equals Netherlands, redirecting visitors automatically. Step two wants a single script pasted just below the opening head tag. It offers install tabs for 14 platforms, among them Google Tag Manager, WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Squarespace and Webflow.

The URL fields add https:// themselves. Pasting a full address gave https://https://www.example.com, and we needed two corrections. Redirect plus link took about 7 minutes with those corrections (our own approximate timing, not a benchmark).

A Geo Link needs no script. Netherlands went to https://example.org/ and All Other Locations to https://example.com/, with a short link on a shared gtly.link domain and a QR code. The page recommends your own domain because shared domains can go down when others abuse them.

Opening the short link from the Netherlands first showed an interstitial, 'You will be redirected in 3', with Geo Targetly branding, and then https://example.org/ loaded. A notice says the branding is in effect during the free trial. Geo Targetly's text says a subscription removes it; we did not buy one, so we did not see that.

Pageview counting comes from the vendor help page 'What are pageviews quota?', which we read and did not measure: every page view counts, including visitors who match no rule; bots do not count; a Geo Link counts only a click; and multiple products on one page count as multiple pageviews, because each instance of the tracking script consumes one.

The in-app plan screen is in euros. Monthly: Dev 14, Startup 29, Growth 59, with 1,000, 20,000 and 100,000 pageviews a month. Yearly, shown per month: 11, 23 and 47 with 12,000, 240,000 and 1,200,000 pageviews a year, or 132, 276 and 564 in total. Yearly billing was preselected, under the banner 'SAVE 20% ON YEARLY BILLING'.
The Startup and Growth cards list 'Access to all features' and the Dev card does not. We did not check which features Dev lacks, so we cannot confirm that higher plans only add pageviews.
The dashboard holds a hidden notice for an exceeded quota ('Upgrade or re-subscribe'). We did not trigger it, so we do not know what happens to live redirects at the limit.

findings: The account opened with 100 of 100 credits and no card request, matching the '100 free verification credits' claim.
We uploaded a two-row CSV of example.com addresses at 15:00 UTC. The tool found the e-mail column itself ('2 Email addresses to be verified').

The verification window showed Standard at 1 credit per address and Deep Scan Recovery at 3 credits per address, 'Total cost 2 - 6 CR'. Deep Scan was switched on by default and adds up to 30 minutes after Standard. The page says credits are refunded for addresses it cannot resolve.

The list finished in about a minute and cost 2 credits (98 of 100 left). Deep Scan charged nothing because Standard resolved both addresses. Both came back Invalid MX, which is correct because example.com has no mail server.
Email Finder charges 5 credits when a first or last name is given and 10 credits when only a domain is given, from the same balance. We did not run a lookup with that feature.

The pricing page preselects pay as you go: 10,000 credits for EUR 27 (EUR 0.0027 per address) and 50,000 for EUR 98 (EUR 0.0020). A monthly plan for 50,000 is EUR 89 a month. The switch 'Automatically buy the same package when your credits run low' was on by default.
The page states prices exclude VAT, with tax calculated at checkout. We did not go past it.

sessions.what: Two sessions on the free plan. On 7 September we ran it by hand: Daan logged in, and we read every counter against a test file of exactly five minutes that we built inside the page; Descript was not a partner of ours then and contributed nothing. On 30 September, by then a PartnerStack partner, we drove Descript from Claude through Descript's connector, for Descript's partner content challenge, which pays the first five entries $250: we uploaded one of our own five-minute review videos and asked for vertical clips in plain sentences, once directly and once from a claude.ai chat.
findings: The free plan's 100 AI credits are one-time, not monthly. Descript says so itself in two places: the plan card reads "100 AI credits at signup" for Free against "400 AI credits / month" for Hobbyist, and the usage screen inside the app puts "Lifetime AI credits used 0/100" next to "Monthly media minutes used 0/60". That pair of words -- lifetime against monthly -- is the whole answer.

Media minutes come off at IMPORT, not at export, and per minute of media. Two five-minute files took the counter from 60m to 50m. Their own upload dialog says it too: "Each file added uses media minutes". Exporting costs no minutes and no credits, according to Descript itself.

The AI assistant, Underlord, charges per instruction, and it does run on the free plan. Importing and transcribing cost 3 credits, Studio Sound over a ten-minute track 9 credits, and a question about the export settings 6 credits.

An instruction that returns nothing still costs credits. "Remove all filler words" answered "No filler words were found -- the script shows 0 words, so there's nothing to remove" and deducted 2 credits anyway.
Five instructions without a single real edit spent 20 of the 100 one-time credits. Anyone using the free plan as a trial is through it in an afternoon, and no more arrive.

Studio Sound ran on Free, while the pricing table presents it as a Hobbyist benefit ("Studio Sound, Remove Filler Words, Create Clips, and more"). The line "Limited use of Underlord" on the free card is therefore more generous than the comparison table suggests.
In onboarding, the consent "Our team analyzes your project information" is TICKED BY DEFAULT, in a step most people click straight through. You can turn it off, but you have to do it yourself.
The watermark on the free plan sits in the bottom right of the frame; paid plans do not have it.

Through Claude's Descript connector, a 5:15 review video of ours (94 MB) uploaded and transcribed in about 30 seconds. The import used 315 media seconds, consistent with minutes being charged at import.

One sentence to Underlord through Claude (a vertical 9:16 clip of about 30 seconds on the price and the 90-day data limit, with captions, keeping the words and numbers as spoken) produced a new 24-second vertical composition in two and a half minutes for 48.3 AI credits. The original composition was left untouched, and the clip's transcript matched the source word for word, numbers included.

From a claude.ai chat, Claude asked permission before each Descript action, read the transcript itself, chose the passage from 01:15 to 01:40 and had Underlord cut a 21-second vertical clip with burned-in captions in about three minutes. It also fixed the transcript's misspelling of the product name in the captions and said that it had.

The vertical version is a centre crop. On our 16:9 video it cut off the text card at the side of the frame, and because our video already carries subtitles, Descript's captions landed on top of them. Ask for the full frame on a blurred background, and skip added captions when your source already has them.

Our request to fix that was refused because the free plan had run out of AI credits: the one-time 100 were gone after our first session plus these two edits. Real editing work through Claude needs a paid plan.

Publishing gave an unlisted share link and an MP4 download in about a minute and a half. We asked for 1080p and received 720x1280 with the watermark in the bottom right, so the 720p cap on the Free plan card is what applies, not the 4K that Descript's own assistant named in our first session.

Setting the brand colour to #663399 with the colour picker recoloured our own chat bubbles at once. In Dark the brand colour stayed; the primary and secondary text colours switched automatically (#FFFFFF and #989898, against #141414 and #727272 in Light).

Chat Features has about 20 switches (among them typing indicator, photo, video, audio and files, editing, deleting, delivery and read receipts, presence, threads, quoted replies, pin, AI user copilot and moderation). With read receipts off, the double ticks disappeared from the bubbles and the conversation list, and came back when switched on. The typing indicator cannot be checked in a static preview.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 on the Free plan, with no card, no top-up and nothing published: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We had MindStudio's built-in Architect build an agent that pulls record IDs and dates out of four made-up records (one without a date) and tried to run it. The run failed for lack of credit, so the extraction itself was not tested.
findings: The Free plan in the app lists 'One Agent' and '1,000 runs / month', but model usage is paid from a separate prepaid balance that starts at $0.00 on a new workspace (shown in red, 'Click to top up'). Topping up opens a card form with $10, $25, $100 and $500; we did not fill it in.

Our first run of our own agent, in the debugger, stopped while waiting for the model with 'You are out of usage credits' and 'Run Failed: insufficient_credits/balance'. There was no output, so we cannot say how well it extracts dates or whether it marks the record without a date as unknown.

'Generate Agent' started the built-in MindStudio Architect, which first asked three clarifying questions (date format, output format, several dates per record), then showed a readable plan with the rule to never infer, guess or fabricate dates, and built the agent in about one and a half minutes after 'Build'. The Architect's own debug log listed billing events of about $0.88 over ten steps, while our workspace balance stayed at $0.00. We were not shown a charge for this work.

The debugger logs every step with timings, the resolved variables, the full prompt sent and the model used (Claude 5.5 Sonnet at 0.5°); the error and its reason appear verbatim. The Architect added a second agent next to the empty first one, although Free names 'One Agent'; both were drafts.

Onboarding offered two ways to connect AI models: the recommended Service Router ('Charged only when agents run', at provider rates without markup) or your own API keys. We chose the Service Router and did not try our own keys.

We found no export or download option for an agent in the editor. The debugger shows 'Open Script' for the workflow and the Architect run has 'Copy for LLM', which copies the conversation; we did not test these further.

findings: The sidebar showed '10 / 10 Pro messages left'. One question used one Pro message and the counter read 9 / 10.

Question: 'Does regular physical activity reduce the risk of depression in adults?' The answer said yes, with a 17% to 25% lower risk. The Consensus Meter, based on 19 papers, showed Yes 100%. A note says it 'may not be a perfect reflection of the current science'.

The upgrade screen preselects Annual. Pro is $12 a month billed yearly ($144) or $20 monthly. The Free column says 'without any AI analysis' and lists 10 Pro messages a month in the same column.
Monthly Pro checkout read EUR 18.61 for the Netherlands, with annual billing offered at EUR 133.98 a year. No VAT line showed before card entry.

sessions.what: We trained one monitored robot on Browse AI's Free plan on 13 November 2026, using its AI-assisted Table Studio on a public practice shop, books.toscrape.com, category Travel. The account is Daan's, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We joined an existing Free account, so we did not see sign-up. We did not test export, integrations, support, checkout or cancellation.
findings: The start screen offered 'Extract structured data' or 'Monitor for changes'. We chose monitoring. Three training methods followed: Table Studio (AI training, labelled Beta), Robot Studio (point and click) and a Chrome extension. We used Table Studio and installed nothing. No card was requested.

Table Studio trained itself and returned a table called Books List after about 35 seconds (our approximate timing, not a benchmark): 11 rows with position, title, price, availability, rating, URL and cover image. We checked the result against the live page with curl. All 11 prices matched, and the category holds exactly 11 books.

Save Robot asked how often to check for changes: hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. We chose daily and switched email alerts on data changes off. The robot saved and fetched fresh data from the live page. The Monitor tab then read 'Every day, No changes'.

Training the robot was free. The first run, 11 rows, cost 1.10 credits in the task history. That fits the pricing line of 1 credit per task with 10 list items included plus 0.10 per extra item. At one run a day this list would use about 33 credits a month (our own arithmetic), inside the free allowance.
The billing page showed 60 monthly credits on Free, for 2 websites, with 58.90 available after the first run. Our dossier had said 50, so we corrected it to what the app shows.

The plan cards offered yearly billing with 20% off and all credits paid upfront: Personal $19 a month, Professional $69 a month, Premium from $500 a month. We did not see monthly prices and opened no checkout, so tax, renewal terms and the payable total are unknown.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 28 October 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We logged three time entries with known durations, set a billable rate, exported the reports, tried to import one export again and opened the upgrade without paying.
findings: Signing up at track.toggl.com put us in the new Toggl Focus app. After three onboarding screens a dialog said 'The whole product is unlocked for 31 days' and 'No credit card needed'; the pricing page we read on 25 October says a 30-day trial. Our three entries (a 2m 18s timer, 15:00 and 1:30 by hand) added up to exactly 18m 48s in the report breakdown. The summary tiles rounded that to 19m, while the day header in the timer list showed 18m.

A project with a $60 hourly rate turned the 15-minute entry into $15.00 and 79.79% billable, both correct. Billable rates are one of eight features the project view labels as unlocked by the Premium trial.

Importing our own Time logs export again did not work as is: the importer asked for a duration column, could not use the combined start-and-stop column, and read the export's '-' placeholders as names, so all three entries would have been skipped. We stopped before importing; there is no ID column to update by.

Monthly prices in the app were $12 for Starter and $24 for Premium per license ($9 and $16 a month billed yearly). Choosing Premium warned that 'your current trial will finish immediately', so we stopped there. sessions.what: We ran the import ourselves instead of summarising Capsule's help pages. Daan created the account; everything after that was measured in the product. We built a deliberately messy CSV: 24 rows, one row repeated with a different job title and phone number, and one row carrying nothing but an organisation name: imported it with “Import and update duplicates” and the overwrite box ticked, and then tried to undo it. The account was a fresh one on the 14-day premium trial, so nothing below is a free-plan restriction.
findings: 24 rows became 34 contacts. Capsule creates a separate Organisation record for every distinct organisation name in the file: 22 people plus 12 organisations. Nobody warns you, and it matters: the free plan stops at 250 contacts, so a 24-row spreadsheet costs 34 of them.
A row with only the Organisation column filled does build a company record on its own. Our “Solitary Holdings BV” row arrived as an organisation with its phone number attached.

The duplicate row wins. Anna Bakker went in twice, second time as “Head of Marketing” instead of “Marketing Lead”, and the record ended up with the later title. So the last occurrence in the file overwrites the earlier one, inside a single import.

But “overwrite” means exactly the four fields it names (name, job title, organisation and custom fields) and nothing else. The two rows carried different phone numbers and the contact now holds BOTH, sitting side by side. Contact channels are appended, not replaced, so a bad update pass leaves duplicate numbers on the record rather than wrong ones.

We could not find an undo or bulk-delete action in the screens we checked during this trial. The import history logs '34 total imported, 34 contacts created' and offers View and Close; View opens a saved filter with those 34 contacts, whose bulk actions were Tag, Create Campaign and Export. We found no delete on that list, on the full contact list, on the contact record or on its edit screen.
We did not establish that Capsule has no recovery route. Test a small import first and check the available rollback options before updating real contacts.

sessions.what: A 14-day trial of Freshservice for Business Teams on the Pro plan, set up for an HR team. Note the variant: this is Freshworks' service desk for HR, finance and facilities, priced separately from the IT edition whose plans this review lists. We sent six HR requests by email to the desk's default address: a missing payslip, a parental-leave request with a date, 'URGENT: my salary was not paid today' (rent due tomorrow), a request to change the bank account for salary payments, a remote-work policy question, and the payslip email a second time as a duplicate. We changed no default setting first, so this is what a team gets on day one.
findings: Email-to-ticket worked: all six emails became tickets (CASE-1 to CASE-6) within seconds, and the sender got a 'Ticket Received' confirmation for each within the same minute.

Every ticket came in at priority Low with the same deadlines: first response by 13 October, five days and seven hours after we wrote, and resolution by 20 October. That includes the unpaid-salary email, which the subject line itself marked URGENT. Out of the box nothing reads urgency from the text; you have to build rules for it.

Freddy AI Copilot, available in the Pro trial, summarised the urgent ticket correctly in two lines and named the urgency ('an urgent need as his rent is due tomorrow'). The summary did not change the priority or the deadline: the AI saw what the triage did not act on.
The duplicate was not caught. The second identical payslip email opened its own ticket, and its Related tickets tab read 'No related tickets yet'.
The bank-account change, a request payroll teams treat as a fraud risk, was handled like any other ticket: same priority, no verification step, no flag.
not_tested: the IT edition, the paid plans after the trial, the employee portal, approvals, automation rules we could have written ourselves, and replies sent from the desk

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Atlas AI Store Builder on a Shopify development store: the install with no payment screen, one AI product page for Demo Mug made in about 1.5 minutes and 9 clicks and saved as a draft, with invented placeholder social proof in the preview (10,000+ and 438 people purchased) and a sample review, then Upgrade to generate and Upgrade to publish everywhere. The Subscription page showed the $39 plan with a 7-day trial and the limits as the dossier says, and a dialog with the usage rates; Start 7-day free trial kept spinning and led to a login page of the vendor, so the Shopify approval screen was not reached and nothing was approved. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the App Store listing (English) was used and the install form was submitted in our own tab at 18:41; the Shopify dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked. There was no plan choice and no payment screen at the install. The app opened directly on Create with Atlas AI with three choices (Store, Product pages, Landing pages); the sidebar of the app had Your Pages, Bundle Deals, Cart Upsells and Subscription. No password, card, phone number or sign-up form of the vendor was asked. The admin was in English. Core action, one AI product page for the product Demo Mug: Product pages, Demo Mug ticked (1 product selected), Continue setup, the template Atlas Default (Universal) (Used by 174,553 stores), Continue setup, Upload research (Optional) skipped, Continue setup, then Researching your product... and Writing your page.... The result stood there at 18:43, about 1 minute 30 seconds after the install and 9 clicks. The editor showed the page of Demo Mug with $9.50, four labels, 10,000+ next to the stars, the line Sarah and 438 people purchased, a sample review card that says This is a sample review, please input your genuine customer review and 25 in stock. The store had no such numbers: they are invented placeholder social proof in the preview, recorded here as an observation. The buttons were Save as draft and Upgrade to publish; Save as draft was clicked and nothing was published. After that every generate button on the home page of the app said Upgrade to generate (Full store, Product page and so on) and the setup guide said 1 out of 4 steps completed. Plans in the app: the Subscription page showed the Atlas base plan, $39 per month, All features included, only pay more as your business grows, with a button Start 7-day free trial. Included: published product and landing pages up to 10, bundle revenue up to $1,000, cart orders up to 250. The text says that if the usage is exceeded, the usage rates are charged. Usage rates (read in the app, they answer the open dossier question about them): published pages, Base up to 10 included, up to 15 +$10 a month, up to 25 +$20, up to 50 +$30, up to 75 +$40, up to 100 +$50, unlimited +$70; bundler, Base up to $1,000 included, up to $2,500 +$10, up to $5,000 +$20, up to $10,000 +$35, up to $20,000 +$65, up to $35,000 +$110, up to $50,000 +$150 and above $50,000 +$195 a month. The tab Cart drawer could not be read because the click was not processed. Difference with the dossier: the dossier says the rendered pricing page showed no per-feature prices on 9 October; the app shows the usage rates in a dialog, so that line is out of date for the app. The $39 plan, the 7-day trial and the limits (10 pages, $1,000, 250 orders) are as the dossier says. Checkout: NOT reached. Start 7-day free trial was clicked; the button kept spinning for more than 20 seconds and the Shopify screen Approve subscription did not appear. A next click (closing the rates dialog) sent the tab to the login page of the vendor (app.helloatlas.io/api/auth), which only said Enter your shop domain to log in or install this app.; nothing was entered. No test charge was seen, nothing was approved, no card was entered and nothing was paid. The app home was blank several times (about 30 seconds, directly by address and from the sidebar) and loaded after a detour. Cancelling: no plan was started, so a stop of the billing could not be tested. The uninstall route is Settings, Apps, the menu of Atlas, Uninstall; the dialog says that after uninstalling any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information; a reason for uninstalling is required before the button works. Not tested: publishing (it needs an upgrade), bundles, cart upsells, Store and Landing pages, the trial approval screen, the Cart drawer tab of the rates and whether billing stops after the uninstall. Clean up: before the uninstall no new page was found under Online Store, Pages (5 existing pages, none from Atlas) and no new theme was found (the live theme and two drafts were older); the draft stays in the app, not in Shopify; the app embeds in the theme were not checked. Atlas was uninstalled after the test in our own tab and our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.
findings: Text we checked: "Published product and landing pages Up to 10". What we saw: The Subscription page showed the Atlas base plan at $39 per month with a button Start 7-day free trial and the limits up to 10 published pages, up to $1,000 of bundle revenue and up to 250 cart orders, as the dossier says; the trial itself was not started.

Text we checked: "If you exceed your plan usage, you are charged based on this usage rates". On 17 November 2026 the session tested HelpCenter on a Shopify development store: the install, an onboarding, the Free plan with 10 tickets and a FAQ limit of 5 articles, and two FAQ questions saved in the app. We did not see the FAQ page in the web shop: the checklist item and the preview did not open anything, and the theme editor has embeds only for a contact form, live chat, tabs and a widget. The plan page showed Standard $40, Advanced $70 and Enterprise $120 a month (500, 1000 and 2000 tickets) and, on the yearly view, $33.33, $58.33 and $100 a month, without a price per extra ticket. No paid plan was started, so nothing was approved, and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at 18:49; the Shopify dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked at about 18:50 and the app was open at about 18:51. In the admin the app is called SB: FAQ | HelpCenter (Shark Byte, Inc). The onboarding was Thank you for installing Helpcenter!, Continue, Unlock AI Content Generation and Later. No password, card, phone number or sign-up form of the vendor was asked. The admin was in English. Plan choice: Free was chosen with Get started at about 18:52, free and with no card. The Helpdesk tab said My plan: Free, Tickets: 10, Monthly ticket limit 0/10 (0%) and Top-ups are only available on paid plans, and asked to Create account for the helpdesk (not done). The FAQ Page tab said My plan: Free and FAQ: Up to 5 articles; the template Minimalistic was already Active, and the example categories Orders (Tracking, Shipping) and Exchange & Returns were there, switched off. Core action, a FAQ page with two test questions: the articles How long does shipping take? and What is your return policy? were made in Orders, Tracking, with the message Article saved! (about 18:57 and 18:59). Each article took 3 steps (the question, the answer in the text editor, Save); the slug field filled itself. New articles were switched on by default and the example article How to track my order? stayed off. In all 3 articles of the 5 allowed on Free were in the app. From the install click (about 18:50) to the second saved question (about 18:59) it took about 9 minutes, including the onboarding and the plan choice. The FAQ page in the web shop was NOT seen: the checklist item Add FAQ page to your store did not react to a click; Preview in Customize FAQ template opened nothing in our tab; in the theme editor, App embeds, HelpCenter has only Contact form, Live Chat, Tabs and Widget (all off) and no embed for a FAQ page. The Widget was switched on in the preview, showed no visible result on the home page, and was switched off again; the editor was left with Leave page and nothing was saved. So the two questions were saved in the app (yes), but that they show in the web shop is not proven, and no route to the FAQ page was found without a theme change. Plans in the app, monthly view: Standard $40/month (14-Day Free Trial; Knowledge Base 100 Articles; FAQ translations up to 5; AI-generated FAQs; unlimited seats; CRM with 500 tickets/mo), Advanced $70/month (14-Day Free Trial; All from Standard; unlimited articles and translations; premium templates; CRM with 1000 tickets/mo) and Enterprise $120/month (All from Advanced; prioritized support; performance report; CRM with 2000 tickets/mo); under them the Free plan: No AI integrations, Limited FAQ articles, Default FAQ designs, Knowledge Base: Up to 10 Articles. Annual view (Annual (save 2 months)): Standard $33.33/month, Advanced $58.33/month and Enterprise $100/month, with CRM 6000 tickets/yr, 12000 and 24000. Difference with the listing and the dossier: the listing says save 17% and names the price per extra ticket ($0.25, $0.15, $0.12); the app did not show a price per extra ticket on the plan cards. The plan prices and ticket limits in the app are the same as in the dossier; the Free plan limit of FAQ: Up to 5 articles was seen in the app. Checkout: NOT reached. Only the Free plan was chosen; no paid plan was started, so no Shopify approval screen, no trial and no test charge was seen. Cancelling: no plan was paid, so nothing could be cancelled. The uninstall route is Settings, Apps, the menu of the app, Uninstall; the dialog says a request will be sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information, and a reason for uninstalling is required (Testing multiple apps). Not tested: paid plans, the trial, the Helpdesk account (Create account), live chat, the e-mail channel, Messenger, AI generation, translations, Product Tabs, Contact Form and the FAQ page in the web shop. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 19:03 with the message that it was uninstalled; nothing was saved or left in the live theme (the Widget switch was not saved); our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested the start of Attribuly on a Shopify development store: the install, a welcome survey and then four screen steps to a wall. The first screen offered only Klaviyo, MambaSMS, Omnisend and CartSee, with Book a Demo for stores on another e-mail platform; the onboarding asked to connect a Klaviyo account and its Continue button stayed greyed out; the link for an attribution-only set-up did nothing when clicked twice. So the first result was not reached, no plan or checkout screen was seen, and the prices come from the listing and not from a test. The uninstall dialog was seen and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 19:00; the Shopify dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked at about 19:01. The app went through a page of the vendor (Verifying your session authorization) and was open at about 19:02. Welcome to Attribuly asked how we first heard about it (Shopify App Store was chosen) and had a required field about what we searched for; a popup about a new attribution template was closed. No password, card or phone number was asked. The admin was in English. Core action, set up abandoned-cart recovery or attribution: NOT reached. At about 19:04 the screen Choose your ESP offered Klaviyo (Selected), MambaSMS, Omnisend and CartSee, with the line Not using above ESPs or want to identify anonymous visitors? Book a Demo and the line Only want to use Attribution? Click here to set up. The link Click here to set up was clicked twice and did nothing visible (no new page and no new tab). Start email recovery led to the onboarding Find the shoppers Klaviyo can't see, with four steps (Connect Klaviyo, Select events, Enable App embed, Activate Klaviyo flow) and the text Connect your Klaviyo account to start recovering missed revenue; the button Continue stayed greyed out as long as no Klaviyo account was connected. Connecting Klaviyo was not done, because it needs an account at another vendor. So there were 4 screen steps up to the wall, about 5 minutes after the start, and no first result: no recovery e-mail, no attribution view and no measurement. What the app looked like in Shopify after the install (Manage app): Pixels Disconnected, Extensions 0 active, Expiring access tokens Missing, Enforced IP restrictions Enforced; access to Online Store, Customers and Discounts (view and edit), Orders and Products (view only) and Marketing and Store analytics (view and edit). Plans: no plan choice and no subscription screen was seen in the app, because the onboarding blocked first. The charges address of the app in Shopify (charges, pricing plans) gave There's no page at this address. The Shopify screen Approve subscription was not reached, so nothing was approved. From the App Store listing of 17 November (not a test result): Free plan available and Free trial available; Free recovers $1000 of e-mail revenue and has multi-touch attribution, new customer CPA benchmarks by cohort and a missed revenue audit for Klaviyo or another ESP; Pro $99 a month and Enterprise $219 a month, both charged based on the GMV (with Capture, to identify anonymous visitors, as an add-on on Enterprise), with a 7-day free trial on both; all charges in USD, recurring and usage-based charges billed every 30 days. Difference with the dossier (from the listing, not from the app): the dossier of 14 October gives ReCapture at $100 a month plus a 10% revenue share and Capture at $450 a month flat; the listing now shows Pro $99 and Enterprise $219, GMV based, so the dossier prices are out of date or renamed; the rating on the listing is 4.8 from 172 reviews (the dossier says 167). The price fields are not changed here; this is for the price bundle. Checkout: NOT reached, no plan screen and no Shopify approval screen were seen, no card was entered and nothing was paid. Cancelling: no paid plan ran, so nothing could be cancelled; the uninstall dialog was seen: it says that after uninstalling any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information, and it has a list of reasons (Testing multiple apps, Too expensive and others). Not tested: connecting Klaviyo or Omnisend, abandoned-cart recovery, e-mail, anonymous visitors (Capture), the attribution dashboard, the app embed, the ROI guarantee, paid plans, payment, a plan choice in the app and Book a Demo. Clean up: Attribuly was uninstalled at about 19:12 with the reason Testing multiple apps and no longer appeared in the list of installed apps; other apps were not touched; our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.
findings: Text we checked: "Klaviyo or Omnisend stores with real traffic". What we saw: The first screen offered Klaviyo, MambaSMS, Omnisend and CartSee, and the onboarding for Klaviyo asked to connect a Klaviyo account; Klaviyo and Omnisend are on the list, but the connection itself was not made, so what the app does for such a store was not tested.

Text we checked: "Not using above ESPs or want to identify anonymous visitors? Book a Demo". sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested AutoWrite on a Shopify development store: the install (with an error on the first open that went away after a reload), one SEO blog post made on the Free plan in 4 steps without a card (1500 words, a featured image, Content quality 95/100, status Draft), the usage counter (1 / 10), a brand voice saved on Free, and the plan screen on which Starter, Pro and Business were Not available on a development store. The generation screen did not refresh by itself and the text appeared only after a reload, about 3 minutes after the start. Publishing, automations and the paid plans were not tested, and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 19:05; the Shopify dialog Install app asked only for View staff and contributor data (store owner, blog contributors) and View and edit store data (products, Online Store). No card was asked. The install was done at about 19:07. First open: the first screen after the install was an error, Application Error: Cannot coerce the result to a single JSON object. The result contains 0 rows. Code: PGRST116. After reloading the same address the dashboard opened normally (Total Posts 0, Published 0, Scheduled 0). It looks like a first-time error while the store record was being created; it was not seen again. The admin was in English. Core action, make an SEO blog post: on the Free plan, Posts, Create New Post, Create with AI, the topic How to choose a snowboard for beginners, Generate post: 4 steps, no keyword and no product chosen. The screen stayed on This post is still generating, with a line that a generation stuck for a long time may have failed silently, and empty text; it did not refresh by itself, and the text appeared only after reloading the page, about 3 minutes after the start. A message about unsaved changes blocked leaving the page until Discard was clicked; the post stayed. Result: the title How to Choose Your First Snowboard (and Avoid Bad Advice), 1500 words with 5 H2 and 6 H3 headings, an excerpt, a generated featured image of snowboards, status Draft, and Content quality 95/100 with checks for length, SEO title, meta description, headings, URL handle (a warning), readability (Flesch 83/100), AI filler phrases, sentence rhythm and active voice, plus Version History (1). The text reads well but opens with an invented anecdote and has no sources and no store products (product references are a Pro feature). The score is the app's own and was not checked by a second tool. The post was not published to the blog; it stayed a draft in the app. Counter: Usage & Plan showed Posts generated 0 / 10 and Images generated 0 / 10 before the post and 1 / 10 for both after it. What is included on Free: 10 posts and 10 images every 30 days, 1 automation, Basic SEO; usage window 17-11-2026 to 17-12-2026. The vendor FAQ, as read before the test, says 3 posts for the free plan; the app and the plan screen say 10. Plans: Manage plan opened the Shopify screen Select a plan. Free to test: these plans are free to test on this store, regular pricing applies when the store goes live; Free with a Select button. Under Unavailable on dev stores: Starter $9 / 30 days, Pro $29 / 30 days and Business $79 / 30 days, all with a greyed out Not available. The amounts and contents match the dossier and the listing (the listing of 17 November: Free, Starter $9, Pro $29, Business $79, all charges billed in USD, no reviews yet). Because paid plans cannot be picked on a development store, no Approve subscription or test charge screen was reached, nothing was approved, nothing was paid and no card was asked. Difference with the dossier: the dossier lists brand voices and auto-publish as Starter features; on Free, Settings, Brand voices accepted a new voice (name, tone, custom instructions, banned words, preferred words) and showed Brand voice saved and 1 voice, Test voice, professional. Whether a saved voice is used in a generation or an automation on Free was not tested. Automations on Free: the page showed No automations yet with a Create automation button; not tested (the plan says 1 automation). Cancelling: Free plan, no subscription to cancel; the uninstall dialog (Settings, Apps, AutoWrite, Uninstall) says that the app can no longer be used, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information; a reason is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). Not tested: publishing to the Shopify blog, scheduling in the calendar, automations, bulk generation, keyword research, product or collection references, Google grounding, other languages, paid plans and checkout. Clean up: the test brand voice and the draft post existed only in the app and went away with the uninstall; AutoWrite no longer appeared in the list of installed apps; other apps were not touched; our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested GeoStock on a Shopify development store: the install, a three step onboarding on the Free plan, two of three locations chosen, the app embed and the block Product inventory added in the theme editor, and the stock per location on a product page. The first result came after about 5 minutes and about 30 steps and showed My Custom Location 50, but the app said that 1 of the 2 selected locations was no longer valid and not published, so the second location never showed, and a product stocked only there showed Not Available. The Basic approval screen asked for a payment method and was cancelled. The theme was put back and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 19:20; the Shopify dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and Install was clicked. The app is called GeoStock Inventory By Location in the admin and GeoStock: Multi Location Stock in the App Store. We went straight into the app, with no payment step. No card was asked. The admin was in English. Onboarding in 3 steps: Which stores should shoppers see (3 Shopify locations offered, with the line 0 selected, Free publishes up to 2), Add GeoStock to your store (the app embed and an inventory block), and Setup complete. Core action, show stock per location on a product page: 2 of the 3 locations were chosen, the app embed was switched on and the block Product inventory was added to Product information in the theme editor (in our own tab) and saved, which is needed to see the result. The first result in the preview came at about 19:25, about 5 minutes after the install and about 30 steps, many of them navigation in the theme editor. At first the block showed only Not Available on the products tried (Appointment, 3p Fulfilled Snowboard, Hydrogen). On The Collection Snowboard: Hydrogen, which has 50 available at the Shop location in Shopify, the block kept showing Not Available. In the app, the page Store locator showed 1 selected location(s) are no longer valid and are not published. Choose replacements. next to 2 of 2 locations selected (the location names were not visible in the list). Save locations gave Locations saved., but the warning stayed. On The Multi-location Snowboard the preview then showed My Custom Location 50; the Shop location did not appear. So stock per location works for one of the two chosen locations, and the other was not published; a product stocked only there showed Not Available. Why the second location counted as no longer valid was not found. Plans: the app screen Plan & billing showed Current plan Free, 2 locations, Standard design, 14 trial day(s) remaining, and a button Start a trial with Shopify Basic Plan $9.99/month; Free includes a store locator with up to 2 locations, search, directions, e-mail and business hours, and the standard design. Only Basic could be chosen in the app; a Plus Plan at $29.99 was not offered in the app. The App Store listing of 17 November says Free plan available and Free trial available, with a rating of 4.8 (80). Checkout: Start a trial opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription: Base Plan, $9,99 USD every 30 days, a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec, Subtotal $9,99 plus any applicable taxes, Total $9,99 due 1 Dec, and Add payment method, with Approve greyed out. The sentence that you will not be billed for this test charge was not there and a payment method was asked, so nothing was approved; Cancel was clicked, no card was entered and nothing was paid. Difference with the dossier: the dossier says there is no free plan, but the app and the listing have a Free plan with a store locator for up to 2 locations; the rating on the listing is 4.8 from 80 reviews while the dossier says 4.9 from 99. The price fields are not changed here; this is for the price bundle. Cancelling: no subscription was started; the uninstall dialog (Settings, Apps, GeoStock, Uninstall) says that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and requires a reason (Testing multiple apps was chosen). Not tested: the Plus Plan (not offered in the app), a custom theme integration, batch loading with many locations, back-in-stock alerts (Notify me), the store locator map, detecting the nearest store from the visitor's location, and the paid Basic features. Clean up: in the theme the block Product inventory was removed and the app embed was switched off and saved, so the theme is as before the test; GeoStock was uninstalled with the reason Testing multiple apps and no longer appeared in the list of installed apps; our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.
findings: Text we checked: "Free plan available. Free trial available". What we saw: The app and the listing offer a Free plan with a store locator for up to 2 locations (shown on the plan screen as Free, 2 locations, Standard design), while the dossier says there is no free plan.

Text we checked: "My Custom Location 50". What we saw: After the block Product inventory was added and saved, the preview of The Multi-location Snowboard showed the line My Custom Location 50, so stock per location does show on the product page for one location.

Text we checked: "1 selected location(s) are no longer valid and are not published". What we saw: Of the 2 chosen locations 1 was reported as no longer valid and not published, Locations saved. did not remove the warning, the Shop location never appeared, and a product with 50 in stock only at the Shop location kept showing Not Available.
Text we checked: "4.8 (80)". What we saw: The listing of 17 November shows a rating of 4.8 from 80 reviews, while the dossier says 4.9 from 99; the listing figure is newer.

sessions.what: We ran the free plan ourselves rather than describing the paid tiers from the pricing page. Daan created the account; everything after that was measured in the product: funnels built and published one by one until the walls appeared, with the wall text copied out word for word. involve.me contributed nothing to this test: no account, no briefing, no sight of the draft. We do carry an affiliate link to them, disclosed on this page, and the test was run on the free plan we signed up for ourselves.
findings: The free plan allows exactly 2 live funnels. We published two, and the third stopped with: “You have reached your limit of 2 live funnels. Please end any live funnels or upgrade your plan to publish more funnels.” The dialog puts an Upgrade plan button next to Publish now.
A second user is not a paid extra on free, it is nothing at all: “You don't have any team member seats on your plan. Upgrade for more.” There is no referral credit or trial seat.

The AI funnel builder works on the free plan, and it is the real product. One sentence — “build a 4-question quiz that helps a marketer pick a CRM” — produced a five-page funnel with a theme applied, questions, scoring and a result page, and it asked for approval before each risky edit. The comparison table lists “Create funnels with AI” as a Start-plan benefit, so this is more generous than the tier pages suggest.

A free account has no usage panel. “Plans & Billing” in the account menu goes straight to the upgrade page: no current plan, no counters, no AI-credit balance. You cannot find out what you have left; you discover a limit by hitting it.

Free publishing gives you a real subdomain and a choice of ten: daanV.involve.me plus quizzes.cx, forms.ac, calculators.cx, assessments.cx, tests.cx, surveys.so, feedback.ac, funnels.cx, researched.cx and paynow.cx. Every page carries involve.me branding; removing it is a paid step the share screen labels PRO, while the plan is actually called Grow.

The in-app comparison table publishes limits the public pricing page does not: funnel visits a month (10,000 / 25,000 / 100,000), contacts collected a month (300 / 1,000 / 3,000), file storage, embeds, payment accounts, and the price of every top-up. If you are sizing a plan, that table is the one to read.
Prices differ by surface: the public page quotes $29 / $69 / $139 and “Save up to 40%”, the in-app upgrade screen quotes €29 / €69 / €139 and “Save up to 41%”.

Onboarding is compulsory and is itself an involve.me funnel embedded in the app: four questions, carrying the “Made with involve.me” badge. You cannot reach the builder until you finish it. One of the answer options for “How did you discover involve.me?” is “AI - Claude”.

Replaying the same audio cost nothing: the meter stayed at 00:09:59.
The on-screen meter lags. After the one-word change it still showed 00:09:52, and only after a page reload did it show 00:09:46, so read it after reloading.

Because of that lag we cannot split the 14 seconds exactly per step. The most likely split, about 8 seconds for the first generation, nothing for the speed change and about 6 for the word change, fits Murf's help text: delivery settings on unchanged text are free, and a text edit regenerates the whole sub-block.

Downloads are blocked on the free trial. The export dialog lists MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG and other formats up to 48 kHz, but has no download button, only 'Unlock unlimited downloads - You are on free plan' with 'Upgrade Plan'.

sessions.what: A new free account, with no payment method asked for. We ran nine texts whose authorship we knew before we started: three passages from public-domain books (Darwin and William James), a paragraph one of us typed for the test, typos included, three paragraphs a language model wrote for our own reviews, one paragraph Claude wrote on the spot, and one of those machine paragraphs with three of its five sentences rewritten by Claude. We read the credit meter after every check and ran it into the daily limit.
findings: Nine for nine. All four human texts came back 'Human Written', including the 71-word paragraph typed for the test, and all five machine texts came back 'AI Generated', including the paragraph Claude wrote on the spot. Every result put the whole text on one side: the gauge read 100% each time. That figure is the share of the text it assigns to each side, not a confidence score.

A machine rewrite did not shake it. With three of its five sentences rewritten by a second model, the paragraph from our Hubstaff review still scored 100% AI. That measures a model paraphrasing a model; we did not test text a person had edited by hand.

Later the same day we gave it a tenth text: a deliberately clichéd AI paragraph after QuillBot's AI Humanizer had rewritten it (the Humanizer reported '0 AI signals'). Pangram still scored it 100% AI and added a note that the text 'appears to have been paraphrased or rewritten', pointing to one rewritten segment. Our own Claude rewrite of a review paragraph, earlier in the test, did not get that note.

Short texts carry a caveat, and very short ones are refused. Every text of 190 words or fewer was marked 'Confidence limited — short text'; the 224-word passage was not. Below 50 words the button stays grey, with 'Minimum 50 words required for accurate detection', and nothing is charged.

The 2,000 words a day are 20 credits of 100 words, rounded up per check. A 190-word text cost 2 credits and a 222-word text cost 3. Our first six checks came to 1,014 words and used 13 credits, the allowance for 1,300 words. At around 150 words a check, a day holds ten checks, not twenty. The cost shows next to the button before you click, and the balance sits at the top of the page.

Hitting the limit loses nothing. With 3 credits left, a 333-word text (4 credits) could still be submitted. A window then said the entry would cost 4 credits against the 3 remaining and offered the paid plans. Nothing was scanned and nothing was charged: the balance stayed at 3. The window does not say when the credits come back, and it does not offer to trim the text to what you have left.
Signed in and signed out, the pricing page shows the same amounts. The Professional button now reads 'Upgrade to Professional', with '$65 billed now' underneath, so that tier still has no trial.
not_tested: text that mixes human and AI writing, text a person edited by hand, languages other than English, anything longer than 224 words, the plagiarism check (paid plans only), image detection and the API

Three of the four human texts are famous public-domain passages a detector may well have seen before. The paragraph typed for the test is the stronger evidence, and it is a single paragraph of 71 words.

sessions.what: A new free account in ngram's v2 studio. We pasted the link to one of our own published reviews (ActiveCampaign) with a one-line brief, asked for 30 seconds, ran the same prompt twice and read the credit meter before and after each run.
findings: The new account opened with 1,200 credits, while ngram's pricing page (read the same day) lists the Free plan at 600 one-time credits. We report what the meter showed; we do not know why it was double.

The composer states the rate plainly: 10 credits a second, billed on the generated duration. It reserved 300 credits for a 30-second request, but both videos came out slightly long, at 32.5 and 32 seconds, and were charged 330 and 320 credits. The meter went 1,200 to 870 to 550, matching those charges exactly. The 32.5-second video was charged 330 credits, equivalent to 33 seconds at the displayed rate; we did not establish the rounding rule.

From the link alone it read the page, picked up the site's own colours, type and logo, and wrote a scene-by-scene storyboard with the narration script in about a minute and a half. Nothing was charged until we approved that plan, which is the moment to catch a wrong claim.

Every figure in both scripts matched the review: $15 a month as the floor, and $149, $189, $375 and $589 at 10,000 contacts, as read on 29 September 2026. It declined to animate prices between those two points because the review does not print them, and it kept the review's attribution on the contact-billing rule (credited to SendX in one run, labelled as reported in the other).

The same prompt gave a different video each time: five scenes in the first run, four in the second, with different wording and visuals. The facts stayed the same, but do not expect a repeat run to reproduce a video you liked.

Rendering took about six to seven and a half minutes after approval. The narration step failed once in each run and recovered on its own, and the second run said openly that it could not listen to its own voice-over and flagged one word that might sound clipped. Listen before you publish.

The visuals were motion graphics: the log showed ngram writing the scenes as an HTML animation and recording that, not generated camera footage. That suits explainers and product walkthroughs; it is not the tool for filmed-looking scenes.
Videos are private by default; sharing offers a public link, an embed, a download and direct posting to LinkedIn, X and YouTube, and captions are included.

sessions.what: We built a support agent from scratch with the description 'A customer support agent for Acme Headsets that answers customer questions using the attached help centre page', and gave it one public help-centre page of our own as its only knowledge: shipping countries and times, a 15:00 dispatch cut-off, returns, warranty, spare parts, two headsets with prices and support hours, with no phone line. We asked 13 questions, each in a new conversation on the agent's standalone chat page: ten the page answers, and three it does not (Japan, PayPal, and battery life with noise cancelling on). The first round ran without an account; after about ten conversations it stopped with 'This AI Agent has reached its conversation limit', so the last three, plus two repeats, ran on a new agent built the same way in a free Starter account.
findings: Eleven of 13 answers were right. Delivery times, the free-shipping threshold, the return window, free returns, the warranty exclusion, spare-part and headset prices and the 40-hour battery figure all matched the page.

It did not make things up when the page had no answer. It said it could not confirm PayPal, gave the 40-hour figure only for noise cancelling off and said it had no figure for it on, and inferred correctly that it does not ship to Japan because only the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany are listed.

It got the dispatch cut-off wrong. Asked about an order at 4 pm on a Tuesday, the first agent said it would not ship that day but not when it would; the second said it would ship the same day, because orders before 15:00 leave that day. The correct answer is Wednesday. The same question gave a different answer on a near-identical agent.

Asked 'Can I call you?', both agents said a representative had been asked to join and asked for an email address, instead of saying there is no phone support. With no live team behind it, that promise goes nowhere.
Adding the page once showed '2 links' in the knowledge base both times. The guest agent's conversation limit arrived after about ten chats; the free Starter plan lists 100 conversations a month.

On 17 November 2026 the session first installed the Shopify app of Gelato on a development store, which sent us at once to a separate Gelato login, and then tested in the Gelato dashboard with the own Gelato account of Daan. A Gildan 64000 T-shirt with the text Test Print reached the mockup and the Details step in about 6 minutes; Add to store needs a connected store, and a Manual store was enough. The product page showed €4.98 excl. VAT with 30% off the first order, delivery €3.99 and 4-5 business days to the Netherlands, and the shirt is made in 14 countries. The Gelato+ trial pop-up said Unlimited stores & users and that product discounts are not applied on the trial; the trial was not started, nothing was published, ordered or paid, and checkout and cancelling were not tested. Two attempts. First attempt, through the Shopify app: at 19:38 the install form of the App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/gelato-print-on-demand, English) was submitted in our own tab and the Shopify screen Install app warned that Gelato: Print on Demand does not support market-driven shipping (you can switch back to legacy shipping profiles until July 1, 2027) and asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. After Install the app sent us in the same minute to the login of Gelato (Welcome back, with Apple, Facebook and Google or an e-mail and a password, and Dont have an account? Sign up). There was no automatic connection and no Connect button, so the app only opens with a separate Gelato account. Nothing was filled in, no account was made and the app was uninstalled afterwards (reason Testing multiple apps). Second attempt, in the Gelato dashboard with the own Gelato account of Daan (not through the Shopify app, and the Gelato app was not installed in the development store): the dashboard was in English and showed the onboarding 3 simple steps to start selling (Connect your store, Create your first product, Order your first sample), the sidebar offer Try Gelato+ for free and a banner 30% off your first order. A first start at 20:14 was stopped at once on instruction; it was resumed at about 20:1x to 20:2x. Core action, a T-shirt with text up to the mockup, about 6 minutes and 14 steps: Create product, Single product led to Choose product with No templates here; in the Product catalog the page of the Gildan 64000 shirt has Add to store, which asks Connect your store to get started (Shopify, Etsy, Amazon, TikTok Shop, WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, BigCommerce, Manual), so a connected store is required. Manual was chosen (no outside account) with the store name Test Store typed by the tester, which made a store in Gelato. Then Create product, Single product, Bestsellers, Classic Unisex Crewneck T-shirt | Gildan 64000, and the wizard Product, Design, Details. The design editor showed a welcome pop-up (skipped), Add text was used and Test Print was typed; Continue to Details showed the mockup with Test Print on the chest, the title Classic Unisex Crewneck T-shirt | Gildan 64000 White, a description, a size table and care instructions, with Progress saved in Drafts. Nothing was published, ordered, sampled or paid and no address was entered. The draft was deleted with the menu and Delete (Yes, I want to delete product draft). Prices as shown: the product page said €4.98 excl. VAT in red, with the first order discount of 30% if placed in the next 47h 52m 14s, and delivery €3.99, 4-5 business days, Delivery to Netherlands. The catalogue said From € 8.51 excl. VAT and € 8.51 with Gelato+, and the wizard said From € 7.12 excl. VAT. The page also said No minimums, Ships in 4-5 days, 14 countries and Carbon-neutral; the shirt is made in AT, AU, CA, CZ, DE, FR, GB, IT, NL, NZ, PL, PT, SE and US (14 countries); the catalogue text said 680 products and 32 countries. No order was placed, so the real delivery time and the price at checkout were not tested. Plans: the App Store listing (read on 17 November 2026) says Free to install and Free trial available: Gelato Free (Pay for what you print; print on demand for global creators; hundreds of products to design and sell) and Gelato+ at $29.99 a month, or $239.88 a year and save 33% (up to 33% off products, exclusive tools, Magic Mockups, Instant Collections, Price Navigator, Product Migration with Velocity Switch, stock images, graphics and fonts) with a 14-day free trial; all charges are billed in USD and recurring and usage-based charges every 30 days. In the dashboard the pop-up Welcome to Gelato+! said Product discounts Not applied on trial (up to 33% off products; skip the trial to start getting discounts on your next order), Personalization Studio, AI Tools & Premium design assets, Unlimited stores & users, Cancel any time and that a reminder comes 5 days before the trial ends, with the buttons Start 14-day free trial and Skip trial and activate discounts now. Neither was clicked, because it was not known whether a card would be asked; no stored card was seen. No trial was started, nothing was approved and no Shopify approval screen was seen. Differences: the dossier says 2 stores and 2 users, the pop-up says Unlimited stores & users; the dossier says 32 countries and 250+ facilities, the listing says 140+ local production hubs in 32 countries; the dossier gives $19.99 a month billed yearly, the listing shows $239.88 a year (which is $19.99 a month) and save 33% next to $29.99 a month; the listing shows 4.8 stars and 1,044 reviews against 1,007 in the dossier. The price fields are not changed here. Checkout: NOT reached, the trial was not started and no card or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: not tested, no plan was taken; only the text Cancel any time on the trial pop-up was seen. Not tested: a real delivery or sample, publishing to a shop, Magic Mockups (Gelato+), discounts after activation, the cancel route, the plans inside the Gelato app of the Shopify store and local production beyond the list of countries. Clean up: the draft product was deleted; the empty Manual store Test Store stays in the Gelato account of Daan and the account stays; no trial and no card. In the first attempt the app was uninstalled from the development store and nothing was created. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
