sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested the Shopify app Notify Me! Back in Stock Alert on a development store: the install, the onboarding, the embed in an unsaved theme preview and one signup with a made up address. A Notify me button replaced Buy it now on the sold out product about 3 minutes after the start and opened a form for e-mail and SMS; the popup closed after the signup without a visible confirmation, the signup was not looked up in the dashboard and no alert was seen. The plan page of the development store showed only Standard, Rocket and Notify Me Plus, not the Lite, Kickstart and Starter plans of the dossier; choosing Standard (Yearly) gave no Shopify approval screen, so nothing was approved. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 19:40 and the Shopify screen Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; the install was approved at about 19:41. In the App Store the app is called Notify Me! Back in Stock Alert - Premium Preorder, Wishlist, Waitlist (Restock), Low stock App (apps.shopify.com/preorder-back-in-stock); inside the Shopify admin it is called Notify! Back in stock|Preorder. The developer is Notify Me! in Richmond, BC, which fits notify-me.io in the dossier. The admin was in English. Onboarding: one box to accept the Terms of service of Notify Me! and Continue; then the screen Notify Me! has four features to boost your store with Back-in-Stock, Pre-order, Wishlist and Low-stock; Back-in-Stock, Pre-order and Wishlist were ticked and Low-stock was not, and the tester left only Back-in-Stock on; then App embed activation. No password and no sign-up form were shown. Core action, a Notify me button on a sold out product: the product was The Out of Stock Snowboard ($885.95, Sold out, already sold out, the stock was not changed). In the theme editor (the test-data theme, the Default product template, the App embeds tab) the embed Notify Me! was switched on and not saved. The preview showed Notify me in place of Buy it now at about 19:43, about 3 minutes after the start and about 8 actions after the install. A click on Notify me opened a popup Notify me via: with Email, SMS (NL (+31) and a Phone Number box) and the button Notify Me When Available. A made up test address was typed and the form was sent; the popup closed without any visible confirmation. No phone number was entered and no e-mail was sent or received. The signup was not looked up in the dashboard of the app and no back in stock alert was seen. The editor was left with Leave page (Leaving this page will delete all unsaved changes), so nothing was saved. Plans: after Activate later the app showed Development Store: Free Access to all plans, You are currently on a development store, selecting a plan will create a test charge at no cost, giving you full access to all premium features. Yearly (33% off): Standard $39.90 struck through, $26.61 a month, Billed annually at $319.26; Rocket (Most popular) $69.90, $46.61 a month, $559.3; Notify Me Plus $499.99, $333.33 a month, $3999.92. A banner said Early bird: 78% off your first 2 months, until November 15, and was still shown on 17 November. All three buttons said Start 7-day free trial. Limits in the app: Standard 1.500 notifications (pauses at limit), 1.500 PreOrders ($0.15 per extra PreOrder) and 10.000 Wishlist actions; Rocket 5.000 notifications, 10.000 PreOrders ($0.1 per extra) and 25.000 Wishlist actions; Notify Me Plus unlimited; $0.03 per SMS in US/CA on all three. Difference with the dossier and the listing: the dossier and the listing name Lite (free), Kickstart $9.90, Starter $19.90 and Standard $39.90 (the listing gives yearly prices of $79.21, $159.23 and $319.26 and the text 78% Off Until BFCM; the dossier gives yearly prices of $95, $191 and $383 and a Standard limit of 1.500 alerts, the app says 1.500 notifications), while the app on the development store showed only Standard $39.90, Rocket $69.90 and Notify Me Plus $499.99 and no Lite, Kickstart or Starter plan. Why the list differs, for example because of the development store, was not found out. The price fields are not changed here. Choosing a plan: Standard (Yearly) was chosen and the dialog Annual plan confirmation said Standard (Yearly), Billed annually $319.26/yr and that the 7-day free trial starts immediately and nothing is charged until the trial ends. Approve on Shopify was clicked, but no Shopify approval screen appeared and the page stayed on the plan page. So nothing was approved, no test charge was seen and the sentence that the test charge is not billed was not seen. Checkout: NOT reached, no Shopify approval screen, no card and no payment screen were seen. Cancelling: not tested, no plan was active. Not tested: a real notification or restock e-mail, SMS, pre-order, wishlist, low-stock, the list of signups in the dashboard, the Lite plan, an approved test charge and the cancel route. Clean up: no theme change was saved. The app was uninstalled through Settings, Apps with the reason Testing multiple apps; the screen said that Notify! Back in stock|Preorder was successfully uninstalled. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: A new free Basic account. We made one 29-second video from a blank template with a stock avatar and our own 99-word script, read the credit meter on the Billing page before and after, then changed one word and generated it again. The same day we compared the app's upgrade window with the public pricing page.
findings: Onboarding knew who we were before we told it. We skipped the company-website question, yet the prompt box was pre-filled with a brief about our own site, with suggestions such as 'Introduce the Tool Finder', and four draft videos about us appeared in the library without being asked for. They used no credits.

The meter charges by the second. Our 29-second video took the Billing page from 0 to 59 of 1,200 credits, about 2 credits a second, and the app's banner went from '600 seconds' to '571 seconds of video creation time left'. In this account the free month is 10 minutes of finished video. The public pricing page the same day prices video at 100 credits a minute, which would make 59 credits about 35 seconds.

A small edit did not cost the whole video again. After changing one word and generating again, the meter moved from 59 to 63 credits. The second time, though, the button read 'Generate in 15 minutes' instead of 'Generate' and the job went into a queue. Each version took about eight to nine minutes from the click to a finished video.
An upgrade window ('You only have 600 seconds of video creation time left') opened the moment we clicked Generate, and again on every reload of the video page.

On Basic the video carries the Synthesia logo. 'Remove watermark' is marked as paid in the Generate window, and the Billing page lists 'Download your videos' as a Starter feature; we did not try to download.

The app and the public pricing page described different plans on the same day. The app's upgrade window offered Starter at €19 a month or €12 billed yearly with 15,500 credits a year, and Creator at €79 or €49 with 72,500 credits a year. The public pricing page, read without signing in and served in dollars, lists Starter at $29 or $18 with 1,250 credits a month and a Pro plan at $89 or $64 with 6,000 credits a month where Creator used to be; its own comparison table still says 'Free, Starter, and Creator'.
The AI Assistant page that should have built a video from our prompt stayed on a loading screen for over 90 seconds in our session, so we built the video from a blank template instead.

sessions.what: A free account, used on QuillBot's AI Detector, AI Humanizer and Paraphraser. We ran the detector over the texts of known authorship we used for our Pangram test the same day: three passages from public-domain books, a paragraph one of us typed for the test, three paragraphs a language model wrote for our own reviews, and one Claude wrote on the spot. We added a control paragraph written in stock chatbot phrasing, sent it through the Humanizer, and checked the rewrite in QuillBot's detector and in Pangram.
findings: The detector scored all eight texts 0% AI, the four machine-written ones included. Our three review paragraphs and the paragraph Claude wrote on the spot each came back '100% Human-written'. Pangram, given the same eight texts the same day, labelled every one correctly.

It does catch AI text that sounds like AI. The control paragraph, which opens “In today's fast-paced digital landscape”, scored 100% AI, with the stock phrases underlined and the opening sentence listed as 'High'. In our test it picked up the style, not the authorship: plainly written machine text passed as human.

The Humanizer and the detector disagree. The Humanizer rewrote the control paragraph and reported '0 AI signals' on its own output. QuillBot's detector scored that same output 100% AI. Pangram scored it 100% AI too and added that it 'appears to have been paraphrased or rewritten'. The rewrite mostly swapped words: 'seamless' became 'smooth', 'In conclusion' became 'Simply put'.
Every result came with the prompt 'Want your text to sound more authentic? Refine with Paraphraser', including on texts the detector had just rated 100% human.

Signed out, the detector ran four checks (689 words) and then asked us to sign up. It will not run below 40 words, and under 80 it shows 'For more accurate results, add at least 80 words'; it still scored our 71-word paragraph.

The free Paraphraser's 125-word cap is real, and stricter than it sounds. Given 219 words, it reported '219/125 words. Limit exceeded' and showed only the first sentence of the rewrite, with the rest blurred behind an upgrade button, not the first 125 words.
The detector page showed model version v7.1.0.
not_tested: Premium, the plagiarism and grammar checkers, the Humanizer's daily use limit, languages other than English and texts longer than 219 words

sessions.what: The Freddy AI Agent in a Freshchat trial account, built in AI Agent Studio. We wrote a short help page for a made-up headset shop (shipping, returns, warranty, two products, opening hours: about 250 words) and gave the agent its URL as the only knowledge source; learning finished in about two minutes. We then ran 13 customer questions through the studio's Test screen: 10 whose answer is on the page, one that needs a small inference (shipping to Japan when the page lists only three countries) and two whose answer is not on the page at all (PayPal, and battery life with noise cancelling on). We scored every reply against the page.
findings: 11 of the 13 replies were correct, and every factual reply linked the help page as its source. That includes the trickier ones: an order at 4pm on a Tuesday ships on Wednesday because of the 15:00 cut-off, a cable broken by pulling is excluded from the warranty, and 'Do you ship to Japan?' got a clear no with the three countries we do ship to.

It did not invent anything where the page was silent. Asked about PayPal, it said the help centre has no information on payment methods. Asked for battery life with noise cancelling on, it gave the documented 40 hours, said that figure is with noise cancelling off, and declined to give a number for the other case.

The one wrong reply was 'Can I call you?'. The page says there is no phone support; the agent answered 'Sure! Assigning your chat to our support agent.' It treated the question as a request for a human and started a handover, and the 'Sure!' reads as a yes. The Test dashboard still counted this reply as Answered.
One reply added something the page does not contain: after correctly refusing the warranty claim, it offered to explain 'replacing the cable at your own cost', which our page never mentions.

The dashboard's totals (12 answered, 1 unanswered) are a useful first filter, but you have to read the replies: the handover counted as an answer, and the correct 'I don't know' about PayPal counted as unanswered.

Employees took our made-up names with accents, an employee ID, a hire date and a multi-line note. There are no custom fields for codes or amounts.
Each punch shows the IP address of whoever entered it, here the manager.

The standard export ('Export to Excel' on the payroll export) is actually a CSV, with employee ID, names and hours: 1.500 and 2.000, which match our test shifts. It has no notes, emails or start and end times. The employee profile export is part of a paid add-on ($2 per user a month).
The employee import takes eight fixed columns (username, names, email and password required). It has no notes field and no update option, so you cannot change records by importing again.

Buddy Punch told us, and its pricing page (read 12 November 2026) confirms, that API and MCP access are included from the Pro plan, which our trial runs on; Advanced adds higher API and MCP limits. sessions.what: On 26 September 2026 we built the same class-booking web app in Lovable, Replit and Emergent from one identical prompt, each on its free plan, and checked every result against 18 tests we wrote down before the first build. We changed no code: the builder only got our prompt and, where a test failed, a repair prompt in fixed words. Replit ran on a new Starter account, separate from the paid account Daan uses for his own project.
findings: The Agent built a separate API and web app on PostgreSQL in 8 minutes of work by its own count, ran its own functional test and reported everything as passing. It did not publish by itself: publishing is a manual click, and on Starter the deployment is labelled temporary and will expire.

Its own test booked one person at a time. When we sent ten bookings for an empty eight-spot class at the same moment, all ten were accepted, after which the class list returned an error and the public page showed 'No classes on the calendar yet.' until two bookings were cancelled.

Given that exact description, the Agent added a database lock per class in two minutes; the same ten simultaneous bookings then gave exactly eight. The same repair stopped it accepting a name made only of spaces.

On Starter the usage page is closed ('You must have an active subscription to view your own usage'), so you cannot see what a request cost, and the daily allowance was gone after the build and one repair.
The code export, run from the project zip, built and ran outside Replit on our own database, but the export and its Git history carried the generated admin password in plain text.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 6 November 2026 on the free plan: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We asked the AI editor for a two-slide presentation with exact text, then read the sharing, download and upgrade screens. We published nothing and did not start the Plus trial.
findings: No card was asked for at sign-up. The dashboard showed 500 credits. One generation of two slides took about a minute and brought the balance to 350, so 150 credits.

Our third prompt asked for a title slide and a second slide holding one line of text and nothing else. The first two attempts lost characters while we typed, which was our own input slip, so we do not count them. The title came out without 'TEST' and without the brackets. Slide two showed our line in capitals and added a label 'VALIDATION STATUS // AIBM-001' and a large '001' that we had not asked for.

The zooming overview carried an invented headline, 'PROTOCOL ALPHA, Internal hardware validation', over a mountain landscape with hardware renders. None of that was in the prompt. A 'Made with Prezi' badge sits on the slides.

A new presentation is public by default, with a public link and a QR code. AI analysis of viewing behaviour, reuse by viewers (who can make their own editable copy) and viewer downloads as PDF, PowerPoint or SCORM were all switched on.

In the owner's Download tab, PDF, editable PPTX and SCORM are all marked Plus. That sits next to a sharing setting that lets viewers download in the same formats. We did not test the viewer side, so we do not know which of the two wins.

The upgrade dialog offers Plus at €15 a month, billed annually. The trial screen shows €0.00 due now and the first charge on 20 November. It still asks for a payment method: a base of €180.00 a year plus 21% VAT of €37.80, so €217.80 after the trial. Registering the account itself needed no card. We stopped there.

Our earlier test of 28 September 2026 on a Basic account, with a ten-slide investor deck, found the same download lock and a public-only sharing option. That test is described in the four-tool comparison linked below.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 5 and 16 November 2026 on one account: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 5 November we used the free Personal plan up to the upload screen. By 16 November the same account showed Pro, provided by the vendor, so we did not buy it and saw no checkout. On Pro we sent one request to our own test address, signed it ourselves and downloaded the signed PDF and the certificate. Nothing went to a third party.
findings: Sending to signed took 37 seconds on Pro (sent 21:13:28 UTC, signed 21:14:04 UTC, completed 21:14:05 UTC), and about 1.5 minutes from upload. With 'I am also signing' switched on, Send went straight to the sign page. The signature type was Draw, Upload image or Text; we chose Text.

The field editor offers Signature, Text, Checkbox, Date, Initials, Paragraph, File and Stamp (the last ones after 'More...'). The signer was assigned automatically; Mandatory was on and Fixed was off.

The download is the signed PDF (attachment_AIBM_002_signed.pdf, 315 KB, 2 pages: the original plus an extra page) and a separate Certificate of Completion. The certificate lists the request ID, sender email, sent and completed times in UTC, 'sent via web', and per signer the email, sign date, IP address and user agent.

The signed PDF has a real digital signature field (two PAdES signatures, SubFilter ETSI.CAdES.detached) issued to Innovoris Labs Srl by DigitalSign CA G1. AATL is not mentioned anywhere in the app or the certificate, and we did not check whether the chain is on Adobe's approved trust list, so we make no claim about it.

Templates: on Personal the Templates page said 'Available only with a Business plan'. On Pro, New template worked (upload, a role 'Signer' instead of an email address, fields optional) and saved with Edit, Bulk send and Use. We did not test the Business plan itself.

An uploaded file name changes: attachment-AIBM-001.pdf (free, 5 Nov) and attachment-AIBM-002.pdf (Pro, 16 Nov) were shown with underscores instead of hyphens, and the signed download carries the underscore name. We compared display names only, not file contents.

The upload step offers 'Merge into a single document' and the sources 'Upload file' and 'Google Drive'. The file picker accepts PDF, Word and Excel types; we did not upload a .docx, so conversion is untested.

My Account on Pro shows only 'Compare plans', 2FA, API, Notifications, Consent screen and 'Delete Account'. We found no button to stop or downgrade Pro or to manage billing. Nothing was clicked; a route through support or a billing email may exist.

On 5 November the free plan page listed Business at $5 a month ($48 a year) and Pro at $15 a month ($144 a year), each with a 14-day trial. Without a signer the form said 'You must fill in at least one signer' and Send stayed grey.

sessions.what: We did not just read the docs: we ran 40 pricing queries across 20 tools and two engines through the async batch endpoint for a research report of our own, then spent a further handful of credits measuring what individual requests actually cost. Cloro is an affiliate partner of ours, which is why we checked their credit table against the meter instead of quoting it.
findings: A plain async ChatGPT task billed 5 credits, not the 7 the pricing table lists for a full ChatGPT response: that is the web-search rate. It held over 20 requests in a batch and again on a single measured call. Budget from 5 and the free tier is 100 ChatGPT answers, not 71.

The credit meter lags. Straight after a completed ChatGPT task the balance was unchanged; the charge landed about 90 seconds later. If you gate your own spending on a balance read immediately after a call, you will overshoot.

The harvest does not echo your request back: task.payload comes back null. Submit a batch of 40 and nothing in the response tells you which answer belongs to which query: you have to keep your own map of task id to question. This cost us a wrong result on the first pass.

The response shape differs per engine, so there is no single schema to code against. ChatGPT returned text, sources, citationPills and model; Perplexity returned no model but added related_queries, search_model_queries and shopping_cards.
Async tasks came back in roughly 30 to 40 seconds each, and on the free tier's single concurrent job a 40-task batch is a queue, not a burst: budget wall-clock time as well as credits.
Source counts swing wildly and that is the engine, not the API: one Perplexity call returned 10 sources, while in our 20-tool batch 14 of 20 Perplexity answers returned no sources at all.

sessions.what: The free plan on a new account. We uploaded one recording whose exact script we hold: the 2-minute-49 audio of our own Contabo video review, two synthetic voices and 377 words with prices, dates and product names. We compared the transcript word for word with the script, checked how it split the speakers, and read the AI summary and action items against what was said. In setup we chose the narrowest meeting settings: join only meetings we invite it to, recaps to the account owner only.
findings: The transcript was close: after evening out punctuation and number formats, 5.3% of the 377 words differed from the script. Product names such as Contabo, DigitalOcean, Cloud VPS 12, cPanel and Plesk came through.

The errors sat where a buyer would care. '6.70 euros a month' came out as '6.€70amonth', 'the usual fine print' as 'the US fine print', and 'excluding VAT' dropped out of the sentence with the entry price, though a later sentence kept 'Prices on the page exclude vat'.
Speaker detection found six speakers in a recording with two voices, and split single sentences across them.

The AI summary had the facts right: the 24-month prepaid term, about 25% more month to month, backups at 6.70 euros and the DigitalOcean comparison. Its one action item was assigned to 'Daniel Cho', a name that is not spoken anywhere in the recording.

The free plan's 'unlimited transcription' depends on your settings. In setup the switch for unlimited free transcripts sits beside the line 'Users on Join-All and Share-All settings get unlimited meeting transcripts': Fireflies joining every meeting with a link and sending recaps to everyone on the invite. Our narrower choice switched it off, and the account then showed '3 Free meetings'.
Right after the upload the app offered a 7-day Business trial, noting that billing may increase with usage once credits run out. We declined it, and the file was transcribed on the free plan.

sessions.what: We opened a new Databox account through the 'Get started' button under the Free plan on databox.com/pricing, connected Google Analytics 4 and Google Search Console for our own site, asked Genie two questions about that data, let Genie try to build a dashboard, and read the credit meter under Settings → Billing after every step. One account, one evening, our own traffic data, not a month of team use.
findings: The Free button does not give you Free. The account opened as a 14-day trial of Team Core at $249 a month, billed monthly. Free was listed in the app as a 'Downgrade'. Databox's own FAQ says that if no payment details are added by the end of the trial, syncing stops and reports pause, so anyone who wanted Free has to downgrade by hand before day 14.

The downgrade was blocked until we deleted Databox's own sample data. The message: 'You have 1 connected Spreadsheets, but the Free plan is limited to 0.' That one spreadsheet was the Sample dataset Databox adds at sign-up. Free allows no spreadsheets at all: Excel and Google Sheets both open an 'Upgrade to Analyst' wall at $89 a month, something the pricing page does not say.

Your one free dashboard is already taken. Databox's own Sample Dashboard stays after the downgrade and fills the plan's single dashboard slot. 'Create New Databoard' opened the $89 upgrade wall, and so did the button that would hang the sample dashboard on your own data.

What a Genie question costs: 3.7 credits for a simple one ('which pages got the most views in August'), 3.8 for a heavier week-by-week comparison. On Free's 50 a month that is about thirteen questions. The onboarding had already spent 1.9 credits by sending our four setup answers to Genie as a first question we never asked, and the app showed 'Buy more to keep Genie running' at 48 left.

Genie spends credits on things the plan will not allow. It offered to build a dashboard, tried three times, reported that Databox 'rejected the request as invalid' without naming the one-dashboard limit, and charged 5.2 credits for nothing. After one hour we had used 14.6 of the month's 50 credits.

Genie's diagnoses need checking. It called a half-finished Search Console connection 'broken' because 'the login expires' (the data manager said 'Unfinished connection'), and it flagged one of our real review URLs as a typo. The traffic figures themselves came back fast and were usefully broken down, including pages counted twice because of query strings.

What held up: connecting a data source cost no credits, the unfinished connection still counted against the three-source limit, and the plan prices inside the app matched the public pricing page ($89 / $249 / $399 monthly; $71 / $199 / $319 billed annually).
sessions.not_tested: We did not add a fourth data source past the limit, did not build our own dashboard after deleting the sample one, and could not check how fresh each source's data is: the app shows sync frequency but no last-synced time.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Pumper Bundles on a Shopify development store: the install, the Free plan without a card, a Volume Discount template that gave a Live Preview with Buy 2 10% off and Buy 3 20% off about 1 minute 10 seconds and 4 steps after the install click, the plan page, the Shopify approval screen for Build (a 7-day trial; it said there would be no test charge but asked for a payment method; nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Install: the Install button on the App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/pumper-quantity-breaks-product-bundles-discounts, English, vendor Profit Pumper Bundle) was clicked in our own tab at 20:37 and the form led straight to the Shopify screen Install app in the same tab. The screen said the app needs access to View customer data (Device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Customers, products, orders, discounts, Online Store, custom data, Shopify admin). Install was confirmed and the app opened on Choose your plan. No vendor account, password, Google login or terms tick box was seen, and no call or phone number was asked. Core action, a volume discount: Select Free Plan (No charges - Free forever) gave the toast Plan Activated with no Shopify approval screen. The app then showed Offer templates (Every card is the real storefront widget, mounted with that template's settings) with templates such as Volume Discount, Buy X Get Y, Mix & Match, Bundle, Progressive Free Gift and Side-by-Side Packs. One click on Use this template at Volume Discount opened the editor Offer 1 with the tiers Buy 1, Buy 2 and Buy 3, Show on All products and a Live Preview next to it. For the product The Complete Snowboard the Live Preview said Buy More Save More, Buy 1 Standard Price $699.95, Buy 2 10% OFF Save $139.98 $1,259.92 (was $1,399.90) and Buy 3 20% OFF Save $419.97 $1,679.88 (was $2,099.85), with the badge Most Popular. The first result stood there about 1 minute 10 seconds after the install click (20:37 to about 20:38) and 4 steps in all (confirm the install, Select Free Plan, Use this template; nothing had to be filled in). A line under the preview said Remove Powered by Pumper by offer verification, and a chat bubble asking Need any help setting up the offer? with a photo of an agent was in the corner (hidden in the images, not opened). The offer was not published and not saved (Publish and Save as draft were not used) and no theme change was made, so whether the widget shows on a real product page was NOT tested. Plans in the app (Monthly; the Yearly button says Up to 25% Off): Free $0.00 a month with Lifetime limit of $300 in bundle revenue and No charges - Free forever; Build $9.99 a month with Up to $1,000 extra sales for your store and the button Start 7-days trial; Scale $29.99 a month (Most Popular) with Up to $5,000 extra sales; Dominate $49.99 a month with Unlimited extra sales; under the paid plans Full money-back guarantee. Cancel anytime. After the Free plan was activated the Plans page said Current Plan Free and Earned $0 / $300. The Complete feature list is not the same on every plan: Free has crosses for Free shipping, Swatches, Subscription, Target by market, Translation, Predefined variants, Mix & Match deals, Buy X Get Y deals, Upsell, Checkbox upsell, Progressive free gift, Deal reveal and Countdown timer, and ticks for Free gift, Add image, Sold out tier, Bundle deals and Animated border; Build, Scale and Dominate have everything ticked. Checkout: Start 7-days trial on Build (monthly) opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription: a yellow bar You will not be billed for this test charge., the plan Build (monthly), $9,99 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., Subtotal $9,99 plus any applicable taxes, Total $9,99 Due 24 Nov, and a row Add payment method (so no payment method was stored), with By proceeding, you are agreeing to the Terms of Service. The Approve button looked active, but it was not clicked because a payment method was being asked and no card may be entered; Cancel was clicked and nothing was approved. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall: the dialog Uninstall Pumper Bundles? says that you can no longer use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason had to be chosen (Testing multiple apps) before the uninstall. Differences from the review: the listing names the plans Starter, Growth and Unlimited and the app names them Build, Scale and Dominate, with the same prices ($9.99, $29.99 and $49.99); the review and the listing say that every plan has the same features, while in the app Free lacks Free shipping, Mix & Match, Buy X Get Y, Upsell, Translation and Countdown timer among others; the review says Free is the full app up to $300 of extra revenue, while the app says Lifetime limit of $300 in bundle revenue; the review says the vendor site gives a 14 day trial against 7 days on the listing, and the Shopify screen and the plan buttons said 7 days (the vendor site was not opened). The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: publishing the offer and the widget on a real product page, Mix & Match, Buy X Get Y, upsell and Free shipping (not on the Free plan and no paid plan was activated), rule-based bundles, how the extra revenue is measured, Analytics (Beta) and the chat. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 20:41 through Settings, Apps (message: You have successfully uninstalled Pumper Bundles). No offer was saved, no theme change was made, no test product was made and no card was entered. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: Historical test data: these are measurements from 4 September 2026, at that day's free allowance and meters, not today's Free plan or the standard cost of every Bot. We ran the reproducible test BrowserAct's own partner team proposed, on a free account with the 1,500 sign-up credits the card offered at the time. The prompt, verbatim: open books.toscrape.com, collect the first 20 books in listing order, open each detail page and return full title, displayed price, availability and source URL, leave unavailable fields blank, infer nothing. Before touching BrowserAct we fetched the same 20 pages with plain HTTP and saved the four fields as ground truth, so every value below was checked against the source, not against BrowserAct's own claims. Then we built the Bot from the prompt, ran it twice from the published version, and read the credit meter after each step.
findings: Accuracy: 80 of 80 fields correct, three times over. The build's own verification output, run 1 and run 2 each returned 20 rows with title, price, availability and URL identical to our ground truth, including the parenthetical stock counts ('In stock (22 available)') and the currency symbol, which the Bot kept as displayed rather than converting.

The build costs more than the runs. Building the Bot took 4 minutes 59 seconds and 278 credits; the agent inspected the listing and a detail page, wrote a small package (a SKILL.md, a run.py and two DOM helpers), compiled it, and ran it end to end before declaring it ready. On that day's free tier that was about a fifth of the sign-up credits spent before the first real run. The pricing page now estimates 300 to 500 credits for a simple Agent build, and today's free card lists 2 free Agent Builds alongside its 200 credits.

Runs are cheap but not deterministic in cost. Run 1 used 21 credits in 1 minute 56 seconds; run 2, the same Bot on the same 20 pages, used 27 credits in 3 minutes 12 seconds. Identical output, 29% more credits and 65% more wall time. At Basic's 10,000 credits for $13 a month on yearly billing, a run of this size is roughly three cents, so the variance is small in money and worth knowing about in budgeting.

The meter is honest at the account level and confusing at the task level. Balance went 1,500 to 1,222 after the build, 1,201 after run 1 and 1,174 after run 2, which reconciles exactly with the per-task figures in the history list. But the task detail panel showed 'Credits used: 0' for a run that the history list, seconds later, priced at 21. Trust the list and the balance, not the panel.

The agent made one silent design decision. The prompt said 'the first 20 books', and the Bot was built with no parameters and 'first 20' hard-coded; it says so in its own summary and offers to change it on request. Fine for this test, but a Bot you intend to reuse should be built with the count as an input, and you have to ask for that.

Historical: on 4 September the app and the website showed different prices. On first login the app opened a '7-days free trial' panel listing Basic at $16, Essential at $70 and Advanced at $120 a month, with $20, $100 and $200 struck through, while the public pricing page, read the day before, still charged $20, $100 and $200 monthly. That gap closed by 13 September: the public page now shows the same $16, $70 and $120.
not_tested: books.toscrape.com is a static sandbox with no login, no JavaScript rendering and no anti-bot measures, so none of the managed-browser, proxy or CAPTCHA infrastructure in BrowserAct's pitch was exercised. It proves the no-code loop from plain prompt to reusable Bot; it says nothing about hostile sites, where proxy use starts to matter -- free in the cloud for a limited time, 5,000 credits per gigabyte of dynamic proxy traffic on the Local CLI.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Code Bulk Discounts on the Free plan of a Shopify development store: the plan screens, generating 20 unique codes for a 10 percent discount, the CSV download and the delete dialog. Nothing was paid or deleted. The app opens on Select a discount with the text Search and select an existing discount code, so it does not create a discount rule itself; the list showed only existing discounts. We made a 10 percent order discount in Shopify Discounts first; an Amount off products discount asked for products or collections, so an order discount was used. In the app we searched that discount and chose Generate codes (Automatically generate codes, with the counter 0 of 500 allowance). The form has Count (default 1, set to 20), Charset Alphanumeric, Length 8, empty Prefix and Suffix, Include Job ID (recommended) switched on and a Title, and says Free codes remaining: 500 of 500. After Generate the Previous jobs table showed Requested 20, Imported 0, Failed 0 with Importing 0%, and after about 10 seconds Requested 20, Imported 20, Failed 0 with status Complete. Shopify Discounts then showed 21 codes created by the Shopify web app (the 20 generated plus the main code), each customer entering a unique code, and 0 used. Codes have 8 characters plus the job number as a suffix. The Actions menu offers Download CSV, Connect Klaviyo to upload (greyed out), Email QR embed and Delete Set. Download CSV gave a file with the heading Coupon and 20 codes, all unique; that file is not part of the evidence. Delete Set opened the dialog Delete this set? with Cancel and Delete; Cancel was pressed and nothing was deleted. Timing, approximate tester observations: installation at about 14:22 and the first generated codes at about 14:27, mostly spent choosing the plan and making the parent discount by hand; the code generation itself took 3 steps and about 10 seconds of processing. Not tested: more than 20 codes, Pro, Upload codes, the QR code, Klaviyo, using a code in a real checkout, the app Settings screen and uninstalling. No kit records were entered.
findings: Vendor claim "Generate 500 lifetime codes". What we saw: The Free plan card says so and the generator form said Free codes remaining: 500 of 500 before the run of 20 codes. Vendor claim "This plan is free. You will not be billed". What we saw: Shopify showed this on the Approve charge screen for the Free plan and the plan was approved at 0 dollars; nothing was paid. Trying the Free plan costs nothing.

Vendor claim "Search and select an existing discount code". What we saw: The app starts by asking for an existing discount, so a parent discount has to be made in Shopify first; an Amount off products discount asked for products or collections and an order discount was used instead. Vendor claim "$14,99 / 30 days". What we saw: The Pro plan card shows $14,99 / 30 days with the button Not available because the store is in development. Pro adds unlimited codes per month at $14,99 per 30 days on the plan card; the amount at checkout is unknown.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Kite on a Shopify development store: the install, which opened the app at once without a plan choice, the Free plan with 50 orders a month and no card, a free gift for carts of $100 and more built by the Kite AI from one example and saved in test mode (Changes Saved) in about 8 clicks and about 8 minutes, the plan page, the Shopify approval screen for Starter (a 7-day trial; it said there would be no test charge but also asked for a payment method; nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. The screen warned that the app does not support market-driven shipping and said the app needs access to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. Install was clicked at about 20:44 and the app opened at once, with no plan choice and no payment screen. The welcome screen said Ready to convert more carts into customers? with a Get Started button. No terms tick box, no separate vendor account and no popup was seen. Kite AI answered that it would set up a free gift for carts that reach $100 once a gift was chosen and asked Which products are the free gift?; Demo Mug was chosen. The result at about 20:50 was the offer Free gift on orders over $100 with the rule Cart subtotal is at least US$ 100,00 and the gift Demo Mug x1, applied Automatically in the cart, with the visibility Test mode: hidden from shoppers, preview via campaign link, and the note Nothing is saved until you click Save in the editor. Open in editor and Save (at about 20:52) gave the toast Changes Saved on the page Free Gift With Purchase, with a switch Test mode and Live and the notice App not active on your store yet. sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Consentmo GDPR on a Shopify development store: the install, the three-step onboarding with a banner preview, the plan screen with a Black Friday promotion, the Shopify approval screen for Standard (not approved), the Free plan, one click on Activate for the app embed, the banner in the theme editor preview and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and nothing was saved in the theme editor. Install: the App Store listing (English) is called Consentmo GDPR and says Free plan available. Free trial available. The first install try at about 12:21 ended with Installation canceled.; the second try opened a pop-up tab with only the list of apps; the third try opened the Install app dialog in the admin, which asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. Install was approved at about 12:23 and the app opened on its dashboard. Onboarding: three steps, Choose your region (Europe, GDPR), Design your cookie banner and Set your consent options (Accept / Reject / Preferences, marked Popular), ending with the button Finish set up. In step 3 the app shows a preview as Europe with the text We use cookies to run this site, measure traffic, and personalize content. and the buttons Preferences, Reject and Accept. Core action: Finish set up led straight to the plan screen Pick your plan. Back on the dashboard it said Current plan: Free, Cookie banner: Setup needed and App embed is not enabled. One click on Activate gave the message Cookie bar enabled on your store., so the app embed was switched on by the app itself in one click, without a theme edit by us. The dashboard then showed Cookie Consent Health 71 / 100 with 6 issues, among them EU Withdrawal page not set up, Google Consent Mode v2 not configured and Cookie Policy page missing, Banner visible: Europe and Smart Geotargeting: Off. In the theme editor the banner showed on the home page preview with the same text and the buttons Preferences, Reject and Accept; nothing was saved in the theme editor and the storefront outside the editor was not opened. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 2 minutes from the install (12:23) to the banner in the theme editor preview (about 12:25), in about 7 steps (choose region, Next, Next, Finish set up, back to the dashboard, Activate, open the editor). The first try at 12:21 and the second try were wasted by install errors. Plans: the Pick your plan screen is monthly by default and carries the label BFCM Deal: 25% Off for 3 Months. Free $0 a month (Get started); Standard $7.5 a month, was $10.00; Plus $27.75, was $37.00, marked Most popular; Max $74.25, was $99.00; each paid plan has Start 7-day FREE trial, and Pay annually carries the label 2 months free. The comparison table lists Free $0, Standard $10, Plus $37 and Max $99 a month. Free: unlimited impressions, cookie banner and preferences, Privacy Center, Do Not Sell page and 1 scan a month. Standard: Integrations (Google Consent v2, Meta + more), Multi-region compliance, Unlimited cookie scans, Multilingual banner and No Consentmo branding. Plus: Web Accessibility, Smart Geotargeting, EU Withdrawal and Age gate. Max: Consent monitoring, Proof of consent and IAB TCF 2.4. Under the plans a box says Managing more than one store? We offer custom pricing for brands and agencies managing multiple Shopify stores. with a Chat with us button, which we did not press. Checkout: Start 7-day FREE trial on Standard opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: Consentmo GDPR by Consentmo, $2,50 off 3 charges, plan Standard, $10,00 struck through and $7,50 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., subtotal $10,00 plus any applicable taxes, discount $2,50 off -$2,50, total $7,50 due 24 Nov., and an Add payment method row. The sentence about a test charge was NOT on this screen and Approve was greyed out, so we did not approve; no card was entered. The Cancel button did not react, so we went back to the dashboard by navigation. The Free plan stayed active without any approval screen. Cancelling: no subscription ran, because the Free plan was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app with Open app, View details, Get support and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Consentmo GDPR? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required before the button works; we chose Testing multiple apps. Not tested: the Standard features (Google Consent Mode v2, the Meta, Microsoft and TikTok signals and script blocking, because the plan needed a payment method), Plus (accessibility, EU Withdrawal page, Smart Geotargeting) and Max, a price for a second store, the cookie scan, generating a privacy page and annual prices. Clean up: the app embed was switched on with the Activate button of the app (the only setting we changed); no theme was saved in the theme editor. The app was uninstalled after the test with the reason Testing multiple apps. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

On 17 November 2026 the session tested Bot It (Bot It AI in the dossier) on a Shopify development store: the install, the dashboard score, the free catalog scan with its six gaps and six store-level gates, the Billing page, the Shopify approval screen for Pro (not approved), the Free plan and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and nothing was saved in the theme. Install: in the Shopify App Store and in the admin the app is called Bot It (developer Immersive Ecommerce); the dossier calls it Bot It AI. The install form was sent at 12:37:35 in our own tab; the Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data (customers, products, orders, store analytics, Online Store, custom data) and was approved. The dashboard opened without a separate account, demo or phone number. The app is not a chatbot but an audit for AI shopping agents. First screen: AI Agent Visibility Score 23/100 with grade F, Get Started 0/7 complete and as quick win 1: Remove password protection to unlock AI agents. Core action: Discovery and Scan catalog (free plan), 2 clicks from the dashboard, with the result visible about 2 to 3 minutes after the install (about 12:40). Result: Catalog Readiness 32 with grade F, Average product score across 19 products, and the gaps 4 Images missing alt text, 28 Variants missing GTIN, 18 Uncategorized products, 0 Category attributes unset, 19 Thin descriptions and 19 Failing products (score under 50). A banner says 19 products awaiting AI enrichment. The buttons Generate fixes with AI (Pro) and Broadcast (Pro) were greyed out on Free, and the AI token budget box says: Upgrade to Pro to unlock AI-generated alt text, attribute extraction, SEO fields, and agent narratives. Store-level gates: Fail Storefront publicly reachable (Storefront is password-protected), Pass robots.txt allows AI crawlers, Fail /agents.md live (Blocked by storefront password page), Fail /llms.txt live, Warn UCP discovery profile (Valid UCP 2026-08-25, 13 capabilities, NO payment handlers) and Warn Agentic discovery sitemap (HTTP 404). The dossier says 13 checks per product; we did not count them: the app shows 6 gap tiles and 6 store gates. Plans: the Shopify pricing page route said No plans are available for your store; the plans are in the app itself on the Billing page. Free $0 a month, Free forever, Current plan: Native llms.txt, agents.md & robots.txt theme files, Daily AI regeneration (copy/paste or CLI install), UCP manifest, Brand voice configuration, Unlimited collection narratives and Unlimited product narratives. Pro $29 a month with a 30-day free trial: Everything in Free, 1-click push & auto-push of theme files, MCP Enrichment Proxy, WebMCP browser tools, Review integration, Full analytics dashboard and Knowledge Base sync. The Billing page does not name the automated AI fixes, the rank tracker or IndexNow under Pro, while Discovery marks the AI fixes and IndexNow as Pro. Checkout: Start free trial opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: Bot It by Immersive Ecommerce, plan Bot It Pro, You have a 30-day free trial ending on 17 Dec., Subtotal $29,00 plus any applicable taxes, Total $29,00 due 17 Dec., $29,00 USD every 30 days and an Add payment method row. There was no sentence about a test charge and Approve was greyed out, so we did not approve; no card was entered; we pressed Cancel. Cancelling: Pro was not started, so there was nothing to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the app menu and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Testing multiple apps); Shopify then confirmed that the app was uninstalled. Not tested: the Pro fixes (alt text, attributes, SEO fields), the Rank Tracker, IndexNow, the MCP proxy, WebMCP, the review integration, brand voice, switching on the theme extension (no theme change was saved), narratives, the Fix Queue and the Products tab. Our development store has 19 products and Pro was not started, so the group of stores with thousands of incomplete products could not be tested. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test and no Pro plan was started. No payment method was entered and no theme change was made. Other apps were not touched. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app has another name in the admin than in the dossier, the Shopify pricing route says that no plans are available while the plans sit inside the app, the Billing page does not name the AI fixes, the rank tracker or IndexNow under Pro, and the Pro approval screen needs a payment method.

sessions.what: On 26 September 2026 we built the same class-booking web app in Lovable, Replit and Emergent from one identical prompt, each on its free plan, and checked every result against 18 tests we wrote down before the first build. We changed no code: the builder only got our prompt. Lovable paid us nothing when we ran the test; it accepted us into its affiliate programme on 28 September 2026, and these findings were recorded before that.
findings: Lovable built and published the app in about ten minutes and used 4 of the 10 credits on a new account. It asked twice, to create the project and to publish, and published to a lovable.app address that stays online on the free plan with an 'Edit with Lovable' badge.

It was the only one of the three whose first version held the limit when ten people booked an eight-spot class at the same moment: eight accepted, two refused with 'Sorry, this class is full.' The other two accepted all ten.

It checked input on the server as well as in the form (a name of only spaces and a bad email were refused), kept the admin password out of the page and scripts, and prefixed CSV values starting with = + - or @ so a spreadsheet does not run them as formulas.
It needed no repair round. After republishing, every test booking was still there.

Taking the code with you works, taking the running app does not. With GitHub connected (access limited to one repository), Lovable created its own repository with the full source and database migrations and committed no secret keys. Outside Lovable, on Node 22, it installed and built without errors, but loaded no classes: the database service key and admin password stay in Lovable, so moving means setting up your own database and bringing the bookings as a CSV or Lovable's full database export.
sessions.not_tested: One run on one day on the free plan. Not a security audit or a load test, we did not measure how fast the 20 monthly Cloud credits run down, and we did not trigger Lovable's full database export.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Track123 on a Shopify development store: the install from the app address in the admin, because the Install button in the App Store did not work for our test tool, the free Starter plan without a card or account, a tracking page that the app said was generated successfully about 1 minute after the install after 5 onboarding screens, the Customize editor with a sample shipment (progress bar, FedEx scans and a map) after about 10 steps, the Billing page with four plans, the Shopify approval screen for Growth (a 7-day trial and a spending limit of $30,00 per 30 days; it asked for a payment method and had no test charge sentence; nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. The live page and any real parcel were not tested. Nothing was paid. Install: the Install button on the App Store listing (English) did not work for our test tool: the form sent us back to the list of apps without an install. The app address in the Shopify admin (the apps page of the app) showed You don't have this app installed with an Install button, and that worked. The test started at 21:02:53 (the listing loaded). The screen Install app said the app needs access to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked and the app was open at about 21:03:40. No plan choice came first: the app starts on the free plan Starter. Onboarding of 5 screens with one click each: Welcome to Track123!, Dropshiping mode Off (not switched on), Importing shipments (Synchronizing your order of last 14 days), Select tracking page style (Slightly rounded, the default) and Your branded tracking page is ready!, with a link to the tracking page on the store. No terms tick box, no account, no card and no phone number was asked. Core action, a tracking page: the page was ready at about 21:04, about 1 minute after the install, and the Dashboard said Your tracking page is generated successfully. and showed Starter with 50 / 50. The live page was NOT looked at, because the development store has a password. The Customize editor (Tracking page, Track order status, Default, Customize) showed a sample shipment (sample number TK123, Order #TK1231039, status Delivered) with a progress bar (Ordered Aug 7, Order Ready Aug 8, In Transit Aug 9, Out for Delivery Aug 16, Delivered Aug 16), Shipping Details with FedEx scans, a map with Current Location and Package Contents Purple Dress x2 with a button Reorder; the sections were Order lookup, Progress bar, Tracking details and a hidden Shipment review widget, and Product recommendation and Instagram feed said Upgrade. The sample with the progress bar stood there at about 21:05, a little more than 2 minutes after the start and about 10 steps in all. Nothing was saved and no theme change was made; the editor said Store header will appear on the live store. The sample said Powered by Track123 on the search form, and the Dashboard said that the branding can only be removed after a store check by the vendor. No real tracking number or real order was used, so the test covers the page and the sample only, not the link with real carriers, the order lookup with a real order or the Shopify shipping e-mails. Plans in the app (Billing, Monthly; an Annual switch says 20% OFF and was not opened): Starter Free with Orders per month 50 and Unavailable after quota is exceeded (Quota reset date: Dec 17, 2026; Available/Total 50 / 50); Growth $9 a month with Orders per month 300 (a list), $0.05 per extra order and Start 7-day free trial; Advanced (RECOMMENDED) $49 a month with Orders per month 2,000 (a list), $0.05 per extra order, Start 7-day free trial and the features Remove Track123 branding, Estimated delivery time, Checkpoint translation and Klaviyo integration; Enterprise Custom with Orders per month 100,000+, $0.05 per extra order and Contact Us. sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Brandye on a Shopify development store: the install, the onboarding, one AI generated product quiz saved and set live, the Recommendation tab, the Shopify plan page that offered no plans and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and no approval screen was reached; the app embed was saved in the theme. Install: the install form was sent at 12:52:43; the Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data and was approved. The app opened on Welcome to Brandye with the question What do you want to set up first? (AI Shopping Assistant, AI Product Questions, Product Finder Quiz), followed by an optional question How did you hear about Brandye? that we skipped. The dashboard said On your store 0 of 3 live. No separate account, card or phone number was asked. The buttons on the onboarding screen only reacted after a few seconds, and a first click on Create a quiz seemed to do nothing. Core action: from the dashboard, Quiz Set up, Create your quiz, Create quiz (Quiz 1) and Generate Quiz with AI. The dialog Generate quiz with AI had a prefilled Quiz goal and Target customers. The first Generate gave Couldn't generate your quiz and Try again. If it keeps failing, add more detail to the goal. The second try with our own goal (help shoppers pick the right snowboard for their riding level, terrain and budget) worked in about 10 seconds. Result: a flow diagram with 7 questions and branches (among them What's your current snowboarding experience level? and What is your target budget for the board?, and as last question an email request for a stance setup guide) that ends in a results node. We saved it with Save (Questions got a green tick), chose Placement Full-page quiz and saved it; the placement editor shows a style and a Gallery preview but no real shopper view. The dashboard then said Quiz Live with Quiz submissions 0 and Revenue influenced US$ 0, and the Recommendation tab said All products are currently eligible for recommendations. Timing, approximate tester observations: install at 12:52:43, quiz generated and saved at about 12:57 (about 4 minutes and 12 steps including the onboarding), Live on the dashboard at about 12:59. The shopper view was NOT seen: the theme editor showed the added Quiz app block (handle quiz-1, Embedded) empty in the preview, although the Brandye app embed was on. Plans: the app has no plan screen (its menu has AI Product Questions, Quizzes, AI Knowledge, MCP and Settings, and Settings holds only email summaries). The Shopify plan page for the app said Select a plan, No plans are available for your store and Contact the app developer for help choosing a plan. The App Store listing says Free plan available. Free trial available. and the dossier names Starter at $19, but nothing could be chosen or paid in our store. There was no Approve subscription screen, so nothing was approved and no card was asked. Cancelling: no plan or trial existed, so there was nothing to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the app menu and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Brandye? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Testing multiple apps). The uninstall was confirmed at about 13:01 and the app is gone from the installed apps. Not tested: the AI Shopping Assistant, AI Product Questions, French or other languages, the quiz in the store preview, a recommendation result, integrations such as Klaviyo, any plan or paid feature and a data export. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test. In the theme the Brandye app embed was switched on and saved, and the Home page got an empty Apps section because the Quiz app block was not kept after a reload; this stays in the theme and was not changed further. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

The quiz was not seen as a shopper sees it.

sessions.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Seele in a free account of Daan: one prompt for a small cat game, which gave a game brief, 9 concept assets and a playable prototype in about 10 minutes for 45 Koins, the Pro badge on the button for the full game, the plans window on the Monthly and Annually tabs, and the cancel text in the FAQ. The full game, the checkout and the coupon were not reached. Nothing was paid. Start and account: the test started at 16:21:53 (Dutch time) with a prompt sent at the workspace of the vendor site, in the free Seele account of Daan (plan Free, 360 Koins), already logged in, in our own tab. The app was already in English. The model was Seele02-flash (Fast, affordable, perfect for basic games, Current); the Pro and Ultra models showed Unlock this model and were locked. The balance before was 360 Koins. Core action, a small game from one prompt: the prompt was A simple 2D game where a cat jumps over boxes; arrow keys to move, space to jump, score counter. After about 1 minute the app asked 3 questions: Engine (Three.js, Godot, Unity or Unreal, where Unreal was locked), Art style and Run length; we chose Three.js, Pixel arcade and Endless score chase (the recommended default), which took 5 extra clicks. Seele then made a Game brief (Concept, Full game not built yet), 9 concept assets (covers, three cats and three scenes) and a playable prototype, with the message Worked for 9m 34s. The result stood at the latest at 16:32:41, about 10 minutes after the start. The balance after was 315 Koins, so 45 Koins were used; the page Usage and Koin said 29 spent this month and 315 current balance. The prototype (TRY THE BOXES) says that the shapes are drawn in code, so the art is not final. We clicked Start and pressed Space: the cat jumped and the score rose (SCORE 11, BOXES 1 / 26, COMBO 1.1x); after that the screen said THE BOX WON. with a button RUN AGAIN. So the result is playable, but it is a prototype with shapes and not a finished game. The full game: the button Make the full game with AI carries a Pro badge and so does the line LET AI BUILD THE FULL GAME in the brief; the text says the full game is built to commercial quality, with upgraded visuals, levels and audio. We did NOT click it, so no second generation was made and the full game was not seen. On the plan card Standard says it unlocks full game generation, so the Pro badge on the button and the Standard card do not match; this stays an open point. A survey (how did you find us?) appeared and was closed without filling it in; the offer Rate SEELE +100 Koins was not used. Plans: the Upgrade button opened the window One subscription, from games to 3D. Monthly: Standard $20 / mo (Unlocks full game generation, the Pro model and project downloads; 2,000 Koins / mo), Pro $100 / mo (Most popular; Flagship model plus a commercial license, best value; 10,000 + 2,000 Koins / mo) and Ultra $200 / mo (20,000 + 5,000 Koins / mo with the choices 25k, 37.5k, 62.5k and 125k; All-channel commercial use and Mini-game publishing). Annually (Save 22%): Standard $17 / mo (billed $200 / year), Pro $78 / mo (crossed out $100, billed $936 / year) and Ultra $167 / mo (billed $2,000 / year). The card in the sidebar said Upgrade to Pro $100 / mo with 12,000 Koin a month. Koin packs: 2,000 for $20, 5,000 for $50, 20,000 for $200 and 50,000 for $500. Differences with the dossier: Pro is $100 a month and $78 a month billed annually, where the dossier has $50 and $39; Pro has 10,000 + 2,000 Koins a month, where the dossier has 6,000; Standard ($20 and $17) and Ultra ($200 and $167) agree; the dossier says about 120 to 140 Koins give a playable game on the Flash model, and we used 45 Koins for the brief and a playable prototype, which is not the full game; the dossier says the upgrade page applies a 50% first month coupon by default, and we saw no such offer on the plans window or in the sidebar. Checkout: NOT reached. The click on Subscribe to Standard was refused by the permission layer of the session, so we did not go on to the Stripe payment screen, and the coupon could not be checked there. Cancelling: the FAQ in the plans window says Cancel anytime from your billing settings and that paid plans stay active until the end of the current billing period (the text was cut off). The account is Free, so there was nothing to cancel. The account menu has Profile, Usage and Koin, API Keys, Affiliate program, Creator Center, Preferences, Terms and account (User Agreement, Privacy Policy, Subscription and refund policy), Feedback and Log out; no Delete account button was found in Profile or in Terms and account, and nothing was deleted. Not tested: the full game, publishing or sharing, revisions and their Koin cost, the Pro and Ultra models, commercial use, the Stripe checkout and the coupon, the claimed 120 to 140 Koins for a playable game, and cancelling. Clean up: the account and the test project (Cat Jumping Over Boxes Game) were left as they are, with 315 Koins. All our tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Seele in a free account of Daan: one prompt for a small cat game, which gave a game brief, 9 concept assets and a playable prototype in about 10 minutes for 45 Koins, the Pro badge on the button for the full game, the plans window on the Monthly and Annually tabs, and the cancel text in the FAQ. The full game, the checkout and the coupon were not reached. Nothing was paid. Start and account: the test started at 16:21:53 (Dutch time) with a prompt sent at the workspace of the vendor site, in the free Seele account of Daan (plan Free, 360 Koins), already logged in, in our own tab. The app was already in English. The model was Seele02-flash (Fast, affordable, perfect for basic games, Current); the Pro and Ultra models showed Unlock this model and were locked. The balance before was 360 Koins. Core action, a small game from one prompt: the prompt was A simple 2D game where a cat jumps over boxes; arrow keys to move, space to jump, score counter. After about 1 minute the app asked 3 questions: Engine (Three.js, Godot, Unity or Unreal, where Unreal was locked), Art style and Run length; we chose Three.js, Pixel arcade and Endless score chase (the recommended default), which took 5 extra clicks. Seele then made a Game brief (Concept, Full game not built yet), 9 concept assets (covers, three cats and three scenes) and a playable prototype, with the message Worked for 9m 34s. The result stood at the latest at 16:32:41, about 10 minutes after the start. The balance after was 315 Koins, so 45 Koins were used; the page Usage and Koin said 29 spent this month and 315 current balance. The prototype (TRY THE BOXES) says that the shapes are drawn in code, so the art is not final. We clicked Start and pressed Space: the cat jumped and the score rose (SCORE 11, BOXES 1 / 26, COMBO 1.1x); after that the screen said THE BOX WON. with a button RUN AGAIN. So the result is playable, but it is a prototype with shapes and not a finished game. The full game: the button Make the full game with AI carries a Pro badge and so does the line LET AI BUILD THE FULL GAME in the brief; the text says the full game is built to commercial quality, with upgraded visuals, levels and audio. We did NOT click it, so no second generation was made and the full game was not seen. On the plan card Standard says it unlocks full game generation, so the Pro badge on the button and the Standard card do not match; this stays an open point. A survey (how did you find us?) appeared and was closed without filling it in; the offer Rate SEELE +100 Koins was not used. Plans: the Upgrade button opened the window One subscription, from games to 3D. Monthly: Standard $20 / mo (Unlocks full game generation, the Pro model and project downloads; 2,000 Koins / mo), Pro $100 / mo (Most popular; Flagship model plus a commercial license, best value; 10,000 + 2,000 Koins / mo) and Ultra $200 / mo (20,000 + 5,000 Koins / mo with the choices 25k, 37.5k, 62.5k and 125k; All-channel commercial use and Mini-game publishing). Annually (Save 22%): Standard $17 / mo (billed $200 / year), Pro $78 / mo (crossed out $100, billed $936 / year) and Ultra $167 / mo (billed $2,000 / year). The card in the sidebar said Upgrade to Pro $100 / mo with 12,000 Koin a month. Koin packs: 2,000 for $20, 5,000 for $50, 20,000 for $200 and 50,000 for $500. Differences with the dossier: Pro is $100 a month and $78 a month billed annually, where the dossier has $50 and $39; Pro has 10,000 + 2,000 Koins a month, where the dossier has 6,000; Standard ($20 and $17) and Ultra ($200 and $167) agree; the dossier says about 120 to 140 Koins give a playable game on the Flash model, and we used 45 Koins for the brief and a playable prototype, which is not the full game; the dossier says the upgrade page applies a 50% first month coupon by default, and we saw no such offer on the plans window or in the sidebar. Checkout: NOT reached. The click on Subscribe to Standard was refused by the permission layer of the session, so we did not go on to the Stripe payment screen, and the coupon could not be checked there. Cancelling: the FAQ in the plans window says Cancel anytime from your billing settings and that paid plans stay active until the end of the current billing period (the text was cut off). The account is Free, so there was nothing to cancel. The account menu has Profile, Usage and Koin, API Keys, Affiliate program, Creator Center, Preferences, Terms and account (User Agreement, Privacy Policy, Subscription and refund policy), Feedback and Log out; no Delete account button was found in Profile or in Terms and account, and nothing was deleted. Not tested: the full game, publishing or sharing, revisions and their Koin cost, the Pro and Ultra models, commercial use, the Stripe checkout and the coupon, the claimed 120 to 140 Koins for a playable game, and cancelling. Clean up: the account and the test project (Cat Jumping Over Boxes Game) were left as they are, with 315 Koins. All our tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The result is a prototype drawn in code, the full game button has a Pro badge while the Standard card says it unlocks full game generation, the Pro plan costs twice the dossier amount, the 50% first month coupon was not seen, the Subscribe click was refused so the checkout was not reached, and no Delete account button was found.

findings: Sign-up asks four required survey questions (business type, company size, role, how you found Brizy), then shows a member dashboard with 'Start free trial Cloud'. No card was requested.
The trial banner read 'Your trial ends in 14 days! Upgrade to publish your website.' The new project card was labelled PRO PROJECT.
'Create New Website' offers four starting methods: From Scratch, Start with a template, Generate with AI 1.9 and Generate with AI 2.0 (Beta).

Our first prompt in the AI panel ended in 'Out of AI credits - AI credits limit reached', with top-ups of $10, $25 and $50 on offer, plus 'Couldn't finish your request'. The plan cards say 'AI Builder Included', so the trial's AI allowance is unclear.

The plan page had Yearly -20% preselected: Personal $19/mo (1 website), Agency $69/mo (10 websites), White Label $159/mo and a custom Enterprise plan with API access and SSO. We did not look at monthly prices.
